questions.stem: Prior to off-site transport of an intubated patient, an oxygen E-cylinder Bourdon gauge reads 950 psig. The transport requires an FiO2 of 1.0 at a constant mechanical minute ventilation of 10 L/min. What is the approximate maximum duration of oxygen delivery available before cylinder exhaustion?
options: 16 minutes
33 minutes
48 minutes
66 minutes
questions.explanation: At 1900 psig, a full O2 E-cylinder holds ~660 L (Boyle's Law: P1V1 = P2V2). At 950 psig, the cylinder is 50% full (330 L available). At a continuous flow rate of 10 L/min, total time available is 330 L / 10 L/min = 33 minutes.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 12, 13

questions.stem: During volume-controlled mechanical ventilation, the airway pressure waveform below is observed. The peak inspiratory pressure (Point A) has acutely increased to 34 cmH2O while plateau pressure (Point B) remains unchanged at 15 cmH2O. After verifying the external breathing circuit is unobstructed, what is the most appropriate NEXT clinical action?
options: Pass an in-line suction catheter to differentiate luminal secretions from bronchospasm
Perform immediate needle thoracostomy to decompress an expanding tension pneumothorax
Withdraw the endotracheal tube 2 cm to correct an endobronchial intubation
Administer an additional dose of muscle relaxant to relieve acute chest wall rigidity
questions.explanation: An isolated increase in PIP without a change in Pplat reflects increased airway resistance. The lecture specifies that tracheal tube kinking or secretions can be readily identified and differentiated using a suction catheter. Tension pneumothorax, mainstem intubation, and chest wall rigidity all decrease compliance, increasing both PIP and Pplat simultaneously.

questions.stem: In the chemical neutralization of carbon dioxide by wet soda lime, what is the role of sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide?
options: They act as primary binders forming calcium carbonate directly without water
They act as catalytic activators forming intermediate carbonates that subsequently react with calcium hydroxide
They serve as hygroscopic buffering agents preventing premature dehydration of ethyl violet
They absorb carbon monoxide generated during difluoromethyl ether degradation
questions.explanation: NaOH and KOH function as catalysts/activators to accelerate the initial reaction with carbonic acid, forming sodium and potassium carbonates. These intermediate carbonates then react over several minutes with Ca(OH)2 to precipitate calcium carbonate and regenerate the hydroxides.

questions.stem: During direct laryngoscopy, elevating the glossoepiglottic ligament with a curved Macintosh blade achieves glottic visualization primarily through which mechanical vector?
options: Direct downward compression of the corniculate cartilages against the esophagus
Direct entrapment and anterior displacement of the posterior laryngeal surface
Tension applied within the vallecula that indirectly pulls the epiglottis anteriorly
Axial distraction of the atlanto-occipital joint to expand the hypopharynx
questions.explanation: The tip of the Macintosh curved blade is advanced into the vallecula; applying forward traction stretches the glossoepiglottic ligament, which indirectly elevates the epiglottis away from the glottis.

questions.stem: Why does bulk hospital oxygen remain stored in liquid state within cryogenic vacuum-insulated tanks at approximately -160°C (-256°F)?
options: It must be maintained below its critical temperature of -118.6°C to liquefy under pressure
Liquid oxygen freezes into solid crystals at temperatures above -183°C
Cryogenic temperatures are required to convert trace nitrogen into medical grade gas
It prevents pipeline pressure regulators from freezing during peak surgical demand
questions.explanation: The critical temperature of oxygen is -118.6°C. Above this temperature, gas cannot be liquefied no matter how much pressure is applied. Cryogenic storage maintains bulk liquid O2 at ~ -160°C, well below its critical threshold.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 11, 32

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions cause a simultaneous increase in both peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) and plateau pressure (Pplat) while tidal volume remains constant? (Select 3)
options: Steep Trendelenburg surgical positioning
Peritoneal insufflation with carbon dioxide
Airway secretions in the upper trachea
Foreign body aspiration into a main bronchus
Endobronchial mainstem intubation
Herniation of the endotracheal tube cuff
questions.explanation: Simultaneous elevation of PIP and Pplat with a constant tidal volume indicates decreased static and dynamic pulmonary compliance. Trendelenburg positioning, peritoneal insufflation, and mainstem intubation all reduce total lung compliance. Secretions, foreign body aspiration, and cuff herniation increase airway resistance, elevating PIP alone while Pplat remains unchanged.

questions.stem: According to the Nurse Anesthesia textbook, what is the recommended 8-hour time-weighted occupational exposure when nitrous oxide is used with a halogenated anesthetic?
options: 0.5 ppm halogenated agent and 25 ppm nitrous oxide
2 ppm halogenated agent and 25 ppm nitrous oxide
5 ppm halogenated agent and 50 ppm nitrous oxide
10 ppm halogenated agent and 100 ppm nitrous oxide
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia states that workers should not be exposed to more than 2 ppm of a halogenated agent, reduced to 0.5 ppm when it is used with nitrous oxide, and no more than 25 ppm nitrous oxide as an 8-hour time-weighted average.

questions.stem: Anesthesia personnel attempt to mount an E-cylinder to a workstation hanger yoke. The cylinder valve stem features the Pin Index Safety System configuration shown below (pins at 2 and 5). Which clinical hazard is introduced if TWO Bodok washers are accidentally stacked on the yoke nipple?
options: The cylinder post sits flush, but high pressure ruptures the frangible safety disc
The increased spacing clears the index pins, permitting connection of an incorrect gas cylinder
The cylinder check valve remains permanently unseated, causing high backflow leaks
Gas flow into the first-stage regulator is choked, limiting maximum flow to 10 L/min
questions.explanation: Using more than one washer (Bodok seal) creates extra space between the cylinder valve face and the yoke block, allowing the cylinder post to bypass the index pins and permitting attachment of the wrong gas cylinder.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 10, 18, 20

questions.stem: According to the Landesberg et al. vascular surgery trial cited in the monitoring literature, what proportion of intraoperative myocardial ischemic episodes presented as ST-segment depression rather than ST-segment elevation?
questions.explanation: In the Landesberg et al. study, V3 was the most sensitive lead for ischemia (86.8%), and 97% of all recorded perioperative ischemic events showed ST depression, not ST elevation.

questions.stem: Rank the volatile anesthetics in order of decreasing potential for carbon monoxide generation when exposed to dry, desiccated carbon dioxide absorbent:
options: Desflurane > Isoflurane > Enflurane > Sevoflurane
Desflurane > Enflurane > Isoflurane
Sevoflurane > Isoflurane > Desflurane
Enflurane > Desflurane > Halothane
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide production is specific to difluoromethyl ethers and follows the exact order: Desflurane > Enflurane > Isoflurane. Sevoflurane and Halothane lack this moiety and do not produce carbon monoxide.

questions.stem: How is the Eschmann introducer categorized in the airway-equipment lecture?
options: Intubating stylet
Supraglottic airway
Nasopharyngeal airway
Cricothyrotomy device
questions.explanation: The lecture presents the Eschmann introducer under the heading 'Airways: Intubating Stylet.' The prior tactile-click and hold-up details were not present in the cited course material.

questions.stem: Which of the following components are located within the low-pressure system of the anesthesia workstation? (Select 2)
options: Vaporizer mounting manifolds and sumps
Auxiliary oxygen flowmeter
Second-stage pressure regulators
Thorpe flowmeter indicator tubes
Oxygen flush valve conduit
Pipeline pressure line gauges
questions.explanation: The low-pressure system extends from downstream of the flow control needle valves to the common gas outlet, containing flowmeter tubes, vaporizers, pressure relief valves, and outlet check valves. Auxiliary O2, second-stage regulators, and flush valves belong to the intermediate system.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 38, 39, 76

questions.stem: An arterial line fast-flush test shows an underdamped response with marked ringing. How does the lecture say systolic pressure is affected?
options: It is underestimated
It is overestimated, often by 15-30 mmHg
It is unchanged
It cannot be measured
questions.explanation: The lecture states that underdamping tends to overestimate systolic pressure by about 15 to 30 mmHg and amplify artifacts. The prior version also claimed a specific diastolic effect that is not stated on the cited slide.

questions.stem: What is the primary clinical trap associated with the regeneration phenomenon of ethyl violet dye in carbon dioxide absorbents?
options: Absorbent granules permanently dissolve into an amorphous alkaline paste
Exhausted absorbent turns white after resting overnight, falsely mimicking fresh lime
Bleaching of the indicator dye accelerates the catalytic formation of Compound A
Regenerated hydroxides permanently prevent mechanical channeling along canister walls
questions.explanation: The lecture warns that indicator color can fade after use stops, a phenomenon called regeneration. That fading can make nearly exhausted absorbent look fresher than it is, so color change should not be relied on by itself.

questions.stem: How does the Tec 6 Desflurane vaporizer maintain consistent agent output despite desflurane having a boiling point of 22.8°C and a vapor pressure of 669 mmHg at 20°C?
options: It uses an internal bimetallic strip to widen the vaporizing chamber orifice during cooling
It electrically heats the liquid sump to 39°C and pressurizes it to 1500 mmHg (2 atm)
It bubbles fresh gas through a high-surface-area copper kettle wick assembly
It injects liquid desflurane directly into the common gas outlet via ultrasonic nebulization
questions.explanation: Because desflurane boils near room temperature, conventional variable bypass vaporizers cannot deliver controlled concentrations. The Tec 6 heats the liquid agent to 39°C and pressurizes the sump to 2 atm (1500 mmHg) to create a reliable vapor reservoir.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 60

questions.stem: According to ASA Standard II, what is the maximum allowable documentation interval for non-invasive arterial blood pressure and heart rate during general anesthesia?
options: Every 3 minutes during induction and every 10 minutes during maintenance
At least every 5 minutes throughout the entire anesthetic
Every 15 minutes unless vasoactive infusions are active
Continuous display only; manual logging interval is left to clinician discretion
questions.explanation: ASA Standard 2.3 explicitly mandates that arterial blood pressure and heart rate must be determined and evaluated at least every five minutes during all anesthetics.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions produce an acute, sudden DECREASE in measured end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2)? (Select 3)
options: Massive pulmonary thromboembolism
Malignant hyperthermia crisis
Sudden profound cardiac arrest
Intravenous sodium bicarbonate bolus
Accidental tracheal extubation into the pharynx
Surgical release of an aortic cross-clamp
questions.explanation: Decreased EtCO2 occurs with sudden increases in alveolar dead space (pulmonary embolism), severe circulatory collapse (arrest/hypoperfusion), or loss of airway integrity. Malignant hyperthermia, bicarbonate boluses, and clamp release increase EtCO2.

questions.stem: During laser airway surgery, how does the lecture recommend filling a laser-resistant endotracheal-tube cuff?
options: With air only
With saline or water and dye
With nitrous oxide
With carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: The lecture states that laser-resistant tube cuffs are not themselves laser resistant and therefore should be filled with saline or water and dye.

questions.stem: What mechanical principle ensures that pipeline medical gas is consumed preferentially over reserve cylinders if an E-cylinder is inadvertently left open during surgery?
options: The pipeline supply check valve mechanically locks the cylinder hanger yoke closed
The first-stage regulator reduces cylinder pressure to 45 psig, which is lower than the 50–55 psig pipeline pressure
The oxygen fail-safe valve shuts off cylinder inflow when pipeline pressure exceeds 30 psig
The second-stage regulator throttles cylinder inflow to 14 psig while boosting pipeline flow
questions.explanation: Pipeline gas enters the machine at 50–55 psig. The first-stage regulator reduces cylinder pressure to ~45 psig. Because pipeline pressure is higher, cylinder gas is held back upstream by the check valve as long as pipeline pressure remains normal.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 24, 33

questions.stem: Following endotracheal intubation, what quantitative capnographic criterion confirms correct tracheal tube placement and excludes esophageal intubation?
options: A single exhalation registering an EtCO2 value greater than 30 mmHg
Detection of continuous, stable EtCO2 waveforms across at least three consecutive breaths
An inspiratory downstroke returning to a baseline of 5 mmHg
Sustained airway pressure during exhalation above 10 cmH2O
questions.explanation: Confirmation of endotracheal placement requires continuous, stable EtCO2 waveforms across at least 3 consecutive breaths. Gastric CO2 washout from mask ventilation typically diminishes within 1 to 2 breaths.

questions.stem: What action is required to open the variable bypass vaporizer from its locked closed position?
options: Press the release button and rotate the dial counterclockwise
Open the oxygen flush valve first
Set the vaporizer to transport mode
Lift the cassette from the manifold
questions.explanation: The lecture describes an interlock safety mechanism that requires pressing a button and rotating counterclockwise from the locked closed position to open the vaporizer.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 59

questions.stem: Which characteristics differentiate an open-reservoir scavenging interface from a closed-reservoir scavenging interface? (Select 2)
options: An open interface requires spring-loaded positive-pressure pop-off valves
An open interface is entirely valveless
An open interface uses relief ports open to the ambient operating room atmosphere
An open interface requires a negative-pressure relief pop-in valve
An open interface utilizes a dedicated waste gas reservoir bag
An open interface can only be connected to passive through-the-wall conduits
questions.explanation: An open scavenging interface is valveless and relies on ports open to the atmosphere to prevent positive or negative pressure buildup. Closed interfaces use dedicated reservoir bags and spring-loaded pop-off/pop-in safety valves.

questions.stem: During a procedural case with benzocaine spray, a patient develops severe methemoglobinemia. What reading will conventional dual-wavelength pulse oximetry display?
options: It displays a falsely elevated saturation of 100%
It plateaus at approximately 85% regardless of true arterial PaO2
It reads zero due to absence of pulsatile arterial waveforms
It tracks arterial PaO2 accurately but underestimates SaO2 by 5%
questions.explanation: Methemoglobin absorbs 660 nm and 940 nm light equally (1:1 absorption ratio). On a standard dual-wavelength pulse oximeter, this ratio corresponds empirically to a saturation of approximately 85%.

questions.stem: Which head and neck maneuvers achieve optimal alignment of the oral, pharyngeal, and laryngeal axes in a normal non-obese adult?
options: Flexion of the cervical spine with simultaneous flexion at the atlanto-occipital joint
Elevation of the occiput 7–10 cm with head extension at the atlanto-occipital joint
Neutral cervical alignment with anterior mandibular traction only
Extreme posterior hyperextension of the cervical spine without head elevation
questions.explanation: The sniffing position aligns the three airway axes by elevating the occiput (7–10 cm) to flex the lower cervical spine while extending the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

questions.stem: How does gas flow through a traditional Thorpe tube differ at low versus high flow rates?
options: Low flow is laminar; high flow is turbulent
Low flow is turbulent; high flow is laminar
Both are always laminar
Both are always turbulent
questions.explanation: The lecture states that low flow occurs through a long, narrow annular space and is laminar, while high flow behaves more like an orifice and is turbulent.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 43

questions.stem: Which course-described factors can contribute to preventable monitoring or equipment-related harm? Select 3.
options: Ignoring or disabling alarms after alarm fatigue
Spontaneous mechanical disruption of internal ventilator bellows
Latent manufacturing defects within variable bypass vaporizers
Cognitive bias that dismisses a valid alarm as monitor error
Routine calibration of a functioning oxygen sensor
Operator unfamiliarity with anesthesia equipment
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies alarm fatigue as a cause of ignored or disabled alarms, warns that cognitive bias can lead clinicians to dismiss valid alerts, and states that operator unfamiliarity or failure to verify machine function are frequent contributors to equipment-related mishaps. It does not support the prior claim that these exact factors account for more than 65% of closed claims.

questions.stem: During surgery under general anesthesia, hospital pipeline oxygen supply pressure falls to 22 psig. What is the expected response of the anesthesia machine pneumatics?
options: The oxygen flush valve activates automatically to restore circuit volume
The oxygen fail-safe valve proportionately throttles or stops the flow of nitrous oxide
The low-pressure relief valve vents all gas from the common gas outlet
The second-stage oxygen regulator closes completely to preserve cylinder reserves
questions.explanation: The oxygen fail-safe valve resides in the nitrous oxide line. When oxygen line pressure drops below 25–30 psig, the valve closes or throttles, halting or reducing nitrous oxide flow (<20 psig) to prevent delivery of a hypoxic mixture.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 34

questions.stem: A patient undergoing an emergent appendectomy develops the capnography waveform below. What underlying respiratory pathology is present, and what is its characteristic waveform feature?
options: Bronchospasm characterized by a prolonged, sloped Phase II upstroke and absent alpha angle
Carbon dioxide rebreathing characterized by failure of Phase I to return to zero
Partial circuit disconnect characterized by an abrupt reduction in Phase III height
Curare cleft characterized by a mid-plateau inspiratory notch
questions.explanation: This is a classic 'shark-fin' waveform seen in bronchospasm, asthma, or COPD. Airflow obstruction prolongs expiratory emptying, blunting the Phase II upstroke and eliminating the distinct transition (alpha angle) into Phase III.

questions.stem: Why are soda lime granules specifically manufactured to a 4 to 8 mesh size rather than a finer 20 mesh size?
options: Finer granules would dramatically increase resistance to airflow through the canister
Finer granules lack sufficient surface area for adequate carbon dioxide diffusion
Finer granules prevent ethyl violet indicator dye from changing color
Finer granules promote the catalytic production of carbon monoxide
questions.explanation: Soda lime is sized 4 to 8 mesh to balance surface area against airflow resistance. Finer granules would provide higher surface area but would introduce excessive resistance to ventilation within the breathing circuit.

questions.stem: Which endotracheal tube design is preferred for head and neck procedures or prone positioning because of its resistance to external compression and acute kinking?
options: Oral Ring-Adair-Elwyn (RAE) tube
Armored (anode / flexo-metallic) tube
Double-cuffed laser-shield tube
Standard uncuffed polyvinyl chloride tube
questions.explanation: The lecture describes armored (anode or flexo-metallic) tubes as having a spiral metal or nylon reinforcement that resists kinking and compression, with use in head, neck, and tracheal surgery.

questions.stem: During induction, an automated blood pressure cuff whose bladder width covers only 25% of the patient's arm circumference is used. How will this affect the displayed hemodynamic values?
options: Blood pressure readings will be falsely low
Blood pressure readings will be falsely elevated
Diastolic pressure will read low while systolic pressure reads normal
Mean arterial pressure will be accurate but pulse pressure will be blunted
questions.explanation: A blood pressure cuff bladder width should equal ~40% of arm circumference. A bladder that is too narrow requires excessive inflation pressure to transmit occlusion forces to the artery, resulting in falsely high blood pressure readings.

questions.stem: Which of the following volatile anesthetics lack a difluoromethyl moiety (-O-CHF2) and therefore do NOT generate carbon monoxide upon contact with desiccated absorbent? (Select 2)
options: Desflurane
Sevoflurane
Isoflurane
Enflurane
Methoxyflurane
Halothane
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide production is specific to difluoromethyl ethers containing the -O-CHF2 group (Desflurane > Enflurane > Isoflurane). Sevoflurane and Halothane lack this moiety and do not produce CO.

questions.stem: Why is the carbon dioxide absorbent canister located in the inspiratory limb on the bag side of the circle system?
options: To prevent moisture exhaled by the patient from reaching the absorbent granules
To allow apparatus resistance to inspiration to be overcome by assisted or controlled ventilation
To prevent fresh gas flow from entering the common gas outlet prematurely
To allow the APL valve to vent carbon dioxide prior to entering the canister
questions.explanation: The CO2 absorber is placed in the inspiratory limb on the bag side so that apparatus resistance to inspiration is overcome by manual assisted or mechanical controlled ventilation.

questions.stem: What mechanical delivery parameters are produced when depressing the oxygen flush valve on a modern anesthesia workstation?
options: 10–15 L/min at 14–16 psig
20–30 L/min at 25–30 psig
35–75 L/min at 40–50 psig
80–100 L/min at 75–85 psig
questions.explanation: The oxygen flush valve supplies unmetered pure O2 directly to the common gas outlet at a rate of 35–75 L/min at pipeline/intermediate pressure (40–50 psig), completely bypassing flowmeters and vaporizers.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 36

questions.stem: During controlled ventilation, a curare cleft appears in the alveolar plateau. What does the finding indicate, and what should be assessed?
options: Spontaneous inspiratory effort; assess neuromuscular blockade and give additional relaxant if indicated
Rebreathing; replace the CO2 absorbent immediately
Bronchospasm; increase inspiratory flow
Circuit disconnection; increase fresh gas flow
questions.explanation: A curare cleft is a notch in the alveolar plateau caused by spontaneous inspiratory effort during controlled ventilation. The lecture notes that this pattern may indicate the need for more neuromuscular blockade, so blockade should be assessed and additional relaxant given if appropriate.

questions.stem: What is the PISS pin configuration for a medical air E-cylinder?
options: Positions 1 and 5
Positions 2 and 5
Positions 3 and 5
Positions 2 and 4
questions.explanation: Under the Pin Index Safety System, Medical Air uses pin coordinates 1 and 5. Oxygen uses 2 and 5; Nitrous oxide uses 3 and 5.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 18

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical practices are recommended to minimize waste anesthetic gas pollution and atmospheric greenhouse emissions? (Select 3)
options: Calibrating vaporizers on high fresh gas flows before induction
Avoiding nitrous oxide as a routine carrier gas
Avoiding unnecessarily high fresh gas flow rates, especially with desflurane
Maintaining operating room air turnover at 30 exchanges per hour
Utilizing total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) or regional techniques when appropriate
Discarding soda lime absorbent canisters after every individual patient case
questions.explanation: Recommendations to reduce environmental impact include avoiding N2O carrier gas, minimizing fresh gas flows (especially with desflurane, which has a 14-year atmospheric lifespan), and substituting regional/TIVA techniques when appropriate.

questions.stem: Which anatomical structures define the superior and inferior borders of the cricothyroid membrane during an emergency surgical airway?
options: Thyroid cartilage superiorly and cricoid cartilage inferiorly
Hyoid bone superiorly and thyroid cartilage inferiorly
Cricoid cartilage superiorly and first tracheal ring inferiorly
Corniculate cartilage superiorly and arytenoid cartilage inferiorly
questions.explanation: The cricothyroid membrane is bounded superiorly by the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage and inferiorly by the superior border of the cricoid cartilage.

questions.stem: How does a bimetallic strip maintain stable anesthetic vapor concentration across decreasing temperatures in a variable bypass vaporizer?
options: It bends to decrease bypass flow and increase gas flow through the vaporizing chamber
It bends to increase bypass flow and reduce saturation within the vaporizing chamber
It activates an internal electrical heating element to raise sump temperature to 39°C
It closes the machine outlet check valve to prevent the pumping effect
questions.explanation: As liquid anesthetic cools, vapor pressure falls. The temperature-compensation element responds by increasing flow through the vaporizing chamber, helping maintain the dialed concentration.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 56

questions.stem: During general anesthesia, what capnographic finding confirms carbon dioxide rebreathing?
options: A prolonged, sloped Phase II upstroke with loss of the alpha angle
Phase I baseline fails to return to zero (elevated baseline above 0 mmHg)
A deep notch during the latter third of Phase III
An acute drop in peak EtCO2 below 15 mmHg
questions.explanation: CO2 rebreathing is defined by an elevated Phase I baseline (>0 mmHg). During inspiration, CO2-containing gas is re-inspired, commonly caused by exhausted absorbent or incompetent unidirectional valves.

questions.stem: What is the primary physical mechanism of intraoperative heat loss in a patient undergoing general anesthesia in an ambient operating room?
options: Radiation
Convection
Conduction
Evaporation
questions.explanation: Radiation represents the primary source of intraoperative heat loss, accounting for radiant infrared transfer from the warm patient to the cool operating room environment.

questions.stem: Which dyshemoglobin is specifically described as causing a falsely high conventional two-wavelength pulse-oximeter reading?
options: Methemoglobin
Carboxyhemoglobin
Deoxyhemoglobin
Fetal hemoglobin
questions.explanation: The lecture states that carboxyhemoglobin produces falsely high pulse-oximeter readings. Methemoglobin instead drives the displayed SpO2 toward about 85%, depending on the true saturation.

questions.stem: For an operating room equipped with a recirculating ventilation system, what is the minimum required total air exchange rate per hour, and how many must be fresh outdoor air?
options: 10 to 15 total exchanges, with at least 1 fresh outside exchange
15 to 21 total exchanges, with at least 3 fresh outside exchanges
20 to 25 total exchanges, with at least 5 fresh outside exchanges
25 to 30 total exchanges, with at least 8 fresh outside exchanges
questions.explanation: Recirculating OR ventilation systems are required to perform 15 to 21 total air exchanges per hour, of which at least three exchanges must be fresh outside air.

questions.stem: In the four flowmeter manifold configurations pictured below, which sequence represents the safest fail-safe design to prevent hypoxic gas delivery in the event of an upstream tube leak?
options: Configuration A
Configuration B
Configuration C
Configuration D
questions.explanation: Oxygen must be positioned furthest downstream (closest to the manifold outlet). In Configuration C (N2O -> Air -> O2), leaks in upstream tubes allow carrier gases to escape ambiently while O2 continues downstream.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 41

questions.stem: During routine general anesthesia in a healthy supine patient, what ETCO2-PaCO2 gradient does the lecture describe?
options: About 5 mmHg, with a typical range of 2-10 mmHg
About 15-20 mmHg
Exactly 0 mmHg
ETCO2 is normally higher than PaCO2 by 10 mmHg
questions.explanation: The lecture describes ETCO2 as typically about 5 mmHg lower than PaCO2 in healthy supine patients during routine general anesthesia, with a range of approximately 2 to 10 mmHg.

questions.stem: Which of the following components are located within the high-pressure system of the anesthesia machine? (Select 3)
options: Pipeline inlet check valve
Hanger yoke assembly
Oxygen flush valve
Bourdon cylinder pressure gauge
Flowmeter needle valves
First-stage pressure regulator
questions.explanation: The high-pressure system consists of components receiving cylinder gas: hanger yokes, cylinder check valves, cylinder pressure gauges, and first-stage regulators. Pipeline valves, flush valves, and needle valves are downstream in intermediate/low systems.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 5, 6, 76

questions.stem: As an arterial pressure waveform moves from the aorta toward a peripheral artery, what general change does the lecture describe?
options: Wave reflection exaggerates systolic and pulse pressures
Systolic and pulse pressures both become lower
Mean pressure rises sharply while systolic pressure is unchanged
The waveform becomes identical at all sites
questions.explanation: The lecture states that peripheral wave reflection distorts the waveform and exaggerates systolic and pulse pressures. It also notes that local vascular resistance can sometimes make radial pressure underestimate central pressure, so the question now asks for the general waveform effect rather than an absolute diastolic change.

questions.stem: A variable bypass vaporizer is accidentally tilted during transport. Which recovery sequence matches the lecture before returning it to use?
options: Drain it, run high fresh gas flow at the highest setting for 30 minutes, and refill once expired gas analysis no longer detects agent
Leave it upright for 5 minutes and use it normally
Autoclave the vaporizer manifold
Invert it and activate the oxygen flush
questions.explanation: Tipping can place liquid agent in the bypass chamber and raise vaporizer output. The lecture recommends draining the vaporizer, running it at the highest setting with high fresh gas flow for 30 minutes, and refilling only once expired gas analysis no longer detects anesthetic.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 71

questions.stem: What percentage of all operating room anesthetic gas contamination is caused by errors in anesthesia technique?
questions.explanation: Lecture data shows that 94% to 99% of all OR anesthetic contamination stems from provider technique errors (e.g., leaving gas on during intubation, poorly seated masks/LMAs, unsealed ETT cuffs, liquid agent spillage).

questions.stem: How does the Miller blade expose the glottis during direct laryngoscopy?
options: By directly lifting the epiglottis
By stretching the glossoepiglottic ligament from the vallecula
By inflating the vallecula with oxygen
By depressing the arytenoids
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the Miller as a long, straight blade used for direct epiglottic lift, in contrast with the Macintosh blade's indirect lift through the vallecula.

questions.stem: Which of the following actions trigger the 'pumping effect' in an older variable bypass vaporizer lacking an outlet check valve? (Select 2)
options: Continuous use of high fresh gas flows (>10 L/min)
Maintaining an overfilled liquid agent sump
Operating the machine at elevated atmospheric pressures
Using an open-reservoir scavenging interface
Intermittent positive pressure ventilation
Activation of the oxygen flush valve
questions.explanation: The pumping effect is caused by rapid backpressure fluctuations (from positive pressure ventilation or depressing the O2 flush valve) compressing gas back into the vaporizing chamber, transiently increasing delivered output.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 72

questions.stem: A patient's invasive radial arterial line displays a pressure of 145/70 mmHg. What is the calculated Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)?
options: 85 mmHg
95 mmHg
107 mmHg
120 mmHg
questions.explanation: MAP is calculated as: MAP = [SBP + 2(DBP)] / 3. Here, [145 + 2(70)] / 3 = [145 + 140] / 3 = 285 / 3 = 95 mmHg.

questions.stem: How much carbon dioxide can be absorbed by a standard 1000 g pre-packed canister of fresh soda lime absorbent?
options: Approximately 26 L
Approximately 190 L
Approximately 260 L
Approximately 500 L
questions.explanation: Soda lime absorbs approximately 19% of its weight in CO2 (100 g absorbs ~26 L). Therefore, a 1000 g canister absorbs approximately 260 L of CO2.

questions.stem: Which organization is described as enacting and enforcing workplace safety standards after NIOSH recommendations?
options: Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM)
Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)
questions.explanation: The lecture describes NIOSH as conducting research and recommending safety standards, while OSHA was established to enact standards into law after due process and enforce them. The waste-gas slide also notes that there is no universal WAG exposure standard.

questions.stem: Which statements about an oropharyngeal airway are supported by the lecture? Select 3.
options: Its concave surface faces caudally
It lifts the tongue
It improves bag-mask seal in edentulous patients
Awake patients tolerate it better than an NPA
Its most common complication is epistaxis
It lies in the hypopharynx
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the OPA as having a caudally facing concave surface, lifting the tongue, and improving bag-mask ventilation seal in edentulous patients. Awake patients tolerate NPAs better, and epistaxis is the common NPA complication.

questions.stem: What critical temperature does the lecture give for nitrous oxide?
options: About -118.6°C
About -88°C
About +36°C
About +58°C
questions.explanation: The lecture gives nitrous oxide a critical temperature of about 36°C, which is above typical room temperature and allows liquid and gas to coexist in the cylinder under pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 14

questions.stem: On an anesthesia machine spirometry display, what respiratory change causes a Pressure-Volume (P-V) loop to tilt down and shift rightward along the pressure axis?
options: Increased pulmonary compliance
Decreased pulmonary compliance
Circuit disconnection
Zero airway resistance
questions.explanation: On a P-V loop, volume is on the vertical axis and airway pressure is on the horizontal axis. When compliance decreases, higher pressure is required to deliver the same volume, tilting the loop down and to the right.

questions.stem: Why does the Bourdon pressure gauge of a nitrous oxide cylinder remain at 745 psig until nearly all liquid is exhausted?
options: The gauge is electronically locked until liquid levels reach zero
Liquid N2O vaporizes continuously to maintain equilibrium vapor pressure at room temperature
The cylinder check valve throttles backpressure from the pipeline
N2O behaves as an ideal gas that expands nonlinearly
questions.explanation: As long as liquid nitrous oxide remains, liquid and vapor stay in equilibrium and the cylinder pressure remains near 745 psig at 20°C. Once the liquid phase is gone, the pressure begins to fall as the remaining gas is used.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 14

questions.stem: What is the estimated atmospheric lifetime of nitrous oxide?
options: 1.1 years
3.2 years
14 years
114 years
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide is a potent greenhouse gas that persists in the atmosphere for up to 114 years. Desflurane persists for 14 years, isoflurane for 3.2 years, and sevoflurane for 1.1 years.

questions.stem: Which of the following monitoring modalities satisfy the requirements of ASA Standard II for continuous evaluation of patient circulation? (Select 3)
options: Continuous display of the electrocardiogram (ECG)
Arterial blood pressure evaluated at least every five minutes
Pulse plethysmography or continuous pulse oximetry
Transesophageal echocardiography in all cases
Electromyographic train-of-four every 15 minutes
Continuous mixed venous oxygen saturation catheter
questions.explanation: ASA Standard 2.3 mandates continuous ECG display, arterial BP/heart rate at least every 5 minutes, and continuous evaluation of circulation via palpation, auscultation, intra-arterial tracing, Doppler, or pulse oximetry plethysmography.

questions.stem: What is the PISS pin configuration for an oxygen E-cylinder?
options: Positions 1 and 5
Positions 2 and 5
Positions 3 and 5
Positions 2 and 6
questions.explanation: Under the Pin Index Safety System, an oxygen E-cylinder uses pin positions 2 and 5. The matching pins on the hanger yoke prevent attachment of a cylinder with a different gas-specific configuration.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 18

questions.stem: What capnographic change is observed immediately upon Return of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC) during cardiopulmonary resuscitation?
options: Gradual appearance of a curare cleft
Sudden, dramatic increase in EtCO2
Immediate widening of the alpha angle
Progressive fall of inspiratory baseline below zero
questions.explanation: During cardiac arrest, low cardiac output severely limits delivery of CO2 to the lungs. Upon ROSC, the sudden restoration of pulmonary blood flow washes accumulated CO2 out of tissues into the alveoli, causing an abrupt surge in EtCO2.

questions.stem: Which chemical component constitutes approximately 80% of standard wet soda lime?
options: Sodium hydroxide
Potassium hydroxide
Calcium hydroxide
Barium hydroxide
questions.explanation: Wet soda lime is composed of approximately 80% calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2], ~5% activator hydroxides (sodium and potassium hydroxide), and ~15% water.

questions.stem: What is the recommended alignment target when ramping an obese patient prior to induction and intubation?
options: Trendelenburg position at 15 degrees
Horizontal alignment of the external auditory meatus with the sternal notch
Elevation of the shoulders with hyperextension of the neck below the clavicles
Prone flexed position with head elevated 30 degrees
questions.explanation: For morbidly obese patients, the textbook describes ramping the head, upper body, and shoulders until an imaginary horizontal line connects the sternal notch and external auditory meatus.

questions.stem: Which design features are incorporated into mechanical flowmeters on an anesthesia workstation to prevent delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture? (Select 2)
options: The oxygen flow control knob is physically larger and fluted
Nitrous oxide is plumbed into an independent auxiliary manifold
Thorpe tubes have a uniform, non-tapered internal diameter
Oxygen is always positioned last in the manifold sequence closest to the outlet
Flow control valves automatically increase fresh gas flow during apnea
Check valves prevent volatile agent from entering the glass tubes
questions.explanation: To prevent hypoxia, the O2 knob is uniquely tactile (larger, fluted) and O2 is positioned furthest downstream (last on the right) so any upstream leaks will leak other gases rather than oxygen.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 40, 41

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanism of heat loss conserved by utilizing low fresh gas flows and a circle breathing system?
options: Radiation
Conduction
Evaporation
Convection
questions.explanation: Low fresh gas flows conserve exhaled moisture and heat, directly reducing evaporative heat loss from the respiratory tract (which expends 0.58 kcal per gram of water vaporized).

questions.stem: On the invasive arterial pressure waveform shown below, identify the mechanical cardiac event corresponding to the landmark indicated by the arrow:
options: Opening of the aortic valve
Closure of the aortic valve
Peak isovolumetric ventricular contraction
Closure of the mitral valve
questions.explanation: The dicrotic notch on an arterial waveform marks the closure of the aortic valve and signifies the transition from systole to diastole.

questions.stem: What is the PISS pin configuration for nitrous oxide?
options: Positions 1 and 5
Positions 2 and 5
Positions 3 and 5
Positions 2 and 4
questions.explanation: Under the Pin Index Safety System, nitrous oxide uses pin positions 3 and 5. The gas-specific pin pattern is intended to prevent attachment of the wrong cylinder to the hanger yoke.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 18

questions.stem: Which volatile anesthetic requires caution regarding Compound A formation when used with low fresh gas flows and dry absorbent?
options: Isoflurane
Desflurane
Sevoflurane
Halothane
questions.explanation: The lecture shows that Compound A production from sevoflurane is promoted by warmer, drier absorbent, higher agent concentration, and lower fresh gas flow.

questions.stem: Which of the following items are verified under the 'M' (Machine) component of the pre-induction MS MAID room setup? (Select 3)
options: Completed full machine pre-use checkout
Presence of an auxiliary oxygen cylinder
Presence of a rigid stylet within the primary ETT
Verification of IV fluid warmer priming
Baseline 12-lead ECG strip printing
Emergency bag-valve-mask resuscitation device functional
questions.explanation: Under the MS MAID acronym, 'M' stands for Machine: performing a complete check, ensuring an emergency resuscitation bag-valve-mask is available, and confirming a backup O2 cylinder is present.

questions.stem: A variable bypass vaporizer delivering 1% sevoflurane at 2 L/min fresh gas flow requires a splitting ratio of 25:1 between bypass and vaporizing chamber flow. If dialed concentration is increased, how does the concentration control dial adjust internal flow mechanics?
options: It restricts bypass flow and directs a greater proportion of fresh gas into the vaporizing sump
It increases electrical wattage to the heating element to raise vapor pressure
It closes the machine outlet check valve to prevent the pumping effect
It increases total fresh gas flow from the Thorpe tube manifold
questions.explanation: The concentration dial mechanically controls variable restrictor valves. Turning the dial to a higher concentration restricts the bypass path and directs a larger percentage of fresh gas through the vaporizing sump.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 54, 55

questions.stem: What capnographic finding appears when a patient breathes spontaneously against the ventilator due to waning neuromuscular blockade?
options: Shark-fin Phase II upstroke
Curare cleft in Phase III
Cardiac oscillations in Phase IV
Elevated baseline in Phase I
questions.explanation: Inadequate muscle relaxation allows spontaneous diaphragmatic contraction against controlled ventilation, producing an inspiratory dip or notch during the alveolar plateau known as a curare cleft.

questions.stem: What is the recommended total number of air exchanges per hour for an operating room equipped with a nonrecirculating ventilation system?
options: At least 6 exchanges per hour
At least 10 exchanges per hour
15 or more exchanges per hour
Exactly 25 exchanges per hour
questions.explanation: For nonrecirculating operating room ventilation systems, a rate of 15 or more total air exchanges per hour is recommended.

questions.stem: Which second-generation supraglottic-airway feature provides a route for gastric drainage?
options: A dedicated gastric drainage channel
An inflatable pilot balloon on the airway tube
A metal reinforcing wire in the shaft
A Murphy eye at the distal tip
questions.explanation: The textbook describes second-generation supraglottic devices such as the ProSeal and Supreme as incorporating a gastric drainage tube or access port alongside the airway channel.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the Diameter Index Safety System (DISS) are true? (Select 2)
options: It regulates high-pressure E-cylinder connections to the hanger yoke
It utilizes nationally standardized thread and diameter-specific connections
It connects pipeline hoses to machine and wall terminal inlets
It governs the connection between the endotracheal tube and breathing circuit
It utilizes 7 standardized pin positions located on a circular arc
It controls intermediate pressure reduction down to 15 psig
questions.explanation: DISS provides nationally standardized, diameter-specific, threaded connections designed to prevent accidental cross-connection of pipeline gas hoses at wall and machine inlet ports. PISS regulates cylinders.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 30

questions.stem: What happens to the displayed SpO2 reading when a pulse oximeter probe is placed on an extremity experiencing severe hypoperfusion or shivering?
options: It reliably displays the true arterial saturation despite motion
It preferentially measures venous saturation from the extremity
Motion and low perfusion can degrade the pleth signal and produce unreliable values
It automatically changes to co-oximetry mode to correct the signal
questions.explanation: Pulse oximetry depends on detecting a pulsatile arterial signal. Shivering creates motion artifact and severe hypoperfusion reduces pulse amplitude, so the plethysmographic signal may become unreliable or disappear rather than yielding a trustworthy SpO₂ value.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide in wet soda lime?
options: They permanently bind CO2 without undergoing regeneration
They act as catalysts/activators to accelerate the initial absorption reaction
They neutralize toxic carbon monoxide gas
They act as moisture desiccants to prevent rain-out in the circuit
questions.explanation: NaOH and KOH function as catalysts to speed the initial neutralization reaction by forming carbonates; they are subsequently regenerated when reacting with calcium hydroxide.

questions.stem: In a patient breathing 100% oxygen prior to induction, how long should preoxygenation be performed, or to what target expired O2 concentration?
options: 1 minute or until expired O2 reaches 50%
2 minutes or until expired O2 reaches 75%
3 to 5 minutes or until expired O2 is 90% or greater
10 minutes or until inspired O2 equals 100%
questions.explanation: Adequate preoxygenation (denitrogenation) requires tidal breathing of 100% O2 for 3 to 5 minutes or until the expired (end-tidal) oxygen concentration reaches 90% or greater.

questions.stem: What is the pipeline supply pressure delivered from hospital central gas systems to the anesthesia machine intermediate pressure system?
options: 14 to 16 psig
25 to 30 psig
50 to 55 psig
75 to 85 psig
questions.explanation: Normal hospital pipeline supply pressure for oxygen, nitrous oxide, and medical air is maintained at approximately 50 to 55 psig.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 33

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical signs indicate successful endotracheal intubation? (Select 3)
options: Presence of stable, continuous EtCO2 waveforms across 3 consecutive breaths
An immediate drop in plateau pressure below 5 cmH2O
Bilateral chest excursion and equal breath sounds on auscultation
Absence of all heart sound oscillations on the pulse plethysmograph
Persistent elevated baseline on the capnography monitor
Continuous condensation (fogging) in the tracheal tube during exhalation
questions.explanation: Verification of ETT placement requires clinical assessment (bilateral breath sounds, chest expansion, exhaled condensation) and objective confirmation with continuous EtCO2 across at least 3 consecutive breaths.

questions.stem: What is the primary danger of activating the oxygen flush valve during the inspiratory phase of mechanical ventilation?
options: Rapid desiccation of the CO2 absorbent canister
Severe pulmonary barotrauma and circuit pressure spikes
Sudden delivery of 100% saturated volatile anesthetic
Occlusion of the scavenging interface pop-off valve
questions.explanation: During mechanical inspiration, the ventilator pressure relief valve is closed. Pressing the O2 flush valve directs 35–75 L/min at 40–50 psig straight into the circuit and patient's lungs, risking catastrophic barotrauma.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 36, 37; CO₂ & Scavenging · Slide 19

questions.stem: What physical phenomenon describes gas flow preferentially moving along the smooth plastic sides of an absorbent canister rather than through the absorbent granules?
options: Regeneration
Channeling
Pumping effect
Laminar drift
questions.explanation: Channeling is the preferential flow of gas through paths of low resistance, such as along the smooth canister walls or through loosely packed granules, resulting in premature CO2 breakthrough despite unexhausted absorbent.

questions.stem: According to AANA Standard 8, which monitoring technique is strongly recommended when neuromuscular blocking drugs are administered?
options: Visual assessment of spontaneous respiratory rate alone
Quantitative monitoring (e.g., acceleromyography)
Qualitative observation of eye opening
Palpation of peripheral pulse rhythm
questions.explanation: AANA Standard 8.e states that when neuromuscular blocking agents are administered, neuromuscular response must be monitored, and quantitative monitoring (e.g., acceleromyography measuring train-of-four ratio) is recommended.

questions.stem: What is the saturated vapor pressure of Isoflurane at 20°C?
options: 160 mmHg
240 mmHg
244 mmHg
669 mmHg
questions.explanation: At 20°C, the saturated vapor pressure of Isoflurane is 240 mmHg (Halothane is 244 mmHg, Sevoflurane is 160 mmHg, and Desflurane is 669 mmHg).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: Which two wavelengths of light are emitted by conventional dual-wavelength pulse oximeters to differentiate oxyhemoglobin from deoxyhemoglobin? (Select 2)
options: 540 nm
660 nm
780 nm
940 nm
questions.explanation: Conventional pulse oximeters utilize light-emitting diodes at 660 nm (red light, absorbed primarily by deoxyhemoglobin) and 940 nm (near-infrared light, absorbed primarily by oxyhemoglobin).

questions.stem: What error in blood pressure measurement occurs when an excessively wide or large blood pressure cuff is applied to a patient's extremity?
options: Falsely elevated blood pressure reading
Falsely decreased blood pressure reading
Inability to detect cardiac arrhythmias
Blunting of the arterial dicrotic notch
questions.explanation: A cuff that is too large or wide transmits pressure over an excessively broad area, occluding the artery at lower cuff pressures and yielding falsely low (underestimated) blood pressure readings.

questions.stem: Which component of an anesthesia machine prevents transfilling between gas cylinders mounted on a dual hanger yoke assembly?
options: First-stage regulator
Cylinder check valve
Bourdon tube gauge
Fail-safe valve
questions.explanation: A check valve located in each hanger yoke ensures unidirectional gas flow from the cylinder into the machine, preventing transfilling of gas from a high-pressure cylinder into an adjacent lower-pressure cylinder.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 22

questions.stem: What capnographic artifact is created when an assistant leans against the patient's thorax during mechanical expiration?
options: Shark-fin Phase II upstroke
Transient notch mimicking a curare cleft
Complete loss of Phase IV downstroke
Sudden elevation of inspired CO2 baseline
questions.explanation: External chest compression, surgical pressure, or diaphragmatic twitching can indent the alveolar plateau (Phase III), producing a cleft or notch that mimics a spontaneous breathing effort.

questions.stem: What is the formula used to calculate Mean Body Temperature based on core and skin measurements?
options: Mean Temp = 0.50 * Tcore + 0.50 * Tskin
Mean Temp = 0.85 * Tcore + 0.15 * Tskin
Mean Temp = 0.67 * Tcore + 0.33 * Tskin
Mean Temp = 0.95 * Tcore + 0.05 * Tskin
questions.explanation: Mean body temperature is clinically calculated as: Mean Temp = (0.85 * Tcore) + (0.15 * Tskin), reflecting the dominant contribution of the central core thermal compartment.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical conditions are associated with an acute INCREASE in end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2)? (Select 3)
options: Malignant hyperthermia crisis
Sudden pulmonary artery thromboembolism
Severe accidental hypothermia
Complete disconnection of the breathing circuit
Sepsis and severe hyperthermia
Intravenous sodium bicarbonate administration
questions.explanation: Increased EtCO2 results from increased metabolic production (malignant hyperthermia, sepsis, fever) or increased delivery (bicarbonate administration, tourniquet release). Embolism, hypothermia, and disconnections reduce EtCO2.

questions.stem: What safety standard governs the threaded, gas-specific wall outlet connections for hospital medical gas pipelines?
options: Pin Index Safety System (PISS)
Diameter Index Safety System (DISS)
Compressed Gas Association 540
National Fire Protection Standard 99
questions.explanation: The Diameter Index Safety System (DISS) governs pipeline wall and machine connections using unique diameters and thread pitches. PISS governs cylinder posts.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 30

questions.stem: What is the clinical hazard associated with the regeneration phenomenon of ethyl violet indicator dye in exhausted soda lime?
options: The dye permanently stains the plastic canister wall
Exhausted absorbent turns white overnight, falsely appearing fresh the following morning
The absorbent becomes explosive upon contact with sevoflurane
Regeneration accelerates the production of carbon monoxide
questions.explanation: The lecture warns that indicator color may fade after use stops, a phenomenon called regeneration. That temporary fading can make nearly exhausted absorbent appear fresher than it is, so color should not be used as the sole indicator of absorbent status.

questions.stem: Which arterial cannulation site provides the primary source of collateral blood flow to the palmar arch of the hand?
options: Brachial artery
Ulnar artery
Axillary artery
Dorsalis pedis artery
questions.explanation: The ulnar artery is the primary contributor of arterial blood flow to the deep palmar arch of the hand; it can be cannulated if the radial artery is inaccessible, but carries similar risks of thrombosis and ischemia.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the second-stage pressure regulator on an anesthesia machine?
options: Reduces cylinder pressure down to 45 psig
Reduces pipeline or cylinder gas pressure further to 14–16 psig for O2 and 26–38 psig for N2O
Regulates scavenged waste gases into the hospital vacuum disposal line
Maintains the vaporizing sump pressure at exactly 2 atm
questions.explanation: Second-stage regulators receive gas from the pipeline or first-stage regulator and reduce pressure further (to ~14–16 psig for O2 and ~26–38 psig for N2O) to dampen line fluctuations and supply the flowmeters smoothly.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 33

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the hypoxic guard (proportioning) system are true? (Select 2)
options: It directly measures the fractional concentration of oxygen molecules in the delivered gas
It prevents delivery of 100% nitrogen if pipeline gas lines are crossed
It links oxygen and nitrous oxide flow control valves to ensure an FiO2 of at least 25%
It automatically deactivates whenever an auxiliary oxygen flowmeter is in use
It shuts off fresh gas flow if the common gas outlet check valve fails
It is a pneumatic or mechanical link between the gas flow control valves
questions.explanation: The hypoxic guard mechanically/pneumatically links O2 and N2O flow valves to prevent dialing an FiO2 < 25%. However, it senses pressure/valve mechanics, NOT gas identity, and cannot detect crossed pipelines or hypoxic tanks.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 45, 46

questions.stem: What capnographic tracing pattern is produced by small, rhythmic ripples along the plateau phase caused by the mechanical beat of the heart against the lungs?
options: Curare cleft
Shark-fin deformity
Cardiac oscillations
Pigtail baseline
questions.explanation: Cardiac oscillations are small, rhythmic undulations seen during Phase III and Phase IV caused by mechanical pulsatile contractions of the heart and great vessels transmitting gas movement against the airway sensor.

questions.stem: Which direct-laryngoscopy blade exposes the glottis by directly lifting the epiglottis?
options: Miller blade
Macintosh blade
Wisconsin mask
Eschmann introducer
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the Miller as a long, straight blade used for direct epiglottic lift. The Macintosh blade lifts the epiglottis indirectly through tension on the glossoepiglottic ligament.

questions.stem: What is the primary risk of using more than one washer (Bodok seal) when mounting an E-cylinder onto a hanger yoke?
options: It interferes with the pressure gauge calibration
It can allow the cylinder valve to clear the index pins and defeat PISS protection
It causes the cylinder relief device to rupture at normal pressure
It prevents the retaining screw from contacting the cylinder valve
questions.explanation: Only one Bodok washer should be used. Stacking washers increases the distance between the cylinder valve and the yoke face and can allow the valve post to bypass the gas-specific index pins, defeating the Pin Index Safety System.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 10, 18, 21

questions.stem: Which monitored variable may show an unexplained sudden rise during a malignant hyperthermia episode?
options: End-tidal carbon dioxide
Bispectral index only
Urine specific gravity
Central venous pressure only
questions.explanation: The textbook lists an unexplained sudden rise in end-tidal carbon dioxide among the clinical events associated with malignant hyperthermia. Rising temperature and unexplained tachycardia are also listed findings.

questions.stem: Sevoflurane is dialed at 2.5% with a fresh gas flow of 0.8 L/min over a desiccated soda lime canister. Which factors accelerate the chemical degradation of sevoflurane into Compound A? (Select 3)
options: High fresh gas flow rates (> 5 L/min)
High dialed concentration of volatile agent
Low fresh gas flow rates (< 1 L/min)
Water content of the absorbent exceeding 15%
Exclusively using calcium hydroxide without potassium or sodium hydroxides
High temperature and dryness within the absorbent canister
questions.explanation: Production of Compound A from sevoflurane is promoted by higher concentrations of dialed agent, lower fresh gas flows, and warm, desiccated absorbent containing alkali hydroxide activators.

questions.stem: Prior to transport to the CT scanner, an intubated patient is ventilated via an oxygen E-cylinder. The cylinder pressure gauge reads 475 psig. If the patient requires a continuous fresh gas flow of 5 L/min, approximately how long will this cylinder last before completely emptying?
options: 16 minutes
33 minutes
48 minutes
66 minutes
questions.explanation: A full oxygen E-cylinder holds ~660 L at 1900 psig. 475 psig is 25% of full pressure (1900 / 4 = 475), meaning 25% of volume remains: 660 L x 0.25 = 165 L. At a flow rate of 5 L/min: 165 L / 5 L/min = 33 minutes.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 12, 13

questions.stem: Sevoflurane is dialed to 2% with a fresh gas flow of 3 L/min. Using the clinical formula: Total anesthetic used (mL/hr) = Vol % x FGF (L/min) x 3, how many milliliters of liquid sevoflurane will be consumed during a 2-hour surgical procedure?
options: 18 mL
27 mL
36 mL
54 mL
questions.explanation: Using the formula: Total anesthetic used (mL/hr) = 2 (%) x 3 (L/min) x 3 = 18 mL/hr. Over a 2-hour procedure, consumption is 18 mL/hr x 2 hr = 36 mL.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 52

questions.stem: How does an oxygen fail-safe valve reduce or stop nitrous oxide flow when oxygen supply pressure falls?
options: Oxygen pressure normally holds a gate open in the nonoxygen-gas line; falling oxygen pressure allows it to close or throttle
The oxygen analyzer electrically closes the common gas outlet
The vaporizer interlock shuts the nitrous oxide cylinder valve
The scavenging system diverts nitrous oxide to wall suction
questions.explanation: The textbook describes fail-safe systems as gate-like valves in nonoxygen gas lines that are held open by pressure in the oxygen circuitry. When oxygen pressure falls below the device threshold, nitrous oxide is shut off or proportionally reduced.

questions.stem: Which of the following physical and mechanical factors promote preferential gas flow (channeling) through a carbon dioxide absorbent canister? (Select 3)
options: Using granules precisely manufactured to 4 to 8 mesh
Loose or uneven packing of absorbent granules within the canister
Maintaining an optimal absorbent water content of 15%
Positioning the canister in the inspiratory limb on the bag side
Granules with large voids or irregular granule settling
Gas moving preferentially along the smooth interior plastic canister walls
questions.explanation: Channeling is the preferential flow of gas along pathways of low resistance, such as loose packing voids or the smooth interface between the plastic canister and irregular granules. Proper 4–8 mesh sizing, 15% hydration, and circuit positioning promote uniform absorption rather than channeling.

questions.stem: During direct laryngoscopy in an adult with limited neck mobility, the provider transitions from a curved Macintosh blade to a straight Miller blade. How does the anatomical engagement of the epiglottis change?
options: The tip is positioned in the vallecula to apply greater upward force on the glossoepiglottic fold
The tip directly entraps and lifts the posterior surface of the epiglottis to expose the laryngeal inlet
The straight blade enters the pyriform sinus to displace the corniculate cartilages laterally
The straight blade rests on the base of the tongue, lifting the thyroid cartilage anteriorly
questions.explanation: The straight Miller blade is designed to pass posterior to the epiglottis, directly entrapping and lifting its posterior surface to expose the vocal cords. The curved Macintosh blade lifts the epiglottis indirectly from within the vallecula.

questions.stem: A hospital's central cryogenic liquid oxygen reservoir operates at -160°C. If ambient heat warms the liquid and builds internal head pressure above 85 psig, what safety mechanism prevents structural tank rupture?
options: A safety relief valve automatically vents gaseous oxygen to the atmosphere
A superheater coil directs excess liquid into the hospital vacuum line
A control valve diverts high-pressure gas into the nitrous oxide manifold
A frangible disk breaks to dump liquid oxygen into an underground drainage pit
questions.explanation: Bulk cryogenic vacuum-insulated tanks are equipped with spring-loaded safety relief valves that automatically vent gaseous oxygen into the atmosphere when internal headspace pressure exceeds design thresholds (typically ~85 psig).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 32

questions.stem: Which of the following monitoring abnormalities are characteristic features of a patient experiencing acute expiratory airflow obstruction during mechanical ventilation? (Select 2)
options: Simultaneous parallel elevation of both peak inspiratory and plateau pressures
Curare cleft notch appearing in the latter half of the Phase III alveolar plateau
Pressure-Volume loop shifted symmetrically to the left with increased slope
Complete absence of cardiac oscillations during the Phase IV downstroke
Shark-fin capnogram with a prolonged Phase II upstroke and blunted alpha angle
Flow-Volume loop displaying an indented, scooped-out (coved) expiratory limb
questions.explanation: Expiratory airflow obstruction (bronchospasm, asthma, COPD) slows alveolar gas emptying, producing a prolonged Phase II upstroke with an absent alpha angle on capnography ('shark-fin') and an indented, scooped expiratory curve on the flow-volume loop. Compliance-related elevations in Pplat or inspiratory curare clefts are not characteristic of airflow obstruction.

questions.stem: An anesthesia machine hanger yoke is inspected during pre-use checkout. The yoke block features index pins positioned at coordinates 3 and 5. Which gas cylinder is this specific yoke engineered to accept, and what would occur if an oxygen cylinder were forced into this yoke with multiple washers?
options: Nitrous oxide; stacked washers clear the pins, allowing incorrect gas attachment and creating a hypoxic delivery hazard
Medical air; stacked washers seat the check valve permanently, preventing cylinder flow
Nitrous oxide; stacked washers cause immediate rupture of the frangible safety disk
Carbon dioxide; stacked washers restrict the annular orifice, causing high backpressure
questions.explanation: Pin positions 3 and 5 are designated specifically for Nitrous Oxide under the Pin Index Safety System (PISS). Stacking extra washers spaces the cylinder post away from the yoke face, allowing an oxygen cylinder (pins 2 and 5) to clear the pins and mount to the N2O yoke, risking administration of hypoxic gas mixtures.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 10, 18, 20

questions.stem: While monitoring a carotid endarterectomy with a five-lead ECG cable system, which specific lead combinations provide optimal dual monitoring for both rhythm analysis and anterior myocardial ischemia?
options: Lead I for rhythm and Lead aVR for ischemia
Lead II for rhythm and Lead V3 for ischemia
Lead III for rhythm and Lead V1 for ischemia
Lead aVF for rhythm and Lead V6 for ischemia
questions.explanation: The monitoring lecture identifies Lead II for rhythm analysis, including atrial arrhythmias, and identifies V3 as the most sensitive lead in the cited perioperative ischemia study.

questions.stem: How does water vapor generated during the neutralization reaction in soda lime influence the chemical breakdown of sevoflurane?
options: Water neutralizes potassium hydroxide, permanently halting Compound A generation
Water promotes methanol production, breaking Compound A into low-toxicity compounds B, C, D, and E
Water acts as a Lewis acid that accelerates the conversion of sevoflurane into carbon monoxide
Water hydrolyzes ethyl violet dye, preventing visual indication of Compound A accumulation
questions.explanation: As detailed in the degradation schematic, in the presence of water, sevoflurane produces methanol, which promotes the breakdown of Compound A into Compound B and other low-toxicity products (C, D, and E). Desiccated absorbent prevents this degradation pathway, increasing toxic Compound A accumulation.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical factors can cause falsely low oxygen saturation (SpO2) readings or complete waveform loss on a dual-wavelength pulse oximeter despite normal arterial PaO2? (Select 3)
options: Presence of elevated carboxyhemoglobin levels (>20%)
High ambient lighting shielded by an opaque sensor cover
Severe hypothermia with profound peripheral vasoconstriction
Administration of 100% inspired oxygen via tight face mask
Intravenous administration of methylene blue dye
Severe patient shivering and gross motion artifact
questions.explanation: Severe hypoperfusion/vasoconstriction, IV dyes (methylene blue absorbs 660 nm red light, causing a precipitous false drop in SpO2), and motion artifacts impair pulse oximetry accuracy. Carboxyhemoglobin causes falsely elevated or deceptively normal readings, not low readings.

questions.stem: What is the primary operational difference between the GE Aladin cassette vaporizer and a conventional Tec-type variable bypass vaporizer?
options: The Aladin cassette contains no wicks or baffles and vaporizes agent via an ultrasonic plate
The Aladin cassette houses the agent sump, while temperature sensing and flow control valves are integrated into the machine CPU
The Aladin cassette is permanently mounted to the manifold and cannot be removed between cases
The Aladin cassette utilizes an internal bimetallic strip to regulate electrical heating of desflurane
questions.explanation: In the GE Aladin system, the cassette is a removable, agent-specific sump containing wicks and baffles that can be handled in any position. However, concentration dials, CPU processing, temperature sensors, and electronic flow control valves are housed internally inside the anesthesia workstation itself.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 66, 67

questions.stem: During a prolonged surgical procedure with an unheated, unhumidified circle breathing circuit, 50 g of water is vaporized and exhaled by the patient. Approximately how much body heat is lost exclusively through this latent heat of vaporization?
options: 5.8 kcal
14.5 kcal
29.0 kcal
58.0 kcal
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes approximately 0.58 kcal of heat for every gram of water vaporized from the respiratory tract. For 50 g of vaporized water: 50 g x 0.58 kcal/g = 29.0 kcal of heat lost.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions will cause a non-zero, elevated baseline during Phase I of the capnogram? (Select 2)
options: Chemical exhaustion of carbon dioxide absorbent granules
Sudden onset of profound systemic hypotension
Acute pulmonary embolism with increased dead space
Incompetence of the inspiratory or expiratory unidirectional valve
Excessive fresh gas flow exceeding 15 L/min
Deepening of neuromuscular blockade following rocuronium
questions.explanation: An elevated baseline during Phase I indicates carbon dioxide rebreathing. This occurs when absorbent is exhausted, when unidirectional valves fail (allowing exhaled gas to enter the inspiratory limb), or when fresh gas flows are inadequate in semi-closed circuits. Embolism and hypotension decrease EtCO2.

questions.stem: According to the lecture's NIOSH recommendation, what is the occupational exposure limit for nitrous oxide when used as the sole anesthetic agent?
options: 2 ppm
10 ppm
25 ppm
50 ppm
questions.explanation: The lecture states that nitrous oxide, when used as the sole anesthetic agent, should be controlled to a time-weighted-average concentration no greater than 25 ppm during anesthetic administration.

questions.stem: As a variable bypass vaporizer cools during vaporization, what does the temperature-compensation system do?
options: Adjusts the splitting ratio to increase flow through the vaporizing chamber
Shuts off all fresh gas flow
Raises pipeline oxygen pressure
Routes all gas around the vaporizer
questions.explanation: As liquid anesthetic cools, vapor pressure falls. The temperature-compensation element changes the splitting ratio so that more carrier gas reaches the vaporizing chamber, helping maintain the dialed concentration.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 56

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical findings meet the definition of a properly executed 'triple airway maneuver' to relieve upper airway obstruction? (Select 3)
options: Bilateral jaw thrust applied at the mandibular angles
Elevation and forward displacement of the chin (chin lift)
Continuous posterior cricoid pressure (Sellick maneuver)
Head extension at the atlanto-occipital joint
Lateral rotation of the cervical spine to 45 degrees
Insertion of a soft nasopharyngeal airway past the turbinates
questions.explanation: The triple airway maneuver consists of head extension, chin lift, and jaw thrust. It relieves soft tissue obstruction caused by the tongue and soft palate. Cricoid pressure and cervical rotation are not part of the maneuver.

questions.stem: What is the physical state of carbon dioxide inside a full medical gas cylinder at 20°C with a pressure gauge reading of 838 psig?
options: Exclusively gaseous form throughout the cylinder
Liquid in equilibrium with overlying vapor
Supercritical fluid with zero liquid boundary
Solid dry ice compacted beneath compressed gas
questions.explanation: Because the critical temperature of carbon dioxide is +31.0°C (above standard room temperature of 20°C), CO2 inside a pressurized cylinder at 838 psig exists as a liquid in equilibrium with its overlying gas phase.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 7, 14

questions.stem: During maintenance of general anesthesia, an acute rise in exhaled nitrogen is detected on the multi-gas spectrometer alongside a sudden decrease in EtCO2. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Severe venous air embolism
Chemical exhaustion of soda lime absorbent
Acute rupture of the endotracheal tube cuff
Calibration drift of the galvanic oxygen fuel cell
questions.explanation: As outlined in the multi-gas troubleshooting matrix, entrainment of room air into the vascular system during surgery (venous air embolism) introduces nitrogen into the pulmonary circulation, causing an acute appearance of exhaled nitrogen alongside a fall in EtCO2 from pulmonary hypoperfusion.

questions.stem: A nitrous oxide E-cylinder gauge remains near 745 psig for a prolonged period and then begins to fall. What physical change has occurred?
options: The liquid phase has been exhausted, leaving only gaseous nitrous oxide
The cylinder has become completely empty
The cylinder has converted entirely to liquid
The pressure regulator has increased cylinder pressure
questions.explanation: At room temperature, cylinder pressure remains near the vapor pressure of nitrous oxide while liquid and gas coexist. Once the liquid phase is gone, pressure begins to fall as the remaining gaseous nitrous oxide is consumed.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 14

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the Diameter Index Safety System (DISS) are true? (Select 2)
options: It regulates high-pressure E-cylinder mounting on the machine yoke
It governs pipeline wall and workstation gas inlet connections
It utilizes gas-specific diameter threading to prevent cross-connections
It relies on 1 to 7 pin positions located along a circular arc
It operates at pressures slightly above atmospheric pressure
It requires a single Bodok seal washer to prevent forward leakage
questions.explanation: DISS provides nationally standardized, diameter-specific threaded fittings that prevent accidental interchange of pipeline supply hoses at wall and machine terminal connections. PISS governs high-pressure cylinders.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 30

questions.stem: During a check-out of the intermediate pressure system, you disconnect the pipeline oxygen hose while the oxygen cylinder remains closed. At what pressure threshold should the oxygen supply low-pressure alarm activate?
options: 50 to 55 psig
40 to 45 psig
25 to 30 psig
10 to 15 psig
questions.explanation: The oxygen supply failure alarm is set to activate when oxygen pressure within the intermediate system falls below approximately 25 to 30 psig (the same threshold that triggers the fail-safe valve).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 34

questions.stem: Examine the Mason-Likar ECG lead placement schematic below. Where should electrode V3 be positioned on the chest wall?
options: Fourth intercostal space at the right sternal border
Fourth intercostal space at the left sternal border
Equidistant between electrode V2 and electrode V4
Fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line
questions.explanation: According to the Mason-Likar electrode placement criteria, lead V3 is placed on the anterior chest wall exactly midway (equidistant) between lead V2 (4th ICS left sternal border) and lead V4 (5th ICS left midclavicular line).
