questions.stem: What low-flow sevoflurane limitation is stated in the Nurse Anesthesia textbook?
options: Avoid total fresh gas flows below 1-2 L/min for more than 2 MAC-hours
Always use less than 0.5 L/min for the entire anesthetic
Compound A formation is unrelated to fresh gas flow
Sevoflurane requires a minimum flow of 10 L/min
questions.explanation: The textbook notes that the sevoflurane product insert does not recommend total fresh gas flows below 1 to 2 L/min for more than 2 MAC-hours because lower flows can increase Compound A exposure.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical factors will shift the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to the RIGHT, facilitating oxygen offloading to peripheral tissues? (Select 3)
options: Acute hypercapnia (increased PaCO2)
Acute hypocapnia induced by hyperventilation
Systemic metabolic acidosis (decreased pH)
Elevated core body temperature (hyperthermia)
Severe accidental systemic hypothermia
Decreased levels of 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG)
questions.explanation: A right shift in the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve decreases hemoglobin oxygen affinity, improving O2 delivery to tissues. This is caused by acidosis, hypercapnia, hyperthermia, and increased 2,3-DPG (the Bohr effect). Alkalosis, hypothermia, and low 2,3-DPG shift the curve to the left.

questions.stem: A modern circle system incorporates an active waste gas scavenging system connected to hospital wall vacuum. If the vacuum line fails completely, what safety component prevents excessive positive pressure buildup in the patient circuit?
options: The scavenging interface positive-pressure relief (pop-off) valve vents waste gases into the room
The second-stage oxygen regulator shuts off flow to the Thorpe tubes
The ventilator pressure relief valve seats to lock gas in the bellows
The negative-pressure relief pop-in valve opens to draw in operating room air
questions.explanation: In an active closed-reservoir scavenging interface, failure or obstruction of the disposal vacuum leads to pressure buildup. When threshold pressure is reached, the spring-loaded positive-pressure relief (pop-off) valve opens, safely venting excess waste gases into the operating room to prevent pulmonary barotrauma.

questions.stem: Following prone positioning for spine surgery, an intubated patient demonstrates sudden, complete loss of the end-tidal carbon dioxide waveform. Which sequence represents the FIRST and most vital diagnostic priority?
options: Simultaneously verify chest rise, auscultate bilateral lung fields, and assess circuit integrity to rule out accidental extubation or disconnect
Recalibrate the infrared optical sensor against ambient room air to clear moisture
Administer an immediate intravenous bolus of atropine to treat vagal nerve compression
Switch the mechanical ventilator from volume control to pressure support ventilation
questions.explanation: A sudden loss of the EtCO2 waveform is a life-threatening emergency signaling complete circuit disconnect, airway extubation/obstruction, or cardiac arrest. The immediate first action is a rapid multisensory sweep: confirming chest expansion, auscultating breath sounds, and evaluating the circuit connection.

questions.stem: Which quantitative train-of-four ratio is used as the recovery threshold before extubation?
options: At least 0.90
At least 0.50
At least 0.25
Exactly 1 twitch
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia lists a train-of-four ratio greater than 0.9 among criteria indicating recovery from neuromuscular blockade and emphasizes objective monitoring for residual blockade.

questions.stem: In an operating room where an empty room has high background nitrous oxide levels (>50 ppm), which system is the most probable location of the leak?
options: The low-pressure carbon dioxide absorbent canister gasket
The high- or intermediate-pressure nitrous oxide pipeline connections or cylinder yokes
The circle system expiratory limb corrugated tubing
The scavenger open-reservoir atmospheric relief ports
questions.explanation: When an OR is not in use, background N2O contamination is primarily caused by leaks in the high- and intermediate-pressure systems (26 to 750 psig), such as defective wall quick-connects or tank yoke connections.

questions.stem: Which of the following volatile anesthetics undergo less than 0.5% total hepatic metabolism in the human body? (Select 2)
options: Sevoflurane
Desflurane
Halothane
Methoxyflurane
Enflurane
Isoflurane
questions.explanation: Desflurane undergoes <0.05% metabolism and Isoflurane undergoes ~0.2% metabolism. In contrast, Sevoflurane is 2–5% metabolized, and Halothane is 15–40% metabolized.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: During a procedure under general anesthesia, what is the significance of the patient's arterial blood pressure tracing shifting from a radial artery site to a dorsalis pedis artery site?
options: Systolic blood pressure will read falsely lower due to peripheral vascular resistance
Systolic blood pressure will read higher and pulse pressure will widen due to peripheral wave reflection
Mean arterial pressure will increase by 20 to 30 mmHg due to hydrostatic pressure
The dicrotic notch will shift earlier onto the peak systolic upstroke
questions.explanation: Moving from central to peripheral arteries (e.g., radial to dorsalis pedis), wave reflection exaggerates the pressure wave, increasing peak systolic blood pressure and widening pulse pressure, while diastolic pressure falls and MAP remains nearly unchanged.

questions.stem: Which action should be avoided when filling a variable bypass vaporizer?
options: Turning the vaporizer dial completely to the 'OFF' position before opening the filler port
Filling the vaporizer sump while the vaporizer concentration dial remains turned 'ON'
Tightening the keyed adapter firmly onto the anesthetic bottle before insertion
Monitoring the liquid level through the front sight glass during agent delivery
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies filling while the vaporizer is on as a cause of overfilling or contamination of the bypass chamber or vaporizer outlet. It instructs the provider to turn the vaporizer off and fill it to the specified level.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 70

questions.stem: Why does breathing supplemental 100% oxygen make pulse oximetry an insensitive monitor for detecting acute hypoventilation during procedural sedation?
options: High PaO2 creates a large oxygen reservoir in the functional residual capacity, delaying arterial desaturation for several minutes despite apnea
Oxygen blunts peripheral chemoreceptor sensitivity, locking the photodetector ratio at 1:1
Supplemental oxygen converts reduced hemoglobin into methemoglobin at the tissue capillary bed
Pulse oximeters autocalibrate to expired EtCO2 values when high FiO2 is entrained
questions.explanation: Patients breathing supplemental O2 maintain a high alveolar oxygen reserve (FRC). In the event of hypoventilation or apnea, PaO2 can remain on the flat upper plateau of the dissociation curve for several minutes before desaturation registers on the pulse oximeter. Capnography detects hypoventilation instantly.

questions.stem: During a surgical case with Sevoflurane, why is continuous capnographic monitoring far more reliable than distal esophageal temperature monitoring for detecting early malignant hyperthermia?
options: Unexplained rapid increases in expired CO2 reflect immediate muscle hypermetabolism, whereas core temperature elevation is a late sign
Temperature probes fail to register core changes when forced-air warming blankets are active
Sevoflurane acts directly on the hypothalamus to suppress shivering without changing core temperature
Capnography measures dissolved carbonic acid in blood whereas temperature probes measure peripheral skin loss
questions.explanation: An unexplained, rapid rise in EtCO2 is the earliest, most sensitive indicator of malignant hyperthermia, reflecting intense skeletal muscle hypermetabolism. Hyperthermia itself is a late sign of MH; waiting for core temperature to rise delays life-saving dantrolene therapy.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical conditions are recognized causes of an acute elevation in both peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) and plateau pressure (Pplat)? (Select 3)
options: Tension pneumothorax
Tracheal tube cuff herniation
Aspiration of a foreign body
Bilateral pleural effusions
Abdominal laparoscopy packing
Bronchospasm
questions.explanation: Simultaneous elevation of PIP and Pplat reflects decreased pulmonary compliance (e.g., tension pneumothorax, pleural effusion, abdominal packing, ascites, Trendelenburg). Cuff herniation, foreign body aspiration, and bronchospasm increase airway resistance, elevating PIP alone while Pplat remains unchanged.

questions.stem: What is the primary operational mechanism of an oxygen analyzer utilizing a galvanic fuel cell?
options: Oxygen molecules are attracted into a pulsating magnetic field, creating a measurable pressure difference
Oxygen diffuses across a membrane and is chemically reduced at the cathode, generating a current that consumes the sensor
Infrared light absorption at 4.3 microns is measured across a narrow sapphire optical window
A heated zirconium oxide ceramic element generates voltage based on differential ion concentrations
questions.explanation: Galvanic fuel cells generate electrical current from an oxygen-dependent chemical reaction. Oxygen diffuses across a semipermeable membrane and is reduced at a gold cathode and lead anode, consuming the sensor over time. Paramagnetic analyzers use magnetic fields; IR spectrophotometers analyze CO2 and volatile agents.

questions.stem: Which airway approach is included in the textbook's management options for a patient with cervical spine injury when awake intubation is chosen?
options: Awake flexible fiberoptic intubation
Blind nasal intubation with neck extension
Routine direct laryngoscopy without stabilization
Elective cricothyrotomy for every patient
questions.explanation: The textbook's cervical-spine-injury airway algorithm includes awake fiberoptic intubation as an option. Technique selection depends on the clinical situation, urgency, and ability to maintain oxygenation and spinal precautions.

questions.stem: Which of the following physical properties are correctly paired with Desflurane? (Select 2)
options: Blood:gas partition coefficient of 1.46
MAC of 1.17% in a 40-year-old adult
Vapor pressure of 669 mmHg at 20°C
Hepatic metabolic rate of 2% to 5%
Critical temperature of -118.6°C
Boiling point of 22.8°C at 1 atmosphere
questions.explanation: Desflurane has a vapor pressure of 669 mmHg at 20°C, boils at 22.8°C, has a blood:gas partition coefficient of 0.42, and a MAC of 6.6%. Isoflurane has a blood:gas partition of 1.46 and MAC of 1.17%.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: A patient's Pressure-Volume (P-V) spirometry loop demonstrates an open loop failure where the expiratory curve terminates abruptly above the horizontal baseline. What is the clinical cause?
options: Severe acute bronchospasm
A substantial leak within the breathing circuit or around the tracheal cuff
Abnormally increased lung compliance from bullous emphysema
Severe kinking of the inspiratory limb corrugated hose
questions.explanation: An 'open loop' on a P-V spirometry tracing occurs when the expired volume returning to the machine is substantially less than the delivered inspired volume, pathognomonic for a breathing circuit leak or deflated/leaking tracheal tube cuff.

questions.stem: What is the primary clinical utility of an auxiliary oxygen flowmeter mounted on the side of an anesthesia workstation?
options: Provides supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula or mask without disrupting the breathing circuit
Pressurizes the bellows housing during mechanical ventilator cycling
Purges volatile anesthetic vapors from the low-pressure circuit at emergence
Acts as a backup pressure regulator in the event of pipeline failure
questions.explanation: The auxiliary O2 flowmeter delivers pure O2 (up to 10 L/min) from the machine's pipeline connection for supplemental delivery (cannula, face mask, self-inflating bag) without requiring disconnection or altering the main breathing circuit.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 44

questions.stem: What design feature of a standard cuffed endotracheal tube is intended to reduce focal pressure on tracheal tissues?
options: A high-volume, low-pressure cuff
A rigid low-volume, high-pressure cuff
An uncuffed distal balloon
A metal-reinforced Murphy eye
questions.explanation: The airway lecture describes cuffed tracheal tubes as using high-volume, low-pressure cuffs that disperse force over the tracheal tissues.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical scenarios will cause a widening of the normal PaCO2–EtCO2 gradient (>5 mmHg)? (Select 3)
options: Intravenous administration of sodium bicarbonate
Acute pulmonary artery thromboembolism
Severe bullous emphysema (COPD)
One-lung ventilation during thoracic surgery
Release of an extremity surgical tourniquet
Hypoventilation in a healthy young adult
questions.explanation: Conditions that increase alveolar dead space or create severe V/Q mismatch (pulmonary embolism, emphysema, one-lung ventilation, low cardiac output) impair CO2 excretion, widening the PaCO2–EtCO2 gradient. Bicarbonate, tourniquet release, and simple hypoventilation increase both PaCO2 and EtCO2 without necessarily widening the gradient.

questions.stem: How does the proportioning system (hypoxic guard) prevent the delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture on an anesthesia machine?
options: An internal paramagnetic sensor continuously samples the mixed gas at the common gas outlet
A mechanical or pneumatic linkage between oxygen and nitrous oxide valves ensures FiO2 is maintained at ≥25%
An electrical solenoid closes the N2O line whenever inspired oxygen drops below 21%
A pressure-relief pop-off valve dumps nitrous oxide into the scavenging disposal line
questions.explanation: The proportioning system (hypoxic guard) mechanically or pneumatically links the O2 and N2O flow control valves to ensure that when nitrous oxide is dialed, oxygen flow is automatically maintained to guarantee an FiO2 of at least 25%. However, it senses valve position/pressure, NOT gas identity.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 45, 46

questions.stem: In an Ohmeda flowmeter manifold arranged in the standard sequence (Air -> N2O -> O2), a crack develops in the glass Thorpe tube of the upstream nitrous oxide flowmeter. What gas mixture effect will reach the patient?
options: 100% pure nitrous oxide will be entrained into the patient circuit
Nitrous oxide escapes into the room while oxygen continues downstream safely toward the common gas outlet
Oxygen is siphoned backward into the nitrous oxide line, creating a severe circuit leak
The second-stage regulator locks, terminating all gas flow to the common gas outlet
questions.explanation: Because oxygen is positioned furthest downstream (closest to the outlet), a leak or crack in an upstream tube (such as N2O) allows carrier gas to escape into room air while oxygen continues forward unimpeded, preventing the delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 41

questions.stem: According to the monitoring lecture, what can a pigtail capnogram indicate?
options: Poor lung compliance or a unique breath-stacking pattern
A normal Phase I baseline
Only esophageal intubation
Only an exhausted CO2 absorber
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the pigtail capnogram as a sudden sharp upward deflection just before inspiration that can indicate poor lung compliance or a unique breath-stacking pattern.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical factors represent essential elements of AANA Practice Standard 9 regarding alarm management? (Select 3)
options: Alarms may be permanently muted if baseline vital signs fall outside preset limits
Alarm limit parameters and audible warning systems must be actively engaged
Audible ventilator disconnect alarms may be deactivated during low-flow anesthesia
Variable-pitch auditory alarms (such as pulse oximetry) should be utilized
Every sounding alarm must be evaluated clinically every single time rather than dismissed
Visual alarm lights may replace all audible annunciators during microsurgery
questions.explanation: AANA Standard 9 mandates active alarm limits, audible warning systems, variable pitch pulse oximetry alarms, and vigilant provider evaluation of every sounding alarm to combat alarm fatigue and avoid preventable harm.

questions.stem: What physical property of volatile anesthetics determines their rate of elimination and speed of emergence following a prolonged surgical anesthetic?
options: Oil:gas partition coefficient
Blood:gas partition coefficient
Molecular weight in grams per mole
Saturated vapor pressure at 20°C
questions.explanation: Blood:gas solubility (partition coefficient) determines the rate of alveolar wash-in and wash-out. Agents with low blood:gas solubility (e.g., Desflurane 0.42, Sevoflurane 0.65) clear rapidly from the blood into alveoli, facilitating fast emergence.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: During thoracic surgery, one-lung ventilation is established. What arterial blood gas abnormality is expected due to transpulmonary shunt through the non-ventilated operative lung?
options: Severe metabolic alkalosis with widened arterial-to-venous CO2 difference
Significant decrease in PaO2 with a widened alveolar-arterial (A-a) oxygen gradient
Dramatic increase in PaO2 due to hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction
Complete suppression of peripheral chemoreceptor responsiveness
questions.explanation: One-lung ventilation creates a major right-to-left transpulmonary shunt as deoxygenated blood perfuses the non-ventilated, collapsed lung. This widens the A-a gradient, resulting in a marked drop in PaO2 and widening the PaCO2–EtCO2 difference.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the physical characteristics of Nitrous Oxide are correct? (Select 2)
options: It has a molecular weight of 29 g/mol
It has a vapor pressure of 669 mmHg at 20°C
It persists in the atmosphere for approximately 14 years
It is metabolized by hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes at a rate of 5%
It has a boiling point of -88.5°C at 1 atmosphere
It has a critical temperature of +36.4°C
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide boils at -88.5°C, has a critical temperature of +36.4°C, a molecular weight of 44 g/mol, a cylinder pressure of 745 psig at 20°C, and an atmospheric lifetime of 114 years. It undergoes no hepatic metabolism.
questions.citation: CO₂ & Scavenging · Slide 22; Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 14, 50

questions.stem: In an infant undergoing cardiac surgery with an open ductus arteriosus, where should the non-invasive blood pressure cuff be placed to most accurately reflect cerebral perfusion pressure?
options: Left calf (postductal)
Right upper arm (preductal)
Left upper arm (postductal)
Right calf (postductal)
questions.explanation: In neonates and premature infants with potential ductal shunting, preductal arterial pressure (measured on the right upper arm) reflects blood flow prior to the ductus arteriosus, best approximating right common carotid and cerebral perfusion.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical factors can lead to an elevated baseline on the capnography waveform during general anesthesia? (Select 3)
options: Excessive fresh gas flow rates (>10 L/min)
Acute hypothermia with decreased metabolic rate
Exhaustion of wet soda lime absorbent
Incompetent expiratory unidirectional valve
Incompetent inspiratory unidirectional valve
Partial obstruction of the endotracheal tube lumen
questions.explanation: An elevated baseline indicates rebreathing of CO2. Causes include exhausted absorbent, incompetent inspiratory or expiratory valves, and inadequate fresh gas flow in semi-closed circuits. High flows prevent rebreathing; hypothermia and obstruction alter waveform height or slope.

questions.stem: Why does the second-stage oxygen pressure regulator reduce gas pressure to 14–16 psig, while the second-stage nitrous oxide regulator reduces pressure to 26–38 psig?
options: To ensure nitrous oxide flow velocity matches Thorpe tube annular orifice requirements
To dampen line pressure fluctuations and ensure smooth, stable gas flow to flow control needle valves
To prevent liquid nitrous oxide from condensing within the flowmeter manifold
To enforce an automatic pneumatic shut-off of oxygen whenever pipeline pressure fluctuates
questions.explanation: Second-stage regulators receive gas from the intermediate supply (pipeline or 1st stage regulator) and drop pressures further to dampen upstream pressure surges, delivering ultra-stable pressure to the delicate flow control needle valves.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 33

questions.stem: A patient with severe bullous emphysema is mechanically ventilated. How will their Flow-Volume (F-V) spirometry loop appear compared to a normal loop?
options: Narrow and tall with symmetrically reduced volumes ('witch's hat')
Indented, deeply scooped-out (coved) expiratory curve with prolonged expiration
Truncated, flattened plateaus along both inspiratory and expiratory limbs
Coarse, saw-toothed oscillations isolated along the inspiratory limb
questions.explanation: Obstructive lung diseases (emphysema, COPD, asthma) cause expiratory airflow limitation and gas trapping, manifesting as a scooped-out (coved) expiratory curve with prolonged expiratory time and increased residual volume on the F-V loop.

questions.stem: During a prolonged anesthetic using nitrous oxide, what cuff-related change does the textbook list as a possible complication?
options: Increased intracuff pressure
Complete spontaneous cuff deflation
Conversion of the cuff to a rigid solid
Permanent elimination of cuff pressure
questions.explanation: The textbook lists increased intracuff pressure during prolonged procedures using nitrous oxide or carbon dioxide among airway-device complications.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical signs provide immediate physical evidence of successful endotracheal intubation prior to capnographic confirmation? (Select 2)
options: Equal, bilateral thoracic expansion during positive-pressure ventilation
Immediate appearance of cardiac oscillations on the pulse plethysmograph
Sudden decrease in measured circuit peak inspiratory pressure below 10 cmH2O
Bilateral auscultation of breath sounds in the axillae and absence of gastric sounds
Loss of the dicrotic notch on the invasive radial arterial line tracing
Visual identification of condensation clearing during inspiration
questions.explanation: Physical signs confirming tracheal placement include bilateral chest expansion, equal bilateral breath sounds in both axillae with an absence of epigastric sounds, and exhaled condensation (fogging) in the tube.

questions.stem: During a craniotomy under general anesthesia, what capnographic tracing abnormality will appear if the patient's spontaneous diaphragmatic movement occurs asynchronously against controlled ventilator cycles?
options: A prolonged, sloped Phase II upstroke with loss of the alpha angle
A downward dip or notch (curare cleft) in the Phase III alveolar plateau
A failure of Phase IV to return to the zero baseline
Sawtooth oscillations along the inspiratory downstroke
questions.explanation: A curare cleft is an inspiratory notch in Phase III caused by patient spontaneous diaphragmatic effort as neuromuscular block wanes.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the check valve located downstream of the vaporizers near the common gas outlet on certain anesthesia workstations?
options: Prevents fresh gas flow from entering the breathing system if pipeline pressure falls
Prevents backpressure fluctuations (from positive pressure ventilation or O2 flush) from altering vaporizer output
Regulates scavenged waste gases passing into the active vacuum disposal conduit
Maintains the pressure inside the absorbent canister at exactly 50 psig
questions.explanation: An outlet check valve isolates the low-pressure system (flowmeters and vaporizers) from breathing circuit pressure spikes (from positive-pressure ventilation or depressing the O2 flush valve), minimizing the pumping effect.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 38, 49, 72

questions.stem: When difluoromethyl ethers (desflurane, enflurane, isoflurane) pass through an absorbent canister that has been desiccated by high oxygen flows over a weekend, which absorbent formulation produces the HIGHEST concentration of toxic carbon monoxide gas?
options: Barium hydroxide lime (Baralyme)
Standard wet soda lime
Pure calcium hydroxide without metal hydroxides
Silica-gel stabilized calcium carbonate
questions.explanation: As stated in the volatile agent degradation notes, the use of barium hydroxide lime (Baralyme) results in significantly more carbon monoxide production than the use of standard soda lime when reacting with desiccated difluoromethyl ethers.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events will produce an acute INCREASE in measured end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2)? (Select 3)
options: Sudden massive pulmonary thromboembolism
Severe accidental hypothermia with core temp < 32°C
Acute cardiac arrest with cessation of pulmonary blood flow
Intravenous administration of sodium bicarbonate
Deflation and release of a lower extremity surgical tourniquet
Acute hypoventilation in a spontaneously breathing patient
questions.explanation: Increased EtCO2 results from increased metabolic production, increased delivery to the lungs (bicarbonate bolus, tourniquet release), or decreased alveolar elimination (hypoventilation). Pulmonary embolism, hypothermia, and cardiac arrest decrease EtCO2.

questions.stem: Why does the textbook recommend carbon dioxide absorbents with lower or no potassium hydroxide content?
options: Potassium hydroxide is implicated in carbon monoxide and Compound A production
Potassium hydroxide prevents carbon dioxide absorption
Potassium hydroxide eliminates all water from the canister immediately
Potassium hydroxide makes the canister unable to change color
questions.explanation: The textbook notes that potassium hydroxide is used less frequently because it has been implicated in reactions that produce carbon monoxide and Compound A, and it recommends absorbents with lower or no strong-base content, particularly KOH.

questions.stem: What is the intended anatomical effect of cricoid pressure during rapid-sequence induction?
options: Posterior displacement of the cricoid cartilage against the cervical vertebrae to reduce regurgitation risk
Anterior displacement of the thyroid cartilage to open the esophagus
Direct compression of the trachea to stop ventilation
Rotation of the larynx to the left to expose the glottis
questions.explanation: The textbook describes cricoid pressure as posterior displacement of the cricoid cartilage against the cervical vertebrae with the intent of reducing regurgitation and aspiration risk. It also notes ongoing debate regarding the exact anatomic mechanism.

questions.stem: Which of the following monitoring modalities are specifically classified as quantitative rather than qualitative methods for verifying respiratory ventilation? (Select 2)
options: Auscultation of bilateral breath sounds with a precordial stethoscope
Continuous quantitative capnography (EtCO2 numerical value and waveform)
Spirometric measurement of exhaled tidal volume and minute ventilation
Visual observation of reservoir breathing bag excursions
Palpation of chest wall movement during assisted breaths
Assessment of exhaled condensation fogging within the face mask
questions.explanation: Quantitative monitoring provides numerical, objective measurements of respiratory function (EtCO2 in mmHg, exhaled tidal volume in mL). Auscultation, bag movement, chest excursion, and mask fogging are qualitative clinical assessments.

questions.stem: A patient's invasive arterial line transducer is leveled at the right atrium (phlebostatic axis). If the patient is placed into steep reverse Trendelenburg position for robotic surgery, how will the recorded radial arterial pressure compare to actual cerebral perfusion pressure?
options: The transducer reading will overestimate cerebral perfusion pressure due to hydrostatic column height
The transducer reading will underestimate cerebral perfusion pressure by approximately 2 mmHg per inch
The transducer reading will accurately reflect cerebral perfusion pressure without correction
Diastolic pressure will read accurately while systolic pressure drops to zero
questions.explanation: In head-up (reverse Trendelenburg) positions, the brain sits higher than the heart. For every 15 cm (or ~8 inches) vertical distance above the leveling reference, arterial pressure in cerebral vessels is ~10–12 mmHg lower than the pressure measured at the phlebostatic axis. Thus, a heart-level transducer overestimates cerebral perfusion pressure.

questions.stem: What is the maximum recommended concentration dial setting for Sevoflurane on a standard commercial variable bypass vaporizer?
questions.explanation: Variable bypass vaporizers for sevoflurane are calibrated up to 8% to facilitate inhalational inductions. Vaporizers for isoflurane and halothane are typically calibrated up to 5%, while desflurane vaporizers are calibrated up to 12–18%.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 58

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding operating room ventilation and air distribution systems are true? (Select 3)
options: The fresh air inflow port is located in the ceiling
The air exhaust port is located on an adjacent wall approximately 6 inches above the floor
Standard operating rooms must maintain at least 30 total air exchanges per hour
Recirculating ventilation systems effectively scrub ambient volatile anesthetic vapors
Nonrecirculating ventilation systems discard 100% of room air to the outside
Waste gas scavenging may be vented directly into any standard hospital return duct
questions.explanation: OR ventilation systems intake clean air through the ceiling and exhaust stale air through ports 6 inches above the floor. Nonrecirculating systems discard 100% of air outside (>15 exchanges/hr). Standard filtration does NOT remove anesthetic vapors, which is why active scavenging is mandatory.

questions.stem: Which factor is most likely to make a pulse oximeter reading unreliable when the probe is placed on a poorly perfused extremity?
options: Low pulsatile signal amplitude at the sensor site
A high inspired oxygen concentration
Continuous electrocardiographic monitoring
Normal arterial pulsatility at the sensor site
questions.explanation: Pulse oximetry requires an adequate pulsatile arterial signal. Poor peripheral perfusion reduces pulse amplitude at the probe site and can make the displayed saturation unreliable or prevent the monitor from obtaining a reading.

questions.stem: During a pre-use check of an older anesthesia workstation, the low-pressure system is tested using a negative-pressure leak bulb. If a leak is detected, which component is the most probable source?
options: A loose or worn vaporizer filler cap gasket
A damaged pipeline Diameter Index Safety System connector
A loose hanger yoke clamp screw holding the oxygen reserve cylinder
A defective diaphragm inside the primary first-stage pressure regulator
questions.explanation: The low-pressure negative pressure check tests the circuit from flow control needle valves to the common gas outlet. Common leak sites include loose or worn vaporizer filler caps, unseated vaporizer manifold mounts, or defective flowmeter glass seals. Pipeline and cylinder connections are high/intermediate pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 38, 49, 69; CO₂ & Scavenging · Slide 13

questions.stem: What is the PISS pin configuration for a carbon dioxide E-cylinder?
options: Positions 1 and 5
Positions 2 and 5
Positions 3 and 5
Positions 1 and 6
questions.explanation: Under the Pin Index Safety System, Carbon Dioxide uses pin coordinates 1 and 6 (or 2 and 6 depending on percentage mixtures, with pure CO2 being 1 and 6). Oxygen is 2 and 5, N2O is 3 and 5, and Medical Air is 1 and 5.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 18

questions.stem: During direct laryngoscopy with a curved Macintosh blade, which provider error is most likely to cause maxillary dental trauma while failing to adequately expose the vocal cords?
options: Levering the handle backward using the upper incisors as a fulcrum instead of lifting upward and forward along the axis of the handle
Inserting the blade tip too deeply past the glossoepiglottic fold directly into the esophagus
Applying excessive anterior traction on the body of the hyoid bone with the left wrist
Rotating the laryngoscope blade 90 degrees counterclockwise into the left tonsillar fossa
questions.explanation: A curved Macintosh blade lifts the epiglottis indirectly by stretching the glossoepiglottic ligament within the vallecula. Levering the handle backward pivots against the upper incisors, risking tooth fracture while driving the base of the blade down into the visual axis, obscuring the cords.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical conditions are associated with decreased static pulmonary compliance, causing an increase in plateau pressure (Pplat) during volume-controlled ventilation? (Select 3)
options: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
Mucus plug partially occluding the endotracheal tube
Mainstem endobronchial intubation
Severe acute bronchospasm
Severe pulmonary edema
Inadvertent administration of 100% oxygen
questions.explanation: Decreased static compliance (and elevated Pplat) is caused by conditions affecting lung parenchyma, chest wall, or lung volume (ARDS, mainstem intubation, pulmonary edema, pneumothorax). Mucus plugging and bronchospasm increase airway resistance, elevating PIP alone while Pplat remains unchanged.

questions.stem: A patient undergoing general anesthesia with Desflurane is ventilated with 1 L/min O2 and 1 L/min Air. What is the atmospheric lifetime of Desflurane, and why is this an environmental concern?
options: 1.1 years; it accelerates the formation of ground-level tropospheric ozone
3.2 years; it converts ambient nitrogen into nitrous oxide
14 years; it is a potent greenhouse gas that traps escaping thermal radiation
114 years; it destroys stratospheric ozone via chlorofluorocarbon radicals
questions.explanation: Desflurane persists in the atmosphere for 14 years and has a high global warming potential. Inhaled anesthetics trap thermal radiation escaping Earth's surface and account for over one-third of the carbon footprint of an average surgical case.

questions.stem: Compared with a second-generation supraglottic airway, what pressure-related limitation does the LMA Classic have?
options: A lower airway seal, with ventilation pressure limited to about 20 cmH2O
A higher seal than the ProSeal, allowing pressures above 40 cmH2O
No cuff, so positive-pressure ventilation is impossible
A rigid tracheal cuff that prevents gastric insufflation
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia states that the ProSeal LMA provides an improved seal that permits peak ventilation pressures of about 28 to 30 cmH2O, compared with about 20 cmH2O for the LMA Classic.

questions.stem: Which of the following safety mechanisms are built into the intermediate pressure system of an anesthesia machine? (Select 2)
options: Hanger yoke index check valve
Oxygen supply failure low-pressure alarm
Cylinder Bourdon pressure gauge
Vaporizer Select-a-Tec interlock pins
Flowmeter Thorpe tube float stops
Oxygen fail-safe valve
questions.explanation: The intermediate system includes pipeline inlets, line pressure gauges, oxygen supply low-pressure alarms, the fail-safe valve, second-stage regulators, and the O2 flush valve. Yokes and cylinder gauges are high-pressure; vaporizers and flowmeters are low-pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 25, 26, 76

questions.stem: Why is cricoid pressure traditionally used during rapid-sequence induction in patients at risk for aspiration?
options: To reduce regurgitation and aspiration of gastric contents
To improve venous return
To increase lower-esophageal sphincter tone
To eliminate the need for preoxygenation
questions.explanation: The textbook describes cricoid pressure as posterior displacement of the cricoid cartilage intended to reduce regurgitation and possible aspiration during induction, particularly in aspiration-risk patients undergoing rapid-sequence induction.

questions.stem: During maintenance of general anesthesia, the capnography monitor displays cardiac oscillations along the alveolar plateau and downstroke. What physical mechanism creates this tracing?
options: Mechanical contraction of the heart and great vessels transmitting gas movement against the airway sensor
Incompetence of the expiratory unidirectional breathing circuit valve
Diaphragmatic twitching induced by peripheral nerve stimulator testing
Condensed moisture accumulating within the infrared analyzer sample tube
questions.explanation: Cardiac oscillations are small, rhythmic undulations seen during Phase III and Phase IV caused by mechanical pulsatile contractions of the heart and thoracic great vessels transmitting gas movement against the tracheobronchial tree.

questions.stem: Which statements about nasopharyngeal airways are supported by the lecture? Select 3.
options: Awake patients generally tolerate them better than oropharyngeal airways
Water-based lubricant or local anesthetic may be used for insertion
Epistaxis is the most common complication
They are positioned in the trachea
They require direct laryngoscopy for insertion
They are less tolerated than oral airways in awake patients
questions.explanation: The lecture states that awake patients tolerate NPAs better than OPAs, recommends water-based lubricant or local anesthetic for insertion, and identifies epistaxis as the most common complication. It also notes that the device lies in the hypopharynx.

questions.stem: What is the blood:gas partition coefficient of Sevoflurane at 37°C?
questions.explanation: The blood:gas partition coefficient of Sevoflurane is 0.65 (Desflurane is 0.42, Isoflurane is 1.46, and Halothane is 2.50).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: During a general anesthetic case with an endotracheal tube in place, you notice a triangular, slanted drop in the capnogram alveolar plateau. What is the most probable cause?
options: A substantial leak within the breathing circuit or around the endotracheal tube cuff
Severe acute bronchospasm causing complete loss of the alpha angle
Early manifestation of malignant hyperthermia crisis
Chemical exhaustion of potassium hydroxide activator granules
questions.explanation: A slanted, triangular capnogram contour is characteristic of a leak in the breathing circuit or an unsealed/underinflated endotracheal tube cuff, allowing air entrainment and premature pressure loss during exhalation.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the oxygen flush valve are correct? (Select 2)
options: It operates at low pressure (slightly above atmospheric pressure)
It delivers gas at a controlled rate of 10 to 15 L/min
It delivers 100% pure oxygen directly to the common gas outlet
It receives oxygen downstream of the second-stage regulator
It can be used continuously during inspiration to maintain minute ventilation
It bypasses workstation flowmeters and vaporizers completely
questions.explanation: The O2 flush valve delivers 35–75 L/min of unmetered, pure oxygen directly to the common gas outlet at intermediate pressure (40–50 psig), completely bypassing flowmeters and vaporizers. Using it during inspiration risks barotrauma.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 36, 37

questions.stem: When configuring a five-lead ECG system for perioperative monitoring, where should the Right Arm (RA) and Left Arm (LA) electrodes be placed on the surgical patient according to the Mason-Likar system?
options: Directly over the right and left wrists
In the right and left infraclavicular fossae near the outer clavicles
Over the 4th intercostal space at the midaxillary lines
On the right and left superior iliac crests
questions.explanation: To minimize motion artifacts and clear the surgical field during surgery, the Mason-Likar system relocates the limb electrodes to the torso: RA and LA are placed in the right and left infraclavicular fossae (over the outer clavicles).

questions.stem: During general anesthesia with mechanical ventilation, which of the following alarm conditions must provide an immediate AUDIBLE signal to the anesthesia care team?
options: Disconnection of components of the patient breathing system
Depletion of the backup battery to 80% capacity
Closure of the vaporizer filler port sealing screw
Activation of the auxiliary oxygen flowmeter knob
questions.explanation: ASA standards mandate that when mechanical ventilation is in use, a device capable of detecting breathing system disconnection (e.g., low peak pressure, low exhaled volume, low EtCO2) must be active and provide an audible signal when threshold is breached.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical signs indicate an increased risk of difficult face mask ventilation (BVM) during anesthesia induction? (Select 3)
options: Mallampati Class I airway view
Presence of a full beard
Edentulous patient anatomy
Thyromental distance greater than 6.5 cm
Morbid obesity with body mass index > 30 kg/m2
Full range of cervical spine flexion and extension
questions.explanation: Common risk factors for difficult mask ventilation include facial hair (impairs seal), edentulous status (cheek collapse), obesity/high BMI (redundant pharyngeal tissue), advanced age, and history of snoring/OSA.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a check valve placed between the vaporizer and common gas outlet?
options: To minimize the pumping effect from pressure transmitted backward from the breathing circuit
To increase pipeline oxygen pressure
To prevent cylinder transfilling
To open the scavenging reservoir to atmosphere
questions.explanation: The lecture states that a check valve between the vaporizer and common gas outlet minimizes the pumping effect caused by retrograde pressure changes during positive-pressure ventilation or oxygen-flush use.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 72

questions.stem: In a closed-reservoir scavenging interface, what should happen if the hospital vacuum generates excessive negative pressure?
options: The negative-pressure relief valve opens and admits room air into the reservoir
The positive-pressure pop-off valve closes permanently
Negative pressure is intentionally transmitted to the patient
The oxygen flush valve opens automatically
questions.explanation: The lecture states that excessive vacuum causes the negative-pressure relief, or pop-in, valve to open so room air is drawn into the scavenging reservoir, preventing excessive negative pressure from reaching the breathing circuit.

questions.stem: Peritoneal insufflation causes peak inspiratory pressure and plateau pressure to rise in parallel during volume-controlled ventilation. What mechanism best explains the pattern?
options: Decreased pulmonary compliance
Isolated increase in airway resistance
Increased fresh gas flow
Failure of the oxygen analyzer
questions.explanation: The monitoring lecture states that a parallel increase in peak and plateau pressure indicates decreased pulmonary compliance. Laparoscopic insufflation is listed as a cause of decreased compliance.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical factors will lead to an OVERESTIMATION of true systolic arterial blood pressure when using an automated non-invasive oscillometric cuff? (Select 2)
options: Using a blood pressure cuff that is excessively large or wide for the extremity
Positioning the blood pressure cuff significantly above the level of the right atrium
Selecting an inflation cycle interval of exactly 3 minutes
Placing the cuff on the right arm of a premature neonate
Using a blood pressure cuff that is too small or narrow for the extremity
Positioning the blood pressure cuff significantly below the level of the right atrium
questions.explanation: Cuffs that are too small require excessive inflation pressure to compress the artery, falsely elevating readings. Cuffs placed below heart level add hydrostatic fluid column pressure (~0.74 mmHg per cm vertical distance), falsely elevating pressure readings. Cuffs that are too large or placed above heart level cause falsely low readings.

questions.stem: What is the primary clinical difference between fractional hemoglobin oxygen saturation (measured by co-oximetry) and functional oxygen saturation (measured by pulse oximetry)?
options: Functional saturation evaluates oxyhemoglobin as a percentage of all oxygen-capable hemoglobin species, ignoring dyshemoglobins
Fractional saturation is calculated exclusively from arterial blood gas PaO2 using the Severinghaus equation
Functional saturation measures carboxyhemoglobin and methemoglobin as part of the total oxygen carrying capacity
Fractional saturation can be continuously monitored using standard finger probes in the operating room
questions.explanation: Pulse oximeters measure functional saturation: [HbO2 / (HbO2 + Hb)] x 100, ignoring dyshemoglobins. Co-oximetry measures fractional saturation: [HbO2 / (HbO2 + Hb + COHb + MetHb)] x 100, differentiating all hemoglobin species.

questions.stem: During fiberoptic-guided intubation, which visual landmark confirms that the flexible scope has entered the subglottic trachea rather than the esophagus?
options: Pink, smooth, collapsible mucosal folds with prominent longitudinal vessels
White cartilaginous C-shaped rings with a posterior membranous wall
Bifurcation of the pyriform sinuses with lateral recess pooling
Visual identification of the epiglottic tip resting against the posterior pharynx
questions.explanation: The trachea is identified on bronchoscopy by rigid, anterior C-shaped cartilaginous rings, the flat posterior membranous wall, and distal bifurcation at the carina into right and left mainstem bronchi.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events are recognized causes of decreased measured end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2)? (Select 3)
options: Release of a lower extremity surgical tourniquet
Severe systemic hypothermia with core temperature < 34°C
Chemical exhaustion of carbon dioxide absorbent
Sudden profound hemorrhagic shock
Severe shivering during emergence from anesthesia
Hyperventilation with mechanical minute volume of 14 L/min
questions.explanation: Decreased EtCO2 occurs with reduced CO2 production (hypothermia), reduced delivery to the lungs (hemorrhagic shock/hypoperfusion), or excessive alveolar washout (hyperventilation). Tourniquet release, exhausted absorbent, and shivering increase EtCO2.

questions.stem: Which hanger-yoke component is tightened to secure an E-cylinder against the yoke nipple and Bodok seal?
options: The retaining screw operated by the T-handle
The Pin Index Safety System pin
The cylinder pressure-relief device
The pipeline inlet check valve
questions.explanation: The hanger-yoke assembly uses the T-handle and retaining screw to press the cylinder valve firmly against the yoke nipple and Bodok seal, creating a secure gas-tight connection.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 20-21

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanism by which general anesthesia impairs normal human thermoregulatory defense against hypothermia?
options: Inhibition of both afferent and efferent hypothalamic thermoregulatory control, widening the interthreshold range
Direct peripheral vasodilation caused by blockade of beta-2 adrenergic receptors
Uncoupling of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation within skeletal muscle
Stimulation of heat loss exclusively through increased respiratory evaporative loss
questions.explanation: The lecture states that general and regional anesthesia inhibit afferent and efferent thermoregulatory control, impairing normal defenses against perioperative heat loss.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the physical characteristics of Halothane are true? (Select 2)
options: It has a saturated vapor pressure of 244 mmHg at 20°C
It contains a difluoromethyl ether structure that produces high carbon monoxide
It has a blood:gas partition coefficient of 0.42
It undergoes approximately 15% to 40% hepatic metabolism
It has a boiling point of 22.8°C at 1 atmosphere
It has a minimum alveolar concentration (MAC) of 6.6%
questions.explanation: Halothane has a vapor pressure of 244 mmHg at 20°C and undergoes 15–40% hepatic metabolism (associated with halothane hepatitis). It is a halogenated alkane (not an ether), has a blood:gas coefficient of 2.50, and MAC of 0.76%.
questions.citation: CO₂ & Scavenging · Slide 7; Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: During mask ventilation in an edentulous elderly patient, you experience a poor mask seal with substantial gas leakage around the cheeks. What is the most effective immediate intervention?
options: Insert an oropharyngeal airway to lift the tongue and stent the oral soft tissues
Perform extreme hyperextension of the cervical spine to stretch pharyngeal muscles
Switch immediately to a straight Miller laryngoscope blade without preoxygenation
Inflate the face mask pneumatic cushion to maximum pressure with a 20 mL syringe
questions.explanation: In edentulous patients, loss of dental structure allows cheeks to collapse into the oral cavity, impairing face mask seal. Inserting an oropharyngeal airway (OPA) lifts the tongue and provides mechanical structure that dramatically improves mask seal.

questions.stem: What is the critical temperature of Carbon Dioxide, above which it cannot be liquefied by pressure alone?
questions.explanation: The critical temperature of CO2 is +31.0°C. Above this temperature, CO2 behaves strictly as a gas regardless of pressure. Oxygen is -118.6°C and Nitrous Oxide is +36.4°C.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 7, 11, 14

questions.stem: During emergence from general anesthesia, loss of upper-airway muscle tone can cause obstruction through which mechanism?
options: Posterior displacement of the tongue against the pharyngeal wall
Negative-pressure pulmonary edema directly closing the airway
Increased functional residual capacity
Anterior displacement of the soft palate
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia describes poor muscle tone after anesthesia as a cause of tongue-related upper-airway obstruction. Jaw thrust, chin lift, or placement of an oral or nasal airway may be required to restore patency.
questions.citation: Nurse Anesthesia, 7th ed. · Postanesthesia airway obstruction

questions.stem: During general anesthesia with mechanical ventilation, which capnographic waveform feature directly reflects the slope of expiratory ventilation and alveolar gas emptying?
options: The duration of the Phase I flat baseline
The slope and rate of rise of the Phase II upstroke (B–C)
The depth of the cardiac oscillations in Phase IV
The angle of the inspiratory downstroke (D–E)
questions.explanation: Phase II (B–C) represents the rapid transition from anatomic dead space to alveolar gas. The slope of this upstroke is directly determined by the evenness of expiratory emptying; bronchoconstriction and obstruction slow emptying, flattening this slope.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the retaining screw on a workstation cylinder hanger yoke?
options: Prevents gas from transfilling into adjacent lower-pressure cylinders
Tightens and clamps the cylinder valve post firmly against the yoke nipple and Bodok seal
Adjusts the calibrated output of the first-stage pressure regulator
Manually overrides the oxygen fail-safe valve during emergency operation
questions.explanation: The retaining screw (T-handle) is threaded through the hanger yoke clamp. Tightening it drives its pointed tip into the conical depression on the rear of the cylinder post, clamping the valve tightly against the Bodok seal.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 16, 20

questions.stem: An inspired carbon dioxide concentration above zero during maintenance of anesthesia most directly indicates what problem?
options: Rebreathing of carbon dioxide
Excessive oxygen supply pressure
Hyperventilation without rebreathing
A fully functional absorbent canister
questions.explanation: An elevated inspired CO2 or nonzero capnogram baseline indicates rebreathing. The lecture lists exhausted absorbent and incompetent unidirectional valves among causes.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical advantages are provided by second-generation supraglottic airway devices (e.g., LMA Supreme, ProSeal) over first-generation devices? (Select 2)
options: Complete protection against aspiration equal to a cuffed endotracheal tube
A dedicated gastric drainage channel permitting decompression of stomach contents
A higher mucosal seal pressure allowing ventilation at higher peak airway pressures
Elimination of all risk of stimulating laryngospasm during light anesthesia
Resistance to laser ignition allowing use during CO2 laser airway resection
Direct insertion through the cricothyroid membrane during CICO emergencies
questions.explanation: The textbook describes second-generation devices such as the ProSeal as adding a gastric drainage tube and improving the airway seal compared with the LMA Classic, permitting higher ventilation pressures.

questions.stem: What is the primary reason why clinical providers should NOT rely solely on ethyl violet color change when deciding whether to replace a carbon dioxide absorbent canister?
options: Ethyl violet can bleach under intense room lighting and undergoes the regeneration phenomenon overnight
Ethyl violet only changes color when exposed to carbon monoxide, not carbon dioxide
Ethyl violet turns purple prematurely when fresh gas flows exceed 5 L/min
Ethyl violet causes chemical crystallization that permanently masks color transition
questions.explanation: The lecture states that ethyl violet can be bleached by intense light and that some color fades after use stops because of regeneration. It specifically warns that indicator color should not be relied on by itself.

questions.stem: [REINFORCEMENT: Q102] Desflurane is administered at a dialed concentration of 6% with a fresh gas flow of 2 L/min. Using the clinical consumption formula: Liquid agent used (mL/hr) = Vol % x FGF (L/min) x 3, how many milliliters of liquid desflurane will be consumed during a 3-hour surgical procedure?
options: 36 mL
72 mL
108 mL
144 mL
questions.explanation: Consumption rate = 6 (%) x 2 (L/min) x 3 = 36 mL/hr. For a 3-hour procedure: 36 mL/hr x 3 hr = 108 mL of liquid agent.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 52

questions.stem: Examine the variable bypass vaporizer splitting diagram below. To deliver 1% sevoflurane at a total fresh gas flow of 2 L/min (sump vapor concentration 21% at 20°C), total inflow is split into 2000 mL/min bypass flow and 79 mL/min sump flow. What is the precise splitting ratio?
questions.explanation: As shown in the variable bypass calculation, 2079 mL/min entering the vaporizer splits into 2000 mL/min bypass and 79 mL/min sump flow. 2000 / 79 = 25.3:1 (approximately a 25:1 splitting ratio).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 55

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events will produce an acute DECREASE in measured end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) while minute ventilation remains constant? (Select 3)
options: Acute pulmonary artery thromboembolism
Sudden profound hemorrhagic shock
Sudden onset of severe systemic hypothermia
Surgical release of an abdominal aortic cross-clamp
Chemical exhaustion of carbon dioxide absorbent granules
Rapid intravenous administration of sodium bicarbonate
questions.explanation: Decreased EtCO2 occurs with increased dead space (pulmonary embolism), decreased pulmonary blood flow (hypovolemic/hemorrhagic shock), or decreased cellular CO2 production (hypothermia). Aortic unclamping, absorbent exhaustion, and bicarbonate boluses increase EtCO2.

questions.stem: During maintenance of general anesthesia, an unexpected rapid rise in end-tidal CO2 occurs alongside masseter muscle rigidity. Core temperature remains 37.0°C. What is the immediate priority intervention?
options: Administer IV dantrolene, turn off volatile agents, hyperventilate with 100% O2, and call for help
Apply ice packs to axillae and wait for distal esophageal temperature to exceed 38.5°C
Switch the mechanical ventilator to pressure control and replace the ETT with a reinforced tube
Calibrate the galvanic oxygen fuel cell to verify delivered oxygen fractions
questions.explanation: The textbook recommends prompt treatment when malignant hyperthermia is identified: call for help, discontinue triggering agents, administer dantrolene, and hyperventilate with 100% oxygen. A normal temperature does not exclude an evolving episode because rising temperature may occur later.

questions.stem: Why does the Tec 6 Desflurane vaporizer require external electrical power while modern variable bypass vaporizers (e.g., Tec 5, Vapor 2000) do not?
options: Desflurane boils near room temperature (22.8°C) and requires electrical heating to 39°C and pressurization to 2 atm to control vapor output
Desflurane degrades into carbon monoxide unless an electrical cathode continuously hydrolyzes the agent
Desflurane requires ultrasonic nebulization to saturate carrier gas within the variable bypass chamber
Desflurane activates the Select-a-Tec interlock pins via an internal magnetic solenoid
questions.explanation: Desflurane has a boiling point of 22.8°C and an extremely high vapor pressure (669 mmHg at 20°C). In a standard vaporizer, it would boil uncontrollably at operating room temperatures. The Tec 6 electrically heats desflurane to 39°C and pressurizes the sump to 1500 mmHg (2 atm) to inject pure vapor into the fresh gas stream, requiring electrical power.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 60, 65

questions.stem: Which of the following monitoring modalities are classified by the ASA and AANA as acceptable methods for continuously evaluating patient circulatory function? (Select 2)
options: Automated non-invasive blood pressure cycling every 15 minutes
Continuous display of the arterial pulse plethysmographic waveform or pulse oximetry
Precordial stethoscope auscultation restricted to emergence only
Continuous monitoring of central venous pressure via an umbilical catheter
Continuous electroencephalographic Bispectral Index (BIS) monitoring
Continuous display of the electrocardiogram (ECG)
questions.explanation: ASA Standard 2.3 mandates continuous ECG display and continuous circulatory evaluation by pulse palpation, auscultation, intra-arterial tracing, ultrasound, or pulse plethysmography/oximetry. NIBP must be evaluated at least every 5 minutes, not every 15.

questions.stem: A patient with severe emphysema is placed on mechanical ventilation. How will their Flow-Volume (F-V) spirometry loop appear compared to a patient with normal pulmonary mechanics?
options: Narrow and tall with symmetrically reduced lung volumes ('witch's hat')
Prominent concave indentation (scooped-out coving) of the expiratory flow limb with prolonged expiration
Truncated, flattened horizontal plateaus across both inspiratory and expiratory limbs
Irregular saw-tooth oscillations isolated along the inspiratory flow baseline
questions.explanation: Obstructive diseases (emphysema, COPD, asthma) cause expiratory airflow limitation and air trapping, manifesting on the F-V loop as an indented, scooped-out (coved) expiratory curve with prolonged expiration. Restrictive disease shows a narrow, tall 'witch's hat' shape. Fixed obstructions produce flattened plateaus on both limbs.

questions.stem: [REINFORCEMENT: Q106] If the primary pressure regulator on a central bulk liquid oxygen tank fails, what safety mechanism prevents structural rupture of the insulated storage vessel?
options: A safety relief valve vents gaseous oxygen to the atmosphere when pressure exceeds ~85 psig
A superheater coil directs excess liquid into the hospital vacuum line
A check valve diverts liquid oxygen into the medical air pipeline manifold
The vacuum insulation breaks down to convert liquid oxygen into medical grade nitrogen
questions.explanation: Bulk cryogenic vacuum-insulated vessels operate at ~ -160°C and maintain head pressure with safety relief valves that vent vapor to the atmosphere when internal pressures exceed design thresholds (typically ~85 psig).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 32

questions.stem: During direct laryngoscopy, what is the correct anatomical positioning of the tip of a curved Macintosh blade?
options: Directly beneath the posterior surface of the epiglottis to lift it anteriorly
Into the vallecula, stretching the glossoepiglottic ligament to elevate the epiglottis indirectly
Within the left pyriform sinus to displace the left arytenoid cartilage
Directly through the vocal cords to stent the subglottic trachea
questions.explanation: The curved Macintosh blade is advanced into the vallecula anterior to the epiglottis. Elevating the blade tensions the glossoepiglottic ligament, which indirectly lifts the epiglottis forward to expose the vocal cords.

questions.stem: Which of the following physical and mechanical factors directly promote the formation of Compound A when sevoflurane is administered? (Select 3)
options: High concentrations of dialed sevoflurane
Low fresh gas flow rates (< 1 L/min)
Maintaining fresh gas flows above 5 L/min throughout the case
Using absorbent with water content maintained strictly at 15%
Using barium hydroxide-free pure calcium hydroxide absorbent
High temperature within a dry, desiccated carbon dioxide absorbent canister
questions.explanation: Compound A production from sevoflurane is accelerated by warm, dry absorbent, high agent concentrations, and low fresh gas flows. High flows, adequate hydration (~15%), and strong-base-free absorbents reduce Compound A accumulation.

questions.stem: An arterial line transducer is zeroed and leveled at the right atrium. The surgical table is placed into steep Trendelenburg (head-down) position. How will the displayed arterial blood pressure compare to actual arterial pressure at the patient's circle of Willis?
options: The transducer reading will underestimate cerebral arterial pressure due to hydrostatic column pressure
The transducer reading will overestimate cerebral arterial pressure by 2 mmHg per inch
The transducer reading will remain perfectly identical to cerebral pressure regardless of gravity
Systolic blood pressure will read accurately while diastolic blood pressure drops to zero
questions.explanation: In head-down (Trendelenburg) positions, the brain sits below the level of the heart/right atrium. Hydrostatic pressure increases intravascular pressure in vessels below the transducer. Therefore, a transducer at the right atrium underestimates actual arterial pressure delivered to the cerebral circulation.

questions.stem: What is the primary indicator dye used in soda lime, and what color change occurs as the absorbent becomes exhausted?
options: Ethyl violet, which transitions from white to blue-violet
Ethyl orange, which transitions from yellow to orange
Cresyl yellow, which transitions from yellow to red
Phenolphthalein, which transitions from pink to clear
questions.explanation: Ethyl violet is the standard indicator dye added to soda lime; it is white when fresh and turns blue-violet as hydroxides are converted to carbonates and pH falls below alkaline levels.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the Diameter Index Safety System (DISS) are correct? (Select 2)
options: It utilizes pin holes positioned along a circular arc on gas cylinder posts
It governs high-pressure cylinder yoke attachments between 45 and 2200 psig
It provides nationally standardized, diameter-specific threaded fittings
It utilizes purple color coding for central vacuum and white for waste gas
It connects the common gas outlet check valve to the breathing circuit
It prevents accidental cross-connection of pipeline gas hoses to machine wall inlets
questions.explanation: DISS utilizes nationally standardized, diameter-specific threaded connections to prevent pipeline cross-connections at machine and wall terminal inlets. PISS governs high-pressure cylinders. Purple is waste gas and white is central vacuum.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 30

questions.stem: During maintenance of anesthesia, the capnography monitor displays the waveform below with an elevated baseline during Phase I (>5 mmHg). What is the primary diagnosis?
options: Rebreathing of carbon dioxide due to exhausted absorbent or incompetent unidirectional valves
Acute bronchospasm causing severe expiratory airflow obstruction
Curare cleft resulting from patient spontaneous diaphragmatic effort
Complete disconnection of the breathing circuit at the Y-piece
questions.explanation: An elevated capnogram baseline during inspiration (Phase I > 0 mmHg) confirms rebreathing of carbon dioxide. This occurs when absorbent is exhausted, fresh gas flow is inadequate, or inspiratory/expiratory unidirectional valves fail.
