questions.stem: What is the critical temperature of Nitrous Oxide, above which it cannot exist as a liquid regardless of applied pressure?
questions.explanation: The critical temperature of N2O is +36.4°C. Because this is above room temperature (20°C), compressed N2O in a cylinder remains a liquid in equilibrium with vapor. Oxygen is -118.6°C and CO2 is +31.0°C.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 14

questions.stem: Which airway complication does the textbook associate with excessive endotracheal-tube cuff pressure?
options: Laryngotracheal edema
Improved mucosal perfusion
Reduced risk of airway injury
Increased functional residual capacity
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia lists excessive cuff pressure among factors that can cause laryngotracheal edema after intubation.

questions.stem: Why does the oxygen flowmeter control knob feature a fluted, physically larger profile positioned furthest to the right on the manifold?
options: To provide tactile differentiation and place oxygen downstream so upstream leaks do not cause hypoxic mixtures
To increase mechanical torque for overcoming second-stage regulator backpressure
To ensure oxygen enters the vaporizing chamber before carrier gases
To allow manual calibration of the hypoxic guard proportioning gears
questions.explanation: The O2 knob is larger and fluted so it can be identified by touch. Placing oxygen furthest downstream (to the right, closest to the outlet) ensures that leaks in upstream flowmeters vent other gases into the room, preserving oxygen delivery.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 40, 41

questions.stem: During volume-controlled mechanical ventilation, the peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) rises from 20 to 36 cmH2O while plateau pressure (Pplat) rises from 16 to 32 cmH2O. Which clinical condition is most consistent with this change?
options: Endotracheal tube kinking
Tracheal secretions
Acute tension pneumothorax
Severe bronchospasm
questions.explanation: A parallel increase in both PIP and Pplat reflects a decrease in pulmonary compliance (such as tension pneumothorax, pulmonary edema, mainstem intubation, or abdominal insufflation). Tube kinking, secretions, and bronchospasm increase airway resistance, elevating PIP alone while Pplat remains unchanged.

questions.stem: Which of the following volatile anesthetics do NOT produce carbon monoxide when exposed to desiccated carbon dioxide absorbent? (Select 2)
options: Desflurane
Isoflurane
Enflurane
Methoxyflurane
Sevoflurane
Halothane
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide generation requires a difluoromethyl ether moiety (-O-CHF2), found in Desflurane, Enflurane, and Isoflurane. Sevoflurane and Halothane lack this structure and do not produce CO.

questions.stem: Why is a nitrous oxide cylinder pressure gauge a poor indicator of remaining contents while liquid nitrous oxide is still present?
options: The pressure remains near 745 psi while liquid and vapor coexist
The pressure falls linearly from the moment the cylinder is opened
The gauge measures oxygen rather than nitrous oxide
Nitrous oxide has no vapor pressure at room temperature
questions.explanation: The textbook states that nitrous oxide is stored as a liquid and its gauge remains near 745 psi at room temperature until the liquid phase is gone. Only then does pressure decline rapidly with further use.

questions.stem: In an operating room equipped with a nonrecirculating ventilation system, what is the minimum recommended air exchange rate per hour?
options: 6 exchanges per hour
10 exchanges per hour
15 or more exchanges per hour
30 exchanges per hour
questions.explanation: Nonrecirculating ventilation systems discard 100% of room air to the outside, and a rate of 15 or more total air exchanges per hour is recommended.

questions.stem: Which of the following items are included in the intermediate-pressure system of an anesthesia machine? (Select 3)
options: Pipeline gas inlets and line pressure gauges
Bourdon cylinder pressure gauges
Hanger yoke assemblies
Thorpe flowmeter glass indicator tubes
Oxygen fail-safe valve
Oxygen flush valve
questions.explanation: The intermediate system (14–55 psig) contains pipeline inlets, check valves, gauges, the oxygen fail-safe valve, second-stage regulators, auxiliary O2 flowmeters, and the O2 flush valve. Cylinder yokes and Bourdon gauges are high-pressure; Thorpe tubes are low-pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 25, 26, 76

questions.stem: A patient's invasive radial arterial line tracing displays an underdamped dynamic response. What corrective action will improve dynamic measurement fidelity?
options: Remove unnecessary extension tubing, eliminate stopcocks, and aspirate all air bubbles from the line
Add two additional stopcocks and 12 inches of compliant extension tubing
Relevel the transducer 20 cm below the phlebostatic axis
Flush the catheter continuously with high-pressure unmetered oxygen
questions.explanation: Dynamic fidelity requires high natural frequency and adequate damping. Underdamping causes ringing and systolic overshoot. Removing excess tubing and stopcocks, eliminating compliant elements, and purging microscopic air bubbles improves dynamic response.

questions.stem: What is the primary danger associated with activating the oxygen flush valve during the inspiratory cycle of mechanical ventilation?
options: Catastrophic pulmonary barotrauma because the ventilator relief valve is closed
Immediate desiccation of the carbon dioxide absorbent canister
Vaporizer contamination from massive retrograde flow into the sump
Locking of the second-stage pressure regulator diaphragm
questions.explanation: During mechanical inspiration, the ventilator pressure relief valve is closed. Depressing the O2 flush valve delivers 35–75 L/min at 40–50 psig directly to the patient circuit, transmitting massive pressures into the lungs and risking tension pneumothorax or barotrauma.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 36, 37; CO₂ & Scavenging · Slide 19

questions.stem: Which of the following physical mechanisms represent the two primary methods used by clinical oxygen analyzers to measure breathing circuit oxygen concentration? (Select 2)
options: Paramagnetic analysis exploiting oxygen's attraction to magnetic fields
Infrared absorption spectrophotometry measuring light at 4.3 microns
Mass spectrometry analyzing magnetic deflection of ionized nitrogen
Galvanic fuel cell analysis generating current from chemical reduction of oxygen
Piezoelectric crystal resonance oscillation
Electrical heating of an internal bimetallic expansion strip
questions.explanation: Breathing system O2 is measured primarily by paramagnetic analyzers (oxygen is paramagnetic and drawn into magnetic fields) or galvanic fuel cells (electrochemical reduction of O2 generates current). Infrared analysis cannot measure O2 because O2 is a nonpolar diatomic molecule.

questions.stem: When an Eschmann introducer is advanced into the trachea, which tactile finding can help confirm tracheal placement?
options: A bouncing sensation over the tracheal rings
Complete absence of any tactile feedback in every case
A pulse transmitted from the carotid artery
A sudden increase in pilot-balloon pressure
questions.explanation: The textbook notes that feeling the Eschmann introducer bounce along the tracheal rings can help confirm tracheal placement, although the sensation is not always present.

questions.stem: What is the PISS pin configuration for a Medical Air E-cylinder?
options: Positions 1 and 5
Positions 2 and 5
Positions 3 and 5
Positions 2 and 6
questions.explanation: Medical Air uses pin positions 1 and 5 under the Pin Index Safety System. Oxygen is 2 and 5; Nitrous Oxide is 3 and 5.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 18

questions.stem: A curare cleft appears during controlled ventilation. What should be assessed next?
options: Neuromuscular blockade, with additional relaxant considered if indicated
The oxygen cylinder color only
The scavenging vacuum pressure only
The vaporizer filling port
questions.explanation: A curare cleft reflects spontaneous inspiratory effort during controlled ventilation and can indicate waning neuromuscular blockade. The appropriate next step is to assess blockade and determine whether additional relaxant is indicated.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events are recognized causes of increased peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) with an UNCHANGED plateau pressure (Pplat)? (Select 3)
options: Mainstem endobronchial intubation
Endotracheal tube kinked by patient positioning
Acute bronchospasm
Acute pulmonary edema
Peritoneal carbon dioxide insufflation
Airway secretions obstructing the tracheal lumen
questions.explanation: An isolated increase in PIP without a change in Pplat reflects increased airway resistance (e.g., kinked tube, bronchospasm, secretions, foreign body). Mainstem intubation, pulmonary edema, and peritoneal insufflation decrease compliance, causing both PIP and Pplat to rise simultaneously.

questions.stem: What is the saturated vapor pressure of Desflurane at 20°C?
options: 160 mmHg
240 mmHg
244 mmHg
669 mmHg
questions.explanation: At 20°C, the vapor pressure of Desflurane is 669 mmHg. Sevoflurane is 160 mmHg, Isoflurane is 240 mmHg, and Halothane is 244 mmHg.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: According to ASA basic monitoring standards, how often must non-invasive arterial blood pressure and heart rate be documented during monitored anesthesia care (MAC)?
options: At least every 3 minutes
At least every 5 minutes
At least every 10 minutes
Every 15 minutes if sedation remains light
questions.explanation: ASA Standard 2.3 applies to all anesthetics (general, regional, and MAC) and mandates that arterial blood pressure and heart rate must be determined and evaluated at least every five minutes.

questions.stem: Which of the following components of an anesthesia machine belong to the high-pressure system? (Select 2)
options: Diameter Index Safety System pipeline inlets
Reserve gas cylinder hanger yokes
Bourdon cylinder pressure gauges
Second-stage pressure regulators
Auxiliary oxygen flowmeter
Rotameter flow control needle valves
questions.explanation: The high-pressure system includes components upstream of the first-stage regulator: cylinder yokes, check valves, Bourdon gauges, and first-stage regulators. DISS inlets, second-stage regulators, and auxiliary flowmeters are intermediate-pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 5, 6, 76

questions.stem: What is the primary consequence of applying an excessively small blood pressure cuff to an adult patient's arm?
options: Blood pressure readings will be falsely elevated
Blood pressure readings will be falsely low
The oscillometric monitor will fail to detect mean arterial pressure
Pulse pressure will narrow without altering systolic values
questions.explanation: A cuff that is too narrow requires higher inflation pressure to compress the artery, resulting in falsely elevated systolic and diastolic blood pressure readings.

questions.stem: Why does the second-stage oxygen regulator drop pressure down to 14–16 psig on an anesthesia workstation?
options: To eliminate pressure fluctuations and supply constant, stable pressure to the flow control needle valves
To prevent liquid oxygen from vaporizing within the Thorpe tubes
To match the downstream pressure of the scavenging active disposal line
To prevent the oxygen fail-safe valve from opening prematurely
questions.explanation: Second-stage regulators receive gas from the pipeline or first-stage regulator and reduce pressure further (to 14–16 psig for O2) to dampen line surges and provide steady pressure to the flow control needle valves.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 33

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical features are characteristic of an armored (anode / flexo-metallic) endotracheal tube? (Select 3)
options: Contains a preformed downward curve to clear the surgical field in oral cases
Contains an embedded wire coil wound in a spiral throughout the shaft
Impermeable to carbon dioxide laser strikes
Eliminates the requirement for cuff pressure monitoring
Resistant to kinking and external compression when bent or flexed
Useful in head, neck, and prone surgical procedures
questions.explanation: Armored tubes feature an embedded wire coil that resists kinking and collapse when flexed during head, neck, or prone surgeries. Preformed curves belong to RAE tubes. Armored tubes are flammable and not laser-resistant.

questions.stem: During a procedure using pulse oximetry, severe patient shivering occurs. What is the expected effect on monitor performance?
options: Motion artifact may distort the pleth waveform and make the SpO₂ value unreliable
The device automatically converts to invasive arterial saturation monitoring
The displayed saturation becomes fixed at 85% until shivering stops
The sensor increases infrared wavelength to remove all motion artifact
questions.explanation: Shivering produces motion artifact that interferes with pulse-oximeter photoplethysmography. The pleth waveform and displayed saturation may therefore become inaccurate or intermittently unreadable until signal quality improves.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2] in wet soda lime absorbent?
options: It serves as the bulk reactant that reacts with intermediate carbonates to permanently form calcium carbonate
It functions as an initial catalyst to hydrolyze carbon dioxide into carbonic acid
It absorbs toxic carbon monoxide gas generated by difluoromethyl ethers
It prevents ethyl violet dye from undergoing the regeneration phenomenon
questions.explanation: Calcium hydroxide constitutes ~80% of soda lime. It reacts with sodium and potassium carbonates to precipitate calcium carbonate and regenerate the hydroxide catalysts.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events can cause carboxyhemoglobinemia leading to falsely elevated SpO2 readings? (Select 2)
options: Topical administration of benzocaine spray
Smoke inhalation from a structural fire
Accidental intravenous overdose of prilocaine
Chemical neutralization of carbon dioxide by fresh wet soda lime
Rapid denitrogenation with 100% inspired oxygen
Exposure of desflurane to completely desiccated carbon dioxide absorbent
questions.explanation: Carboxyhemoglobin (COHb) is formed by smoke inhalation or by degradation of volatile difluoromethyl ethers (desflurane > enflurane > isoflurane) passing over dry absorbent. Benzocaine and prilocaine induce methemoglobinemia, not carboxyhemoglobinemia.

questions.stem: Which airway route does the Nurse Anesthesia textbook say should be avoided when a basilar skull fracture is suspected?
options: Nasal intubation
Oral endotracheal intubation
Mask ventilation
Oral airway placement
questions.explanation: The textbook states that nasal intubation should be avoided when a basilar skull fracture is suspected because cranial-base disruption may be present.
questions.citation: Nurse Anesthesia, 7th ed. · Head injury airway management

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the first-stage pressure regulator on an anesthesia workstation?
options: Reduces high cylinder pressure (up to 2200 psig) down to a constant intermediate pressure of ~45 psig
Reduces pipeline supply pressure from 50 psig down to 15 psig
Controls gas flow entering the common gas outlet during mechanical ventilation
Prevents excessive backpressure from entering the vaporizer bypass chamber
questions.explanation: The first-stage regulator reduces variable high cylinder pressure down to approximately 45 psig. Because pipeline supply enters at 50–55 psig, pipeline gas is consumed preferentially over cylinder reserves.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 24, 33

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical conditions are recognized causes of decreased measured end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2)? (Select 3)
options: Acute hypoventilation in a paralyzed patient
Malignant hyperthermia crisis
Accidental esophageal intubation
Surgical release of a tourniquet
Severe systemic hypothermia
Total breathing circuit disconnection
questions.explanation: Decreased EtCO2 occurs with esophageal intubation (no pulmonary CO2 delivery), hypothermia (reduced CO2 production), and circuit disconnection. Hypoventilation, malignant hyperthermia, and tourniquet release increase EtCO2.

questions.stem: What is the blood:gas partition coefficient of Isoflurane at 37°C?
questions.explanation: The blood:gas partition coefficient of Isoflurane is 1.46. Desflurane is 0.42, Sevoflurane is 0.65, and Halothane is 2.50.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: During a pre-anesthetic checkout, an anesthesia provider notes that a vaporizer has been tipped on its side during transport. What is the proper corrective action?
options: Flush the vaporizer on high fresh gas flow at maximum dialed concentration for 30 minutes until gas analysis clears
Immediately autoclave the manifold and replace the internal bimetallic strip
Submerge the vaporizer sump in sterile water to purge the wicks
Invert the vaporizer completely and open the filler port
questions.explanation: If a variable bypass vaporizer is tipped, liquid agent enters the bypass channel. It must be drained and flushed on high FGF at maximum dial setting for 30 minutes until expired gas analysis confirms zero vapor output.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 71

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the hypoxic guard (proportioning) system are correct? (Select 2)
options: It directly measures the fractional concentration of oxygen molecules in the delivered gas
It protects against delivery of 100% nitrogen if pipeline wall lines are cross-connected
It ensures that dialed FiO2 remains at or above 25% when nitrous oxide is used
It regulates intermediate pressure reduction down to 14 psig
It is located downstream of the common gas outlet check valve
It relies on a mechanical or pneumatic linkage between oxygen and nitrous oxide valves
questions.explanation: The hypoxic guard links O2 and N2O flow valves to prevent dialing an FiO2 < 25%. It senses valve mechanics/pressure, NOT gas identity, and cannot protect against crossed pipeline supplies or hypoxic gas tanks.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 45, 46

questions.stem: Why should an oxygen E-cylinder valve be opened slowly after the cylinder is mounted on the hanger yoke?
options: Rapid compression heats gas and can ignite contaminants
Fast opening tears the Bodok seal and defeats the pin index system
Fast opening freezes the valve stem and blocks further flow
Rapid flow overwhelms the first-stage regulator diaphragm
questions.explanation: Opening the valve quickly compresses the gas already sitting in the yoke and regulator almost instantly, and that rapid compression generates heat. In a high-pressure oxygen environment the heat can ignite grease, dust, or seal material. Valve-stem icing is a nitrous oxide phenomenon from liquid vaporization, and the pin index system works through the pins, not the seal.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 18

questions.stem: During direct laryngoscopy with a Miller blade, how is the epiglottis elevated?
options: By direct lift with the blade tip under the epiglottis
Indirectly from the vallecula
By inflating the pharynx
By applying cricoid pressure
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the Miller as a long, straight blade used for direct epiglottic lift, whereas the Macintosh lifts indirectly through the vallecula.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical benefits are achieved by utilizing low fresh gas flows in a circle breathing system? (Select 3)
options: Conservation of exhaled respiratory heat and humidity
Decreased consumption of expensive volatile liquid anesthetics
Complete elimination of all risk of carbon dioxide rebreathing
Reduced atmospheric greenhouse gas pollution and waste emissions
Permanent prevention of Compound A formation with sevoflurane
Decreased resistance to airflow across the endotracheal tube connector
questions.explanation: Low fresh gas flows conserve exhaled moisture and heat, reduce volatile agent consumption, and minimize environmental pollution. However, low flows require effective CO2 absorption and can increase Compound A accumulation with sevoflurane.

questions.stem: What is the primary clinical problem associated with using an uncalibrated copper kettle vaporizer in modern anesthesia practice?
options: Its output is not concentration-calibrated and must be calculated from carrier-gas flow and vapor output
It must be electrically heated to 39 °C before any anesthetic vapor can be produced
It converts volatile agents to carbon monoxide during routine use
It cannot produce saturated anesthetic vapor because it lacks direct gas-liquid contact
questions.explanation: The copper kettle is not a concentration-calibrated vaporizer. A dedicated carrier-gas flow passes through liquid anesthetic and becomes saturated, so the final delivered concentration must be calculated from vapor output and total fresh-gas flow.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 74

questions.stem: In an adult patient undergoing rapid sequence induction, what anatomical landmark is palpated to identify the cricoid cartilage for application of cricoid pressure?
options: The prominent thyroid notch in the anterior midline
The complete cartilaginous ring located directly inferior to the cricothyroid membrane
The hyoid bone situated superior to the thyroid cartilage
The first tracheal ring located directly above the sternal notch
questions.explanation: The cricoid cartilage is the only complete circumferential cartilaginous ring in the upper airway, located immediately inferior to the cricothyroid membrane.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events will produce an acute INCREASE in measured end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2)? (Select 2)
options: Acute pulmonary thromboembolism
Accidental tracheal extubation into the pharynx
Severe systemic hypothermia
Sudden profound cardiac arrest
Deflation of an extremity surgical tourniquet
Intravenous administration of sodium bicarbonate
questions.explanation: Tourniquet release (washout of metabolic acid and CO2) and bicarbonate administration increase CO2 delivery to the lungs, elevating EtCO2. Embolism, extubation, hypothermia, and cardiac arrest decrease EtCO2.

questions.stem: During general anesthesia with mechanical ventilation, an assistant accidentally leans heavily on the patient's chest during exhalation. What capnographic artifact will appear on the monitor?
options: A transient notch or depression mimicking a curare cleft
A prolonged, sloped Phase II upstroke mimicking a shark-fin waveform
An acute elevation of the inspiratory Phase I baseline above 10 mmHg
A sudden loss of all expired waveforms lasting 30 seconds
questions.explanation: External chest compression, surgical pressure, or diaphragmatic twitching can indent the alveolar plateau (Phase III), producing a cleft or notch that mimics a spontaneous breathing effort.

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanism of action of the oxygen fail-safe valve located in the intermediate pressure system?
options: Throttles or shuts off nitrous oxide flow when oxygen supply pressure drops below 25–30 psig
Automatically depressurizes the patient breathing circuit during ventilator disconnection
Opens an auxiliary port to entrain room air whenever minute ventilation falls below 4 L/min
Dumps liquid volatile agent into the scavenging line during electrical failure
questions.explanation: The oxygen fail-safe valve resides in the nitrous oxide line. When oxygen supply pressure drops below 25–30 psig, the valve throttles or stops N2O flow (<20 psig) to prevent delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 34

questions.stem: Which statements describe the sniffing position taught in the airway lecture? Select 2.
options: The occiput is elevated
The head is extended at the atlanto-occipital joint
The head remains fully flexed without extension
Cricoid pressure is required to create the position
The shoulders must always be raised 20 cm
questions.explanation: The lecture defines the sniffing position as elevation of the occiput with extension of the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

questions.stem: What is the full gaseous capacity and full service pressure of a standard Medical Air E-cylinder?
options: 625 L at 1900 psig
1590 L at 745 psig
500 L at 1600 psig
questions.explanation: A full Medical Air E-cylinder contains approximately 625 L of compressed gas at 1900 psig. Oxygen holds 660 L at 1900–2200 psig, and Nitrous Oxide holds 1590 L at 745 psig.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 7, 15

questions.stem: Why does a patient with severe carboxyhemoglobinemia maintain a deceptively normal or near-100% SpO2 reading on a conventional dual-wavelength pulse oximeter?
options: Carboxyhemoglobin absorbs 660 nm red light identically to oxyhemoglobin, misleading the two-wavelength photodetector
Carboxyhemoglobin shifts the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to the right, increasing tissue oxygenation
Carboxyhemoglobin converts reduced hemoglobin into methemoglobin at the peripheral sensor site
Pulse oximeters detect only dissolved arterial oxygen tension (PaO2)
questions.explanation: Conventional pulse oximeters compare light absorption at 660 nm and 940 nm. Carboxyhemoglobin absorbs 660 nm red light almost identically to oxyhemoglobin, causing the oximeter to calculate a falsely high functional saturation.

questions.stem: Which of the following volatile anesthetics have a minimum alveolar concentration (MAC) of less than 2.0% in a 40-year-old patient at 1 atmosphere? (Select 2)
options: Isoflurane
Desflurane
Nitrous oxide
Sevoflurane
Xenon
Cyclopropane
questions.explanation: In a 40-year-old at 1 atm, the MAC of Isoflurane is 1.17% and Sevoflurane is 1.80%. Desflurane is 6.6% and Nitrous Oxide is 104%.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: During general anesthesia with volume-controlled ventilation, an acute rise in peak inspiratory pressure occurs. Plateau pressure remains completely unchanged. After verifying the circuit is clear, what is the next diagnostic step?
options: Pass an in-line suction catheter down the endotracheal tube to rule out secretions or luminal kinking
Perform needle decompression in the second intercostal space for tension pneumothorax
Withdraw the endotracheal tube 3 cm to treat an endobronchial intubation
Replace the carbon dioxide absorbent canister
questions.explanation: An isolated increase in PIP with an unchanged Pplat signals an increase in airway resistance. Passing a suction catheter readily identifies and resolves secretions or tube kinking. Pneumothorax and mainstem intubation alter Pplat.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of potassium hydroxide and sodium hydroxide in wet soda lime?
options: They act as catalytic activators that accelerate the initial neutralization of carbonic acid
They serve as hygroscopic binders that permanently store absorbed carbon dioxide
They absorb carbon monoxide generated by difluoromethyl ethers
They prevent the regeneration of ethyl violet dye
questions.explanation: NaOH and KOH function as catalysts to speed the initial neutralization reaction by forming intermediate carbonates; they are subsequently regenerated when reacting with calcium hydroxide.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical statements regarding second-generation supraglottic airways (e.g., LMA Supreme) are true? (Select 3)
options: They incorporate a dedicated esophageal drain tube to vent gastric contents
They provide absolute, complete protection against pulmonary aspiration
They are constructed from laser-resistant stainless steel for airway surgery
They achieve higher mucosal seal pressures than first-generation LMAs
They can be used to facilitate passage of an orogastric tube
They bypass the vocal cords to enter the subglottic trachea
questions.explanation: The textbook describes the ProSeal and Supreme as second-generation supraglottic devices with gastric access or drainage features and improved airway seals compared with the LMA Classic. The gastric channel can also permit passage of a gastric tube.

questions.stem: What is the pipeline supply pressure delivered from hospital central gas systems to an anesthesia workstation?
options: 14 to 16 psig
25 to 30 psig
50 to 55 psig
75 to 85 psig
questions.explanation: Normal hospital pipeline supply pressure for oxygen, nitrous oxide, and medical air is maintained at approximately 50 to 55 psig.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 33

questions.stem: What is the primary risk of using more than one Bodok seal washer when mounting an E-cylinder onto an anesthesia machine yoke?
options: The extra thickness spaces the cylinder post away from the index pins, defeating the Pin Index Safety System
The check valve becomes permanently jammed open, causing rapid cylinder exhaustion
The Bourdon pressure gauge will falsely register zero pressure
The frangible safety disc will rupture upon opening the valve
questions.explanation: Stacking two or more washers increases the space between the cylinder valve and the yoke face, allowing the post to sit clear of the index pins and defeating the PISS safety mechanism.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 10, 20

questions.stem: Which of the following methods are recommended to minimize waste anesthetic gas exposure in the operating room? (Select 2)
options: Routinely administering 100% nitrous oxide via unsealed face mask
Turning off fresh gas flows or using 'pause flow' during intubation and extubation
Ensuring active waste gas scavenging is connected and functional for all cases
Filling vaporizers while the concentration dial remains turned on
Venting active scavenging lines directly into the OR floor exhaust
Allowing deeply anesthetized patients to breathe spontaneously into room air
questions.explanation: 94% to 99% of OR contamination stems from provider technique. Pausing fresh gas flows during intubation/disconnections and utilizing active scavenging reduce ambient trace gases by 90%.

questions.stem: During a craniotomy under general anesthesia, what capnographic tracing abnormality appears when a patient attempts to breathe spontaneously against the ventilator?
options: A downward dip or notch (curare cleft) in the Phase III alveolar plateau
A prolonged Phase II upstroke with loss of the alpha angle
An acute elevation of the Phase I baseline above 5 mmHg
Sawtooth oscillations along the Phase IV downstroke
questions.explanation: A curare cleft is an inspiratory notch in Phase III caused by patient spontaneous diaphragmatic effort as neuromuscular block wanes.

questions.stem: What is the critical temperature of Oxygen?
questions.explanation: The critical temperature of oxygen is -118.6°C. Above this temperature, oxygen can only exist in a gaseous state regardless of applied pressure.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 11

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical signs confirm successful endotracheal intubation? (Select 3)
options: Immediate elevation of the inspiratory baseline above 10 mmHg
Continuous, stable EtCO2 waveforms across at least three consecutive breaths
Equal, bilateral thoracic expansion and breath sounds on auscultation
Continuous condensation (fogging) in the tracheal tube during exhalation
A sudden drop in peak inspiratory pressure below 5 cmH2O
Loss of the dicrotic notch on the radial arterial line
questions.explanation: ETT placement is confirmed by clinical assessment (bilateral breath sounds, chest expansion, exhaled tube condensation) and objective continuous EtCO2 across at least 3 consecutive breaths.

questions.stem: What physical property of a gas governs its flow through a Thorpe tube flowmeter at LOW flow rates?
options: Gas viscosity
Gas density
Vapor pressure
Critical temperature
questions.explanation: At low flow rates, the annular space between the float and the tapered tube is tubular, resulting in laminar flow governed primarily by gas viscosity (Poiseuille's law). High flow is turbulent and density-dependent.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 43

questions.stem: How should the cuff of a laser-resistant endotracheal tube be filled according to the airway lecture?
options: With saline or water plus dye
With nitrous oxide
With air only
With volatile anesthetic
questions.explanation: The lecture states that laser-resistant tube cuffs are not themselves laser resistant and should be filled with saline or water and dye.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding an open-reservoir scavenging interface are true? (Select 2)
options: It requires spring-loaded positive-pressure pop-off valves
It is completely valveless
It requires spring-loaded negative-pressure pop-in valves
It contains a dedicated waste gas reservoir bag
It must be connected exclusively to passive through-the-wall disposal ducts
It contains relief ports open to the ambient atmosphere
questions.explanation: An open scavenging interface is valveless and relies on ports open to the atmosphere to prevent positive or negative pressure buildup. Closed interfaces use dedicated reservoir bags and spring-loaded pop-off/pop-in valves.

questions.stem: What is the PISS pin configuration for Nitrous Oxide?
options: Positions 1 and 5
Positions 2 and 5
Positions 3 and 5
Positions 1 and 6
questions.explanation: Nitrous Oxide uses pin positions 3 and 5 under the Pin Index Safety System.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 18

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanism of heat loss in a patient undergoing general anesthesia in an ambient operating room?
options: Radiation
Convection
Conduction
Evaporation
questions.explanation: Radiation (transfer of infrared heat energy from the warm body to cool operating room walls and environment) represents the largest source of heat loss in the surgical patient.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical conditions cause an increase in both peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) and plateau pressure (Pplat) simultaneously? (Select 3)
options: Severe endotracheal tube kinking
Peritoneal gas insufflation
Tracheal secretions
Endobronchial mainstem intubation
Acute pulmonary edema
Increased inspiratory gas flow rate
questions.explanation: Simultaneous elevation of PIP and Pplat reflects decreased static and dynamic compliance (e.g., peritoneal insufflation, mainstem intubation, pulmonary edema). Tube kinking, secretions, and high flow elevate PIP alone.

questions.stem: What is the vapor pressure of Sevoflurane at 20°C?
options: 160 mmHg
240 mmHg
244 mmHg
669 mmHg
questions.explanation: At 20°C, the saturated vapor pressure of Sevoflurane is 160 mmHg. Isoflurane is 240 mmHg, Halothane is 244 mmHg, and Desflurane is 669 mmHg.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: What NIOSH-recommended occupational exposure limit does the lecture give for a halogenated anesthetic agent used alone?
options: 0.5 ppm
2 ppm
10 ppm
25 ppm
questions.explanation: The lecture gives a recommended exposure limit of 2 ppm for a halogenated anesthetic agent used alone. Nitrous oxide used as the sole anesthetic is listed at 25 ppm TWA.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors promote the 'pumping effect' in an older variable bypass vaporizer lacking an outlet check valve? (Select 2)
options: High continuous fresh gas flows (>10 L/min)
Maintaining an overfilled liquid agent sump
Intermittent positive-pressure ventilation
Operating the machine at high altitudes
Using an open-reservoir scavenging interface
Activation of the oxygen flush valve
questions.explanation: The pumping effect is caused by intermittent backpressure fluctuations (from positive-pressure ventilation or depressing the O2 flush valve) compressing gas back into the vaporizing chamber, transiently increasing delivered output.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 72

questions.stem: What is the flow rate and delivery pressure of the oxygen flush valve on an anesthesia workstation?
options: 10–15 L/min at 15 psig
20–30 L/min at 30 psig
35–75 L/min at 40–50 psig
80–100 L/min at 75 psig
questions.explanation: The oxygen flush valve delivers unmetered pure O2 directly to the common gas outlet at a rate of 35–75 L/min at intermediate pressure (40–50 psig), completely bypassing flowmeters and vaporizers.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 36

questions.stem: On an invasive arterial blood pressure tracing, what cardiac event corresponds to the dicrotic notch?
options: Opening of the aortic valve
Closure of the aortic valve
Closure of the mitral valve
Peak isovolumetric ventricular contraction
questions.explanation: The dicrotic notch marks the closure of the aortic valve and signifies the transition from ventricular systole to diastole.

questions.stem: Which statements about an oropharyngeal airway are supported by the airway lecture? Select 3.
options: Its concave surface faces caudally
It lifts the tongue
It can improve bag-mask ventilation seal in edentulous patients
Awake patients tolerate it better than a nasopharyngeal airway
Its most common complication is epistaxis
It lies in the hypopharynx
questions.explanation: The airway lecture describes the OPA as having a caudally facing concave surface, lifting the tongue, and improving bag-mask ventilation seal in edentulous patients. The awake-tolerance, epistaxis, and hypopharyngeal-position statements belong to the NPA.

questions.stem: What is the full gaseous capacity and full service pressure of a standard Oxygen E-cylinder?
options: 1590 L at 745 psig
625 L at 1900 psig
500 L at 1600 psig
questions.explanation: A standard medical oxygen E-cylinder contains ~660 L (range 625–700 L) at a full service pressure of 1900–2200 psig.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 7, 12

questions.stem: Which single ECG lead is the most sensitive for detecting perioperative myocardial ischemia in vascular surgery patients?
options: Lead II
Lead V3
Lead V5
Lead aVF
questions.explanation: According to Landesberg et al., lead V3 is the single most sensitive lead for ischemia detection (86.8%), followed by V4 (78.9%) and V5 (65.8%). Lead II is preferred for rhythm analysis.

questions.stem: Which of the following components are located within the low-pressure system of an anesthesia machine? (Select 2)
options: Auxiliary oxygen flowmeter
Oxygen fail-safe valve
First-stage pressure regulator
Bourdon cylinder pressure gauge
Flowmeter tubes
Concentration-calibrated vaporizers
questions.explanation: The low-pressure system extends from downstream of the flow control needle valves to the common gas outlet, containing flowmeters, vaporizers, pressure relief valves, and outlet check valves. Regulators and gauges belong to high/intermediate systems.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 38, 39

questions.stem: During maintenance of general anesthesia, the capnography monitor displays the classic 'shark-fin' waveform. What clinical pathology is present?
options: Expiratory airflow obstruction or severe bronchospasm
Rebreathing of carbon dioxide from exhausted absorbent
Spontaneous diaphragmatic inspiratory effort
Cardiac oscillations transmitted from ventricular systole
questions.explanation: Airflow obstruction and bronchospasm slow expiratory alveolar emptying, producing a prolonged Phase II upstroke and an upwardly tilted Phase III plateau known as the classic 'shark-fin' waveform.

questions.stem: Despite three minutes of preoxygenation, a morbidly obese patient desaturates within a minute of apnea. What best explains this?
options: Increased dead space limits alveolar oxygen loading
Smaller FRC reserve plus higher oxygen consumption
A thickened alveolar membrane slows oxygen diffusion
Reduced hemoglobin affinity shifts the curve rightward
questions.explanation: The functional residual capacity is the oxygen reservoir during apnea, and obesity shrinks it, especially supine and after induction. Obese patients also consume more oxygen, so the smaller store is used up faster. This is why ramped, head-up preoxygenation and apneic oxygenation are emphasized in obesity.

questions.stem: Which of the following items are verified under the 'M' (Machine) component of the pre-induction MS MAID room setup? (Select 3)
options: Presence of a rigid stylet within the primary ETT
Verification of IV fluid warmer priming
Baseline 12-lead ECG strip printing
Completed full machine pre-use checkout
Presence of an auxiliary backup oxygen cylinder
Emergency bag-valve-mask resuscitation device available and functional
questions.explanation: Under MS MAID, 'M' stands for Machine: performing a complete pre-use checkout, verifying the presence of an emergency resuscitation bag-valve-mask, and confirming a backup O2 cylinder is present and functional.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the interlock safety mechanism on variable bypass vaporizers?
options: Ensures that only one vaporizer can be turned on at any given time
Prevents positive backpressure from entering the vaporizer sump
Shuts off fresh gas flow when agent volume falls below 20 mL
Locks the vaporizer to the manifold to prevent tipping leaks
questions.explanation: The interlock mechanism physically locks adjacent vaporizer dials, ensuring that only one vaporizer can be turned on at a time and preventing concurrent administration of multiple volatile agents.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 59, 73

questions.stem: What mesh size is precisely manufactured for soda lime granules to balance CO2 absorption surface area against airflow resistance?
options: 1 to 2 mesh
4 to 8 mesh
12 to 16 mesh
20 to 24 mesh
questions.explanation: Soda lime granules are sized 4 to 8 mesh to optimize surface area for rapid gas diffusion while preventing high resistance to ventilation within the breathing circuit.

questions.stem: Which two wavelengths of light are emitted by conventional dual-wavelength pulse oximeters to differentiate oxyhemoglobin from deoxyhemoglobin? (Select 2)
options: 660 nm (red light)
540 nm (green light)
780 nm (infrared light)
940 nm (near-infrared light)
1020 nm (far-infrared light)
1280 nm (optical light)
questions.explanation: Conventional pulse oximeters utilize light-emitting diodes at 660 nm (red light, absorbed primarily by deoxyhemoglobin) and 940 nm (near-infrared light, absorbed primarily by oxyhemoglobin).

questions.stem: During carbon dioxide absorption by wet soda lime, what happens after sodium and potassium carbonates are formed?
options: They react with calcium hydroxide to form calcium carbonate and regenerate the hydroxide catalysts
They permanently store carbon dioxide and remain unchanged until the canister is discarded
They react with ethyl violet to prevent the indicator dye from changing color
They decompose volatile anesthetics into carbon monoxide as part of normal carbon dioxide absorption
questions.explanation: Sodium and potassium hydroxide first form intermediate carbonates. Those carbonates then react with calcium hydroxide to form calcium carbonate while regenerating the hydroxide catalysts.

questions.stem: Core temperature drops 1.2°C in the first hour after induction despite a warm room. What is the main mechanism?
options: Radiant heat loss to the operating room walls
Evaporative loss from dry anesthetic gases
Core-to-periphery heat redistribution
Conductive loss to the operating table
questions.explanation: Anesthetics cause peripheral vasodilation and inhibit thermoregulatory vasoconstriction, so heat moves from the warm core into the cooler arms and legs. This phase 1 redistribution accounts for most of the early core drop. Radiation is the largest ongoing loss to the room, but it does not explain a rapid first-hour fall.

questions.stem: During laparoscopy, EtCO2 keeps climbing despite a 50% increase in minute ventilation, and crepitus appears over the chest wall. What is the most likely cause?
options: Subcutaneous CO2 emphysema from insufflation
Malignant hyperthermia triggered by the volatile agent
Exhausted absorbent causing CO2 rebreathing
Endobronchial migration of the tracheal tube
questions.explanation: Insufflated CO2 that tracks into the subcutaneous tissues provides a large absorptive surface, so EtCO2 can keep rising even as ventilation increases, and crepitus confirms the diagnosis. Malignant hyperthermia would bring tachycardia, rigidity, and temperature change rather than crepitus. Rebreathing raises the inspired baseline, and endobronchial intubation raises airway pressure and lowers SpO2.

questions.stem: Where is the carbon dioxide absorber almost invariably placed in the circle system described in the lecture?
options: In the inspiratory limb on the bag side
In the expiratory limb on the patient side of the expiratory valve
Directly at the patient Y-piece connection
Downstream of the scavenging interface
questions.explanation: The lecture states that the absorber may be placed in any quadrant but is almost invariably placed in the inspiratory limb on the bag side so apparatus resistance can be overcome during assisted or controlled ventilation.

questions.stem: What is the blood:gas partition coefficient of Desflurane at 37°C?
questions.explanation: The blood:gas partition coefficient of Desflurane is 0.42 (Sevoflurane is 0.65, Isoflurane is 1.46, and Halothane is 2.50).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: Which of the following design features are incorporated into mechanical flowmeters on an anesthesia workstation to prevent delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture? (Select 2)
options: Nitrous oxide is plumbed into an independent auxiliary manifold
The oxygen flow control knob is physically larger and fluted
Oxygen is always positioned last in the manifold sequence closest to the outlet
Thorpe tubes have a uniform, non-tapered internal diameter
Flow control valves automatically increase fresh gas flow during apnea
Check valves prevent volatile agent from entering the glass tubes
questions.explanation: To prevent hypoxia, the O2 knob is uniquely tactile (larger, fluted) and O2 is positioned furthest downstream (last on the right) so any upstream leaks will leak other gases rather than oxygen.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 40, 41

questions.stem: For what type of difficult laryngoscopic view does the textbook describe use of an Eschmann introducer?
options: Cormack-Lehane grade IIb or III
Only grade I
Only when the glottis is fully visible
Only after a surgical airway
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia describes the Eschmann introducer as useful when the glottic opening is difficult to visualize, including Cormack-Lehane grade IIb or III views.

questions.stem: How much carbon dioxide can be absorbed by 100 g of fresh soda lime absorbent?
options: Approximately 5 L
Approximately 12 L
Approximately 26 L
Approximately 50 L
questions.explanation: Soda lime absorbs approximately 19% of its weight in carbon dioxide; therefore, 100 g of soda lime absorbs approximately 26 L of CO2.

questions.stem: From the first breath of the case, the capnogram baseline sits at 4 mmHg. The absorbent is fresh and both unidirectional valves move normally. What should be done next?
options: Replace the CO2 absorbent canister
Replace the expiratory valve disk
Re-zero the capnograph to room air
Raise fresh gas flow above minute ventilation
questions.explanation: A raised baseline that is present from the very first breath, with fresh absorbent and normal valve movement, points to the analyzer rather than true rebreathing. Water in the sample cell or a drifted zero offsets every reading, and re-zeroing against room air corrects it. Changing the canister or valve disk treats rebreathing that the other findings have already ruled out.

questions.stem: Which anatomical structures form the superior and inferior boundaries of the cricothyroid membrane during an emergency surgical airway?
options: Thyroid cartilage superiorly and cricoid cartilage inferiorly
Hyoid bone superiorly and thyroid cartilage inferiorly
Cricoid cartilage superiorly and first tracheal ring inferiorly
Corniculate cartilage superiorly and arytenoid cartilage inferiorly
questions.explanation: The cricothyroid membrane is bounded superiorly by the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage and inferiorly by the superior border of the cricoid cartilage.

questions.stem: What is the primary consequence of applying an excessively large blood pressure cuff to an adult patient's extremity?
options: Blood pressure readings will be falsely low
Blood pressure readings will be falsely elevated
Inability to detect cardiac dysrhythmias
Blunting of the arterial dicrotic notch
questions.explanation: A cuff that is too large or wide transmits pressure over an excessively broad area, occluding the artery at lower cuff pressures and yielding falsely low blood pressure readings.

questions.stem: Which dyshemoglobin can cause a falsely elevated reading on a conventional two-wavelength pulse oximeter?
options: Carboxyhemoglobin
Methemoglobin
Deoxyhemoglobin
Fetal hemoglobin
questions.explanation: Carboxyhemoglobin can cause a conventional two-wavelength pulse oximeter to overestimate oxygen saturation. Oxyhemoglobin is the normal species being measured and should not be keyed as a deceptive dyshemoglobin.

questions.stem: What is the boiling point of Desflurane at 1 atmosphere of pressure?
questions.explanation: At 1 atmosphere, Desflurane boils at 22.8°C (Isoflurane boils at 48.5°C, Halothane at 50.2°C, and Sevoflurane at 58.6°C).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: During CPR on a patient with a confirmed tracheal tube, EtCO2 stays near 8 mmHg. What is the BEST first response?
options: Increase the ventilation rate to clear more CO2
Give sodium bicarbonate to raise the EtCO2 value
Remove the tube and reintubate under direct vision
Improve compressions or switch compressors
questions.explanation: With tube position already confirmed, EtCO2 during CPR mainly reflects how much blood the compressions push through the lungs. A value below about 10 mmHg points to inadequate compressions, so the fix is better compressions. Faster ventilation lowers EtCO2 further, and bicarbonate produces a misleading CO2 rise without improving perfusion.

questions.stem: [REINFORCEMENT: Q201] Isoflurane is delivered at a dialed concentration of 1.5% with a fresh gas flow of 2 L/min. Using the clinical formula: Total anesthetic used (mL/hr) = Vol % x FGF (L/min) x 3, how many milliliters of liquid isoflurane will be consumed during a 4-hour operation?
options: 18 mL
27 mL
36 mL
54 mL
questions.explanation: Using the formula: Total anesthetic used (mL/hr) = 1.5 (%) x 2 (L/min) x 3 = 9 mL/hr. Over a 4-hour surgical case: 9 mL/hr x 4 hr = 36 mL.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 52

questions.stem: Examine the variable-orifice Thorpe tube flowmeter schematic below. During administration of high fresh gas flows, what physical law and gas property dictate flow through the annular opening?
options: Poiseuille's law, governed primarily by gas viscosity
Graham's law / orifice flow, governed primarily by gas density
Fick's law, governed primarily by concentration gradients
Boyle's law, governed primarily by ambient temperature
questions.explanation: At high flow rates, the annular space between the float and the tapered tube wall is wide and orifice-shaped, creating turbulent flow governed by gas density (Graham's law). At low flow rates, the narrow tubular gap creates laminar flow governed by viscosity (Poiseuille's law).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 43
