questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events will produce an acute DECREASE in measured end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2)? (Select 3)
options: Accidental tracheal extubation into the pharynx
Acute hypoventilation in a spontaneously breathing patient
Chemical exhaustion of carbon dioxide absorbent granules
Sudden profound hypovolemic shock
Intravenous administration of sodium bicarbonate
Severe accidental hypothermia with core temperature < 32°C
questions.explanation: Decreased EtCO2 occurs with airway displacement/extubation, decreased pulmonary blood flow/perfusion (hypovolemia/shock), or decreased metabolic CO2 production (hypothermia). Hypoventilation, exhausted absorbent, and bicarbonate increase EtCO2.

questions.stem: During a general anesthetic case with an endotracheal tube in place, you note a triangular, slanted downward drop in the capnogram alveolar plateau (Phase III). What is the most probable cause?
options: A leak within the breathing circuit or an underinflated endotracheal tube cuff
Severe acute bronchospasm causing complete loss of the alpha angle
Early manifestation of a malignant hyperthermia crisis
Patient spontaneous diaphragmatic effort as muscle relaxation wanes
questions.explanation: A slanted, triangular capnographic waveform is characteristic of a leak in the breathing circuit or an unsealed/underinflated endotracheal tube cuff, allowing fresh air entrainment and loss of alveolar plateau pressure.

questions.stem: What is the critical temperature of Oxygen, above which it cannot be liquefied by pressure alone?
questions.explanation: The critical temperature of oxygen is -118.6°C. Above this temperature, oxygen behaves strictly as a gas regardless of applied pressure. -183°C is its boiling point, +31.0°C is CO2, and +36.4°C is N2O.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 11

questions.stem: Which of the following monitoring modalities are specifically required by ASA and AANA basic monitoring standards during the conduct of monitored anesthesia care (MAC)? (Select 2)
options: Continuous display of the electroencephalographic Bispectral Index (BIS)
Quantitative monitoring of neuromuscular train-of-four ratio at the adductor pollicis
Arterial blood pressure and heart rate determined and evaluated at least every five minutes
Invasive radial arterial line catheterization for all ASA III patients
Continuous distal esophageal core temperature monitoring
Continual evaluation of the adequacy of ventilation via qualitative clinical signs and expired carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Standards mandate arterial blood pressure and heart rate evaluated at least every 5 minutes and continual evaluation of ventilation (clinical signs and expired CO2) during MAC. BIS, invasive A-lines, and quantitative TOF are not mandatory for all MAC cases.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the second-stage pressure regulator on an anesthesia machine?
options: It further reduces intermediate gas pressure and dampens supply-pressure fluctuations before the flow-control system
It reduces full cylinder pressure directly from about 2,200 psig to atmospheric pressure
It regulates active scavenging suction at the waste-gas interface
It prevents reverse flow from the breathing circuit into the vaporizer
questions.explanation: The second-stage regulator further reduces gas pressure within the intermediate-pressure system and smooths fluctuations before gas reaches sensitive downstream components. The lecture lists approximately 14–16 psig for oxygen and 26–38 psig for nitrous oxide.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 33

questions.stem: [REINFORCEMENT: Q208] A central hospital bulk liquid oxygen tank stores oxygen in vacuum-insulated cryogenic vessels at -160°C. Which component of the central piping system warms the evaporating cryogenic liquid into room-temperature gas before it reaches the hospital pressure regulator?
options: The superheater and vaporizer heat-exchanger coils
The intermediate second-stage reducing valve
The low-pressure negative-pressure relief valve
The zone shut-off isolation manifold
questions.explanation: Bulk liquid O2 is stored at approximately -160°C. As liquid is drawn from the vessel, it passes through ambient vaporizer coils and superheater tubing that absorb environmental heat, warming the gas to room temperature before distribution at 50–55 psig.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 32

questions.stem: Which direct laryngoscopy blade design requires directly trapping and elevating the posterior surface of the epiglottis to expose the vocal cords?
options: Macintosh blade
Miller blade
Phillips blade
Guedel blade
questions.explanation: The straight Miller blade is advanced underneath the epiglottis, directly trapping and lifting its posterior surface. The curved Macintosh blade lifts the epiglottis indirectly from within the vallecula.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical conditions are recognized causes of decreased pulmonary compliance, resulting in a simultaneous parallel increase in both peak inspiratory pressure (PIP) and plateau pressure (Pplat)? (Select 3)
options: Airway secretions partially obstructing the trachea
Acute tension pneumothorax
Mainstem endobronchial intubation
Acute severe bronchospasm
Peritoneal carbon dioxide insufflation during laparoscopy
Endotracheal tube kinking by the surgical drape
questions.explanation: Simultaneous elevation of PIP and Pplat reflects decreased pulmonary compliance (e.g., tension pneumothorax, mainstem intubation, peritoneal insufflation, pulmonary edema). Secretions, bronchospasm, and tube kinking increase airway resistance, elevating PIP alone.

questions.stem: During maintenance of general anesthesia, an acute rise in exhaled nitrogen is detected on the multi-gas analyzer alongside a sudden decrease in end-tidal CO2. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Venous air embolism
Chemical exhaustion of soda lime absorbent
Accidental extubation into the esophagus
Acute malignant hyperthermia crisis
questions.explanation: Entrainment of ambient room air into the venous circulation (venous air embolism) introduces nitrogen into the pulmonary vasculature, manifesting as an acute appearance of exhaled nitrogen on the gas monitor and a fall in EtCO2 from pulmonary hypoperfusion.

questions.stem: What is the PISS pin configuration for a Medical Air E-cylinder?
options: Positions 1 and 5
Positions 2 and 5
Positions 3 and 5
Positions 1 and 6
questions.explanation: Medical Air uses pin positions 1 and 5 under the Pin Index Safety System. Oxygen is 2 and 5; Nitrous Oxide is 3 and 5.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 18

questions.stem: Which of the following volatile anesthetics undergo greater than 1.0% hepatic metabolism in the human body? (Select 2)
options: Isoflurane
Desflurane
Nitrous oxide
Xenon
Halothane
Sevoflurane
questions.explanation: Halothane undergoes 15% to 40% metabolism and Sevoflurane undergoes 2% to 5% metabolism. In contrast, Isoflurane is ~0.2%, Desflurane is <0.05%, and Nitrous Oxide undergoes zero metabolism.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanism of intraoperative heat loss in a patient undergoing general anesthesia in an ambient operating room?
options: Radiation
Convection
Conduction
Evaporation
questions.explanation: Radiation (transfer of infrared heat energy from the warm patient to cooler room surfaces) represents the largest contributor to intraoperative heat loss.

questions.stem: What mesh size is precisely manufactured for soda lime granules to balance carbon dioxide absorption surface area against resistance to airflow?
options: 1 to 2 mesh
4 to 8 mesh
12 to 16 mesh
20 to 24 mesh
questions.explanation: Soda lime granules are sized 4 to 8 mesh to optimize surface area for rapid gas diffusion while preventing high resistance to ventilation within the breathing circuit.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical factors will shift the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to the RIGHT, facilitating oxygen offloading to peripheral tissues? (Select 3)
options: Severe accidental hypothermia
Systemic metabolic or respiratory acidosis (decreased pH)
Systemic alkalosis (increased pH)
Elevated carbon dioxide tension (hypercapnia)
Depleted levels of erythrocyte 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG)
Hyperthermia (elevated body temperature)
questions.explanation: A right shift of the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve reduces hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, enhancing tissue delivery. This occurs with acidosis, hypercapnia, hyperthermia, and increased 2,3-DPG. Alkalosis, hypothermia, and low 2,3-DPG cause a left shift.

questions.stem: Which finding is classically associated with tracheal rather than esophageal passage of an Eschmann introducer?
options: Tactile clicks as the angled tip passes over tracheal rings
Completely smooth advancement without tactile feedback
Immediate resistance at the oropharynx before the glottis
Loss of resistance at the upper esophageal sphincter
questions.explanation: When a bougie is advanced into the trachea, the angled tip may produce palpable clicks as it passes over tracheal rings and may eventually meet distal hold-up. Smooth advancement without these findings is more consistent with esophageal passage.

questions.stem: What is the primary clinical utility of an auxiliary oxygen flowmeter mounted on an anesthesia workstation?
options: Provides supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula or mask without disrupting the main breathing circuit
Supplies driving gas to the pneumatic ventilator bellows during mechanical cycling
Flushes volatile anesthetic vapors from the low-pressure circuit at emergence
Serves as a backup pressure regulator in the event of pipeline failure
questions.explanation: The auxiliary O2 flowmeter provides pure oxygen (up to ~10 L/min) from the machine's pipeline connection for supplemental devices (cannula, face mask, self-inflating bag) without requiring disconnection or altering the main breathing circuit.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 44

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics describe an open-reservoir waste gas scavenging interface? (Select 2)
options: It is completely valveless
It requires spring-loaded positive-pressure pop-off valves
It requires a negative-pressure relief pop-in valve
It utilizes relief ports open to the ambient operating room atmosphere
It contains a dedicated waste gas reservoir bag
It must be connected exclusively to passive through-the-wall conduits
questions.explanation: An open scavenging interface is valveless and relies on ports open to the atmosphere to prevent positive or negative pressure buildup. Closed interfaces use dedicated reservoir bags and spring-loaded pop-off/pop-in safety valves.

questions.stem: [REINFORCEMENT: Q220] A nitrous oxide E-cylinder is in continuous use. The cylinder Bourdon gauge has read 745 psig for two hours, but then suddenly begins a rapid, linear drop to 400 psig. What physical change within the cylinder accounts for this sudden pressure drop?
options: All liquid nitrous oxide has fully vaporized, leaving approximately 253 L of gas remaining
The cylinder temperature has dropped below its critical temperature of -88.5°C
The first-stage regulator has failed, venting gas into the high-pressure relief valve
Nitrous oxide has condensed into solid state crystals along the internal cylinder walls
questions.explanation: In an N2O cylinder, the Bourdon gauge remains at 745 psig (at 20°C) as long as liquid N2O remains to generate saturated vapor. Once all liquid has vaporized, only gaseous N2O remains (~253 L or ~16% of a full 1590 L tank), and pressure subsequently drops linearly with gas consumption.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 14

questions.stem: What is the normal gradient between arterial carbon dioxide tension (PaCO2) and end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) in healthy supine patients under general anesthesia?
options: 0 mmHg
2 to 5 mmHg
10 to 15 mmHg
20 to 25 mmHg
questions.explanation: In healthy supine patients under general anesthesia, alveolar dead space creates a normal PaCO2–EtCO2 gradient of approximately 2 to 5 mmHg (EtCO2 being slightly lower than PaCO2).

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical events will produce an acute INCREASE in measured end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2)? (Select 3)
options: Sudden massive pulmonary thromboembolism
Severe accidental hypothermia with core temperature < 32°C
Intravenous administration of sodium bicarbonate
Release of an extremity surgical tourniquet
Acute cardiac arrest with cessation of pulmonary blood flow
Acute hypoventilation in a spontaneously breathing patient
questions.explanation: Increased EtCO2 results from increased metabolic production, increased delivery to the lungs (bicarbonate bolus, tourniquet release), or decreased alveolar elimination (hypoventilation). Pulmonary embolism, hypothermia, and cardiac arrest decrease EtCO2.

questions.stem: An operating room routinely uses nitrous oxide together with a halogenated volatile anesthetic. Which measured halogenated anesthetic concentration reaches the NIOSH recommended occupational exposure limit for this combined-use setting?
options: 0.25 ppm
0.5 ppm
2 ppm
25 ppm
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia states that the advisory exposure limit for a halogenated anesthetic is reduced to 0.5 ppm when it is used with nitrous oxide; nitrous oxide is limited to 25 ppm as an 8-hour time-weighted average.

questions.stem: What is the intended anatomical effect of cricoid pressure during rapid-sequence induction?
options: Posterior displacement of the cricoid cartilage against the cervical vertebrae to reduce regurgitation risk
Anterior displacement of the thyroid cartilage to open the esophagus
Direct compression of the trachea to stop ventilation
Rotation of the larynx to expose the glottis
questions.explanation: The textbook describes cricoid pressure as posterior displacement of the cricoid cartilage against the cervical vertebrae with the intent of reducing regurgitation and aspiration risk. It does not require a C6-specific explanation.

questions.stem: Which of the following actions trigger the 'pumping effect' in an older variable bypass vaporizer lacking an outlet check valve? (Select 2)
options: Continuous use of high fresh gas flows (>10 L/min)
Intermittent positive-pressure ventilation
Activation of the oxygen flush valve
Maintaining an overfilled liquid agent sump
Operating the machine at high altitudes
Using an open-reservoir scavenging interface
questions.explanation: The pumping effect is caused by rapid backpressure fluctuations (from positive-pressure ventilation or depressing the O2 flush valve) compressing gas back into the vaporizing chamber, transiently increasing delivered output.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 72

questions.stem: What is the blood:gas partition coefficient of Halothane at 37°C?
questions.explanation: The blood:gas partition coefficient of Halothane is 2.50 (Isoflurane is 1.46, Sevoflurane is 0.65, and Desflurane is 0.42).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: What capnographic finding confirms carbon dioxide rebreathing during general anesthesia?
options: Failure of the Phase I baseline to return to zero (elevated baseline above 0 mmHg)
A prolonged, sloped Phase II upstroke with loss of the alpha angle
A deep notch during the latter third of Phase III
An acute drop in peak EtCO2 below 15 mmHg
questions.explanation: CO2 rebreathing is defined by an elevated Phase I baseline (>0 mmHg). During inspiration, CO2-containing gas is re-inspired, commonly caused by exhausted absorbent or incompetent unidirectional valves.

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical factors can lead to an elevated baseline on the capnography waveform during general anesthesia? (Select 3)
options: Chemical exhaustion of wet soda lime absorbent
Incompetent expiratory unidirectional breathing circuit valve
Incompetent inspiratory unidirectional breathing circuit valve
Excessive fresh gas flow rates exceeding 12 L/min
Acute hypothermia with core temperature < 34°C
Partial obstruction of the endotracheal tube lumen
questions.explanation: An elevated baseline indicates rebreathing of CO2. Causes include exhausted absorbent, incompetent inspiratory or expiratory valves, and inadequate fresh gas flow in semi-closed circuits. High flows prevent rebreathing; hypothermia and obstruction alter waveform height or slope.

questions.stem: What is the critical temperature of Carbon Dioxide?
questions.explanation: The critical temperature of CO2 is +31.0°C. Above this temperature, CO2 behaves strictly as a gas regardless of applied pressure. Oxygen is -118.6°C and Nitrous Oxide is +36.4°C.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 7, 11, 14

questions.stem: Where is the carbon dioxide absorbent canister located within a standard circle breathing circuit?
options: In the inspiratory limb on the bag side
In the expiratory limb on the patient side of the expiratory valve
Directly at the patient Y-piece connection
Downstream of the scavenging interface
questions.explanation: The CO2 absorber is placed in the inspiratory limb on the bag side so that apparatus resistance to inspiration is readily overcome by manual assisted or mechanical controlled ventilation.

questions.stem: During a long case using high nitrous oxide flow from an E-cylinder, frost forms on the cylinder and the gauge drops below 745 psig, then recovers after flow stops. Why?
options: The first-stage regulator is failing under the high flow
The cylinder is nearly empty and is refilling from the yoke
Gas is leaking past the Bodok seal and chilling the valve
Vaporizing liquid N2O cools it and lowers its vapor pressure
questions.explanation: A nitrous oxide cylinder holds liquid in equilibrium with gas, and the gauge reads the liquid's vapor pressure. Rapid withdrawal makes liquid vaporize faster, which absorbs heat and cools the remaining liquid, lowering its vapor pressure and the gauge reading; frost forms on the outside. When flow stops, the liquid rewarms and pressure returns. A truly empty cylinder would not recover.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 14

questions.stem: What is the boiling point of Isoflurane at 1 atmosphere of pressure?
questions.explanation: At 1 atmosphere, Isoflurane boils at 48.5°C (Desflurane boils at 22.8°C, Halothane at 50.2°C, and Sevoflurane at 58.6°C).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: A heliox mixture runs through a flowmeter calibrated for oxygen at a high flow rate. How does the actual flow compare with the indicated flow?
options: Lower, because heliox has a lower viscosity than oxygen
The same, because the tapered tube compensates for gas type
Higher, because heliox has a lower density than oxygen
The same, because viscosity and density effects cancel out
questions.explanation: At high flows the annular gap around the float is wide and flow is turbulent, so density governs it. Heliox is much less dense than oxygen, so more gas passes for a given float position and the meter under-reads the true flow. Viscosity matters at low, laminar flows, which is why flowmeters are gas-specific.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 43

questions.stem: Which of the following clinical signs indicate successful endotracheal intubation? (Select 3)
options: Presence of stable, continuous EtCO2 waveforms across at least three consecutive breaths
Bilateral chest excursion and equal breath sounds on auscultation
An immediate drop in plateau pressure below 5 cmH2O
Absence of all heart sound oscillations on the pulse plethysmograph
Persistent elevated baseline on the capnography monitor
Continuous condensation (fogging) in the tracheal tube during exhalation
questions.explanation: Verification of ETT placement requires clinical assessment (bilateral breath sounds, chest expansion, exhaled condensation) and objective confirmation with continuous EtCO2 across at least 3 consecutive breaths.

questions.stem: Which ventilator design uses no drive gas, so during a pipeline failure the cylinder supplies only fresh gas?
options: An ascending pneumatic bellows ventilator
A descending pneumatic bellows ventilator
An electrically driven piston ventilator
A pneumatic ventilator run on medical air
questions.explanation: A piston ventilator is moved by an electric motor, so the only oxygen it consumes is the fresh gas flow. Bellows ventilators are pneumatically driven and use oxygen (or air, on some machines) as drive gas, which can drain a backup cylinder quickly. A ventilator driven by air spares oxygen but still needs a compressed-gas source.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 34

questions.stem: In a patient with atelectasis, the inspiratory limb of the pressure-volume loop shows a lower inflection point near 10 cmH2O. Which adjustment does this suggest?
options: Lower the PEEP to zero
Set PEEP just above that point
Reduce the set tidal volume
Increase the inspiratory flow
questions.explanation: Below the lower inflection point, collapsed alveoli need extra pressure before they open, so the curve is flat until recruitment begins. Setting PEEP just above that point keeps alveoli open between breaths and moves ventilation onto the steeper, more compliant part of the curve. Reducing tidal volume addresses an upper inflection point (overdistension), not a lower one.

questions.stem: On many modern workstations, a small oxygen flow continues whenever the machine is on, even with the oxygen knob closed. What is its purpose?
options: To keep the vaporizer sump primed with agent
To ensure some oxygen always enters the circuit
To pressurize the bellows housing for the ventilator
To power the oxygen supply failure alarm whistle
questions.explanation: A minimum mandatory oxygen flow, typically about 50 to 250 mL/min depending on the model, means the machine cannot deliver a gas mixture with zero oxygen from the flowmeters. It adds to the proportioning system and fail-safe valve, but it does not protect against a crossed pipeline, which only the oxygen analyzer detects.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 40, 41, 45

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the pressure-relief device (frangible disk or fusible plug) built into a cylinder valve?
options: To vent gas before heat ruptures it
To limit flow while the cylinder is moved
To stop backflow from the hanger yoke
To reduce output pressure to 45 psig
questions.explanation: If a cylinder is exposed to fire or extreme heat, internal pressure can climb past what the cylinder can hold. A frangible disk bursts at a set pressure, and a fusible plug melts at a set temperature, releasing the gas in a controlled way rather than letting the cylinder explode. Backflow is handled by the yoke check valve and pressure reduction by the regulator.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 10, 18

questions.stem: A circle system runs with fresh gas flow of 8 L/min while minute ventilation is 6 L/min. How is it functioning?
options: As a closed system with full rebreathing
As a semi-closed system with partial rebreathing
As a semi-open system with little rebreathing
As an open system without any reservoir bag
questions.explanation: When fresh gas flow exceeds minute ventilation, nearly all exhaled gas is vented and almost none is rebreathed, so the circle acts as a semi-open system and the absorbent does little work. Lower flows produce partial rebreathing (semi-closed), and a fresh gas flow equal to the patient's uptake is a closed system.

questions.stem: In MS MAID room setup, which preparation belongs to the D step?
options: Backup IV access supplies ready
Oral and nasal airways sized
Induction and emergency drugs labeled
Self-inflating bag present and working
questions.explanation: D stands for drugs: induction agents plus emergency drugs drawn up, labeled, and within reach before the patient enters. Backup IV supplies belong to I, airway adjuncts to A, and the self-inflating bag to the Machine step as a backup ventilation device.

questions.stem: What is the saturated vapor pressure of Halothane at 20°C?
options: 160 mmHg
240 mmHg
244 mmHg
669 mmHg
questions.explanation: At 20°C, the saturated vapor pressure of Halothane is 244 mmHg (Isoflurane is 240 mmHg, Sevoflurane is 160 mmHg, and Desflurane is 669 mmHg).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: A patient's core temperature falls to 33°C during surgery. How does the volatile anesthetic requirement change?
options: It falls by about 20 percent
It rises by about 20 percent
It does not change with temperature
It falls by about 50 percent
questions.explanation: MAC decreases by roughly 5 percent for each degree Celsius of hypothermia, so a 4 degree drop lowers requirement by about 20 percent. Continuing the usual dose in a cold patient deepens anesthesia and slows emergence, which adds to the other effects of hypothermia such as slowed drug metabolism.

questions.stem: During a sudden desaturation in a cold, vasoconstricted patient, which probe site will usually show the fall first?
options: A toe probe on the foot
A finger probe on the hand
An earlobe or forehead probe
All sites show it at the same time
questions.explanation: Central sites such as the earlobe and forehead are closer to the heart and stay better perfused during vasoconstriction, so they detect desaturation sooner. Finger and especially toe probes can lag by tens of seconds or more. A central probe is useful when peripheral perfusion is poor.

questions.stem: A hospital backup oxygen manifold uses H-cylinders. About how much oxygen does a full H-cylinder hold compared with a full E-cylinder?
options: About 2 times as much
About 5 times as much
About 10 times as much
About 25 times as much
questions.explanation: A full oxygen H-cylinder holds roughly 6,900 L, compared with about 660 L in an E-cylinder, about ten times as much. H-cylinders are too large to mount on a workstation and are used in manifolds and as bulk backup, while E-cylinders hang on the machine yoke and travel with patients.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 7, 12

questions.stem: Which single ECG lead is the most sensitive for detecting perioperative myocardial ischemia in high-risk patients undergoing vascular surgery?
options: Lead II
Lead V3
Lead V5
Lead aVF
questions.explanation: According to Landesberg et al. cited in the monitoring text, lead V3 detected ischemia earliest and most often (86.8%), followed by V4 (78.9%) and V5 (65.8%). Lead II is preferred for rhythm analysis.

questions.stem: How is the correct oropharyngeal airway size estimated?
options: Mouth corner to the angle of the jaw
Tip of the nose to the earlobe
Incisors to the thyroid cartilage
Chin to the sternal notch
questions.explanation: An oral airway is sized by holding it beside the face: it should reach from the corner of the mouth to the angle of the mandible, so its tip sits behind the tongue base. Nose-to-earlobe (tragus) is the method for a nasopharyngeal airway.

questions.stem: Nitrous oxide is added to the oxygen carrier gas while a variable bypass vaporizer is running. Output briefly falls, then recovers. Why?
options: N2O dissolves in the liquid agent for a while
Nitrous oxide cools the sump and lowers vapor pressure
The interlock closes the chamber when gases are mixed
The bimetallic strip reacts to the added gas density
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide is soluble in liquid volatile agent. When it is first added, some of it dissolves into the liquid in the chamber, so slightly less gas leaves the chamber and output dips until the liquid is saturated. The effect is small and temporary, and it reverses (a brief rise) when nitrous oxide is turned off.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 54, 56

questions.stem: With a hyperangulated video laryngoscope, the glottis is in full view but the styletted tube keeps striking the anterior tracheal wall. What is the BEST adjustment?
options: Advance the blade deeper for a closer glottic view
Replace the curved stylet with a straight stylet
Apply cricoid pressure to bring the larynx posterior
Pull the stylet back as the tube tip enters
questions.explanation: A hyperangulated blade needs a tube shaped to match its curve, so the tip naturally points anteriorly. Once the tip passes the cords, pulling the stylet back lets the softer tube follow the trachea instead of catching on the anterior rings. A straight stylet cannot reach a view around the corner, and pushing the blade deeper usually makes passage harder.

questions.stem: With a mechanical proportioning system, nitrous oxide flow is turned up to 6 L/min. What minimum oxygen flow will the system enforce?
options: 1.5 L/min
2 L/min
3 L/min
6 L/min
questions.explanation: The proportioning system keeps nitrous oxide to oxygen at no more than 3:1, which holds the oxygen concentration of the N2O-O2 mixture at about 25 percent or higher. At 6 L/min of nitrous oxide, oxygen must be at least 2 L/min. At 1.5 L/min oxygen the mixture would be only 20 percent.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 45, 46

questions.stem: Why should an absorber's intergranular air space be at least as large as the patient's tidal volume?
options: So exhaled gas stays in contact long enough
So gas cannot channel along the canister walls
So circuit resistance stays below the APL setting
So enough moisture stays to prevent compound A
questions.explanation: About half of a packed canister is air space between granules. If that space holds an entire tidal volume, each exhaled breath sits within the absorbent between breaths, giving time for full CO2 neutralization. When the space is smaller than the tidal volume, part of each breath passes through before it can react. Channeling depends on packing, not total volume.

questions.stem: Besides its long atmospheric lifetime, what environmental harm sets nitrous oxide apart from the halogenated ethers in current use?
options: It forms chlorine radicals in the stratosphere
It has the highest warming potential per kilogram
It is a major ozone-depleting emission
It breaks down in soil to nitrate pollutants
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide is both a greenhouse gas and one of the largest remaining ozone-depleting emissions, through nitrogen oxides formed in the stratosphere. It contains no chlorine, and per kilogram its warming potential is far below desflurane's. Its long lifetime is why each release keeps acting for about a century.

questions.stem: During an out-of-OR intubation, a colorimetric CO2 detector stays purple after six breaths. What does this indicate?
options: CO2 is detected, confirming tracheal placement
Little or no CO2 is reaching the detector
The detector needs 20 breaths to change color
The patient is hyperventilating normally
questions.explanation: Colorimetric detectors change from purple to yellow when exhaled CO2 is present. Persistent purple means little or no CO2, which suggests esophageal placement, or no pulmonary blood flow during arrest. It is a qualitative check, so waveform capnography is used as soon as available.

questions.stem: Why does alveolar concentration approach inspired concentration faster with sevoflurane than with isoflurane?
options: Sevoflurane has a higher saturated vapor pressure
Sevoflurane has a lower oil:gas partition coefficient
Sevoflurane has a higher minimum alveolar concentration
Less sevoflurane is taken up from the alveoli by blood
questions.explanation: Uptake into blood removes agent from the alveoli and holds alveolar concentration down. Sevoflurane's lower blood:gas coefficient (0.65 versus 1.46) means less is removed, so alveolar concentration rises toward inspired more quickly. Its vapor pressure is actually lower than isoflurane's, and oil:gas solubility and MAC describe potency, not speed.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: The capnogram shows a slow, sloping inspiratory downstroke that blends into a baseline above zero. Which problem best explains this?
options: Exhausted CO2 absorbent in the canister
Incompetent inspiratory unidirectional valve
Bronchospasm slowing expiratory emptying
Leak in the sidestream sampling line
questions.explanation: When the inspiratory valve does not seat, exhaled gas flows backward into the inspiratory limb and is re-inhaled at the start of the next breath. That smears the downstroke and lifts the baseline. Exhausted absorbent also raises the baseline but keeps a crisp downstroke, bronchospasm slants the upstroke, and a sampling leak lowers the plateau.

questions.stem: A patient with carbon monoxide poisoning is given 100% oxygen. What does this do to the carboxyhemoglobin half-life?
options: Shortens it from 4 to 5 hours to about 1 hour
Lengthens it as oxygen competes for hemoglobin
Leaves it unchanged since CO binding is permanent
Shortens it to a few seconds as CO is released
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide and oxygen compete for hemoglobin, so high inspired oxygen displaces CO faster. The half-life falls from roughly 4 to 5 hours on room air to about 60 to 90 minutes on 100 percent oxygen, and further with hyperbaric oxygen. Because SpO2 reads falsely normal, co-oximetry guides treatment.

questions.stem: What is the boiling point of Sevoflurane at 1 atmosphere of pressure?
questions.explanation: At 1 atmosphere, Sevoflurane boils at 58.6°C (Desflurane boils at 22.8°C, Isoflurane at 48.5°C, and Halothane at 50.2°C).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: What is the primary risk of using more than one washer (Bodok seal) when mounting an E-cylinder onto a hanger yoke?
options: It can allow the valve post to bypass the gas-specific index pins
It lowers the vapor pressure of gas entering the regulator
It causes the cylinder relief device to open at normal pressure
It completely blocks gas flow through the yoke nipple
questions.explanation: Only one Bodok washer should be used. Extra washers can space the cylinder valve away from the yoke enough to bypass the Pin Index Safety System, creating a wrong-cylinder connection hazard.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 10, 18, 21

questions.stem: Which of the following interventions are recommended to minimize the environmental impact and atmospheric emissions of volatile anesthetic agents? (Select 3)
options: Routinely calibrate vaporizers to 100% dial concentration before induction
Avoid nitrous oxide as a routine carrier gas
Increase room air turnover to greater than 30 exchanges per hour
Replace soda lime absorbent canisters after every individual patient case
Avoid unnecessarily high fresh gas flow rates, especially with desflurane
Use intravenous or regional anesthesia techniques whenever clinically appropriate
questions.explanation: Recommendations to reduce environmental greenhouse gas impact include avoiding N2O carrier gas, minimizing fresh gas flows (especially with desflurane, which has a 14-year atmospheric lifespan), and substituting regional/TIVA techniques when appropriate.

questions.stem: What is the minimum fresh outside air exchange requirement per hour in an operating room equipped with a recirculating ventilation system?
options: At least 1 fresh outside exchange per hour
At least 3 fresh outside exchanges per hour
At least 6 fresh outside exchanges per hour
At least 15 fresh outside exchanges per hour
questions.explanation: Recirculating OR ventilation systems must deliver 15 to 21 total air exchanges per hour, of which at least three exchanges must be fresh outside air.

questions.stem: Why is cricoid pressure traditionally used during rapid-sequence induction in a patient at risk for aspiration?
options: To reduce regurgitation and aspiration of gastric contents
To improve venous return
To increase lower-esophageal sphincter tone
To eliminate the need for preoxygenation
questions.explanation: The textbook describes cricoid pressure as an aspiration-risk maneuver traditionally used during rapid-sequence induction to reduce regurgitation and possible aspiration.

questions.stem: During a nitrous oxide, oxygen, and sevoflurane anesthetic, inspired oxygen climbs toward 95% while end-tidal sevoflurane falls and circuit volume stays high. What is the most likely cause?
options: The oxygen flush valve is stuck partly open
The proportioning system is overcorrecting
The vaporizer dial has drifted toward zero
The nitrous oxide flowmeter tube is cracked
questions.explanation: A flush valve that does not reseat sends a continuous stream of pure oxygen straight to the common gas outlet, bypassing the flowmeters and vaporizer. That raises inspired oxygen, dilutes the agent, and keeps the circuit full. A drifting vaporizer lowers agent but not oxygen, a cracked nitrous oxide tube does not dilute the agent, and the proportioning system only limits nitrous oxide relative to oxygen.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 36, 37

questions.stem: What is the primary consequence of applying an excessively small blood pressure cuff to an adult patient's extremity?
options: Blood pressure readings will be falsely elevated
Blood pressure readings will be falsely low
Inability to detect cardiac dysrhythmias
Blunting of the arterial dicrotic notch
questions.explanation: A cuff that is too narrow requires higher inflation pressure to compress the artery, resulting in falsely elevated systolic and diastolic blood pressure readings.

questions.stem: A variable bypass vaporizer set to 2% is used with a very high fresh gas flow of 15 L/min. How does its output compare with the dial?
options: Slightly higher, as more gas enters the chamber
Slightly lower, as chamber gas is not fully saturated
Exactly 2 percent, since the splitting ratio is fixed
Close to zero, since the bypass carries all of the flow
questions.explanation: The splitting ratio assumes gas leaving the vaporizing chamber is fully saturated. At very high flows, gas passes through the chamber too quickly to saturate, so output falls a little below the dial. Output also drops at very low flows (under about 250 mL/min) because there is too little turbulence to carry vapor out.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 54, 55

questions.stem: Which requirements does the ASA basic monitoring standard specify for evaluating oxygenation during general anesthesia? (Select 3)
options: Arterial blood gas analysis at least every hour
Inspired oxygen analyzer with a low-concentration alarm
Transcutaneous oxygen tension monitoring in all adults
Pulse oximetry with a variable-pitch tone and audible low alarm
Adequate lighting and exposure to assess patient color
Continuous mixed venous oxygen saturation monitoring
questions.explanation: The ASA oxygenation standard covers both the gas and the patient: an inspired oxygen analyzer with a low-concentration alarm, quantitative pulse oximetry with a variable-pitch tone and audible low-threshold alarm, and enough illumination and exposure to assess color. Blood gases, transcutaneous monitoring, and mixed venous oximetry are case-specific tools, not basic requirements.

questions.stem: An oxygen-driven ascending bellows develops a hole while air and oxygen are being delivered at an FiO2 of 0.40. Which change is most likely?
options: Inspired oxygen falls below the set mixture
The bellows fails to rise during exhalation
Exhaled CO2 rises because of rebreathing
Inspired oxygen climbs toward 100 percent
questions.explanation: During inspiration the oxygen drive gas in the bellows housing is at higher pressure than the gas inside the bellows, so a hole lets drive gas enter the patient circuit. The inspired oxygen rises above the set mixture and the volatile agent is diluted. A bellows that stays collapsed points to a disconnection, and the hole does not cause rebreathing.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 33

questions.stem: Which direct-laryngoscopy blade exposes the glottis by directly lifting the epiglottis?
options: Miller blade
Macintosh blade
Eschmann introducer
RAE tube
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the Miller as a long, straight blade used for direct epiglottic lift. The Macintosh lifts indirectly through the vallecula.

questions.stem: A department wants a CO2 absorbent that will not form meaningful carbon monoxide or compound A even if it dries out. Which change achieves this?
options: Barium hydroxide lime in place of soda lime
Soda lime with a higher potassium hydroxide content
Calcium hydroxide lime without NaOH or KOH
Soda lime used only with fresh gas flows above 2 L/min
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide and compound A formation are driven by the strong bases in the absorbent (KOH, NaOH, and barium hydroxide). Calcium hydroxide lime without those bases does not degrade the volatile agents in a clinically meaningful way, even when desiccated. Raising fresh gas flow lowers compound A rebreathing but does not change the chemistry, and high flows are what dry the absorbent in the first place.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of calcium hydroxide in wet soda lime absorbent?
options: It serves as the bulk reactant that permanently converts intermediate carbonates into calcium carbonate
It functions as an initial catalyst to hydrolyze carbon dioxide into carbonic acid
It absorbs toxic carbon monoxide gas generated by difluoromethyl ethers
It prevents ethyl violet dye from undergoing the regeneration phenomenon
questions.explanation: Calcium hydroxide constitutes ~80% of soda lime. It reacts with sodium and potassium carbonates to precipitate calcium carbonate and regenerate the hydroxide catalysts.

questions.stem: During use, where in a properly packed absorber does the indicator color change usually appear first?
options: Along the central core of the canister
Where gas leaves toward the inspiratory limb
Evenly throughout all of the granules
Where exhaled gas first enters the canister
questions.explanation: Exhaled gas meets the granules at the inflow end first, so those granules are neutralized and change color first, and the exhaustion front moves toward the outlet as the case continues. A canister that changes along its walls or in streaks suggests channeling. Once color reaches the outflow end, little capacity remains.

questions.stem: Under volume control with a tidal volume of 450 mL, PEEP is 8 cmH2O and plateau pressure is 26 cmH2O. How should the driving pressure be interpreted?
options: 26 cmH2O, within the 30 cmH2O plateau limit
18 cmH2O, above the usual target of about 15
18 cmH2O, well inside the safe range
34 cmH2O, so PEEP should be removed
questions.explanation: Driving pressure is plateau pressure minus PEEP: 26 minus 8 equals 18 cmH2O. It reflects tidal volume relative to the compliant lung available, and values above roughly 15 cmH2O are associated with ventilator-induced lung injury even when plateau pressure stays below 30. Lowering tidal volume, or adjusting PEEP to recruit lung, can bring it down.

questions.stem: When the central oxygen pipeline is suspected of contamination, what must be done before relying on the backup oxygen cylinder?
options: Open the cylinder only and leave the pipeline connected
Open the cylinder and disconnect the pipeline hose
Close the cylinder and increase the oxygen flowmeter
Activate the oxygen flush continuously
questions.explanation: Pipeline pressure normally exceeds regulated cylinder pressure, so simply opening the cylinder does not isolate a contaminated pipeline. The guide instructs opening the cylinder and disconnecting the pipeline so the cylinder becomes the source.

questions.stem: Which end-tidal carbon dioxide change is listed as a clinical event during malignant hyperthermia?
options: An unexplained sudden rise in ETCO2
A fixed ETCO2 of zero in every case
An isolated decrease caused by hypometabolism
No ETCO2 change until after hyperthermia develops
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia lists an unexplained sudden rise in end-tidal carbon dioxide among the clinical events associated with malignant hyperthermia. Rising temperature is also a recognized finding and may occur later.

questions.stem: An LMA cuff inflated during a long nitrous oxide anesthetic measures 90 cmH2O. What is the main concern and target?
options: Poor seal, so add air until the leak stops
Aspiration risk, so raise the cuff further
Laryngospasm, so deflate the cuff completely
Nerve and mucosal injury; aim for 60 or less
questions.explanation: Excess cuff pressure compresses pharyngeal mucosa and nearby nerves (lingual, hypoglossal, recurrent laryngeal), causing sore throat and nerve palsies. Manufacturers recommend keeping LMA cuff pressure at or below about 60 cmH2O, measured with a manometer because nitrous oxide diffuses into the cuff over time. More pressure does not improve the seal beyond a point and adds injury risk.

questions.stem: What is the critical temperature of Nitrous Oxide?
questions.explanation: The critical temperature of N2O is +36.4°C (above room temperature). Because of this, it remains a liquid under compression inside the cylinder at room temperature.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 14

questions.stem: In an arterial pressure waveform, which event corresponds to the dicrotic notch?
options: Closure of the aortic valve
Opening of the aortic valve
Peak isovolumetric ventricular contraction
Closure of the mitral valve
questions.explanation: The dicrotic notch on an arterial waveform marks the closure of the aortic valve and signifies the transition from systole to diastole.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors promote the degradation of sevoflurane into Compound A? (Select 3)
options: High concentrations of sevoflurane
High fresh gas flows (>10 L/min)
Low fresh gas flows (<1 L/min)
Warm, dry, desiccated absorbent
Cold, water-saturated fresh absorbent
Absence of potassium hydroxide and sodium hydroxide catalysts
questions.explanation: Compound A formation from sevoflurane is promoted by warm/dry absorbent, high concentrations of dialed agent, and low fresh gas flows. High flows and adequate hydration protect against it.

questions.stem: Why should ethyl-violet color change not be used as the sole indicator that soda lime is still fresh?
options: Color may fade after use stops because of regeneration, and intense light can bleach the dye
Fresh soda lime is always purple
The dye measures oxygen concentration rather than absorbent status
Color change occurs only after the canister is removed from the circuit
questions.explanation: The lecture states that ethyl violet can be bleached by intense light and that color may fade after use stops because of regeneration. It specifically warns that indicator color should not be relied on by itself.

questions.stem: During induction with 70% nitrous oxide plus sevoflurane, sevoflurane's alveolar concentration rises faster than with oxygen alone. What explains this?
options: The second gas effect
Diffusion hypoxia
Overpressurization
The pumping effect
questions.explanation: Rapid uptake of a large volume of nitrous oxide concentrates the remaining alveolar gases and pulls more fresh gas into the alveoli, raising the alveolar concentration of the accompanying volatile agent. Diffusion hypoxia is the reverse process at emergence, and overpressurization is a dial technique.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: Which of the following safety features are integrated into mechanical flowmeters on an anesthesia machine to prevent the delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture? (Select 2)
options: The oxygen flow control knob is physically larger and fluted
Nitrous oxide is plumbed into an independent auxiliary manifold
The Thorpe tube diameter is uniform along its entire length
Oxygen is always positioned last in the manifold sequence closest to the outlet
Flow control valves automatically increase fresh gas flow during hypoventilation
Check valves prevent volatile agent from entering the flowmeter tubes
questions.explanation: To prevent hypoxia, the O2 knob is uniquely tactile (larger, fluted) and O2 is positioned furthest downstream (last on the right) so any upstream leaks will leak other gases rather than oxygen.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 40, 41

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanism of heat loss prevented by using humidified breathing circuits and low fresh gas flows?
options: Evaporation
Radiation
Conduction
Convection
questions.explanation: Low fresh gas flows conserve exhaled moisture and heat, directly reducing evaporative heat loss from the respiratory tract (which expends 0.58 kcal per gram of water vaporized).

questions.stem: During an emergency cricothyrotomy, why is the incision placed in the lower third of the cricothyroid membrane?
options: The thyroid isthmus lies over its upper third
The vocal cords attach to its upper border
The recurrent laryngeal nerves cross there
The cricothyroid arteries cross its upper third
questions.explanation: The paired cricothyroid arteries anastomose across the upper portion of the membrane, so cutting low reduces bleeding into the airway. The vocal cords sit about 1 cm above the membrane, the thyroid isthmus lies over the upper tracheal rings, and the recurrent laryngeal nerves run laterally in the tracheoesophageal groove.

questions.stem: During cardiopulmonary resuscitation, what capnographic change most strongly suggests return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC)?
options: An abrupt sustained increase in end-tidal carbon dioxide
A progressive fall of the capnogram baseline to zero
Development of a curare cleft in the alveolar plateau
A gradual widening of the PaCO2–EtCO2 gradient
questions.explanation: Return of spontaneous circulation abruptly restores pulmonary blood flow and delivery of carbon dioxide to the lungs, producing a sudden sustained rise in end-tidal carbon dioxide.
questions.citation: Intraoperative Assessment, Monitoring & Data Interpretation · Slide 46

questions.stem: Which limitation of the anesthesia-machine fail-safe valve is most important when oxygen supply pressure remains normal?
options: It cannot detect the identity or concentration of the gas being supplied
It cannot reduce nitrous oxide flow when oxygen pressure falls
It directly measures inspired oxygen concentration instead of pressure
It shuts off oxygen before other gases
questions.explanation: The fail-safe valve responds to oxygen supply pressure, not gas identity or oxygen concentration. A crossed pipeline or oxygen pipeline contaminated with another gas can therefore maintain normal pressure and escape detection; the inspired oxygen analyzer is needed to identify that hazard.

questions.stem: A sidestream gas analyzer aspirates 200 mL/min during a sevoflurane anesthetic. Where should the analyzer's exhaust gas go?
options: Into the room, since the volume is small
Into the suction canister used for the case
Back to the circuit or into the scavenger
Through the room's recirculating air filter
questions.explanation: The sampled gas carries the same agent concentration as the breathing circuit, and 200 mL/min adds up over a long case. Returning it to the breathing system or routing it to the scavenging system keeps it from becoming an avoidable leak. Recirculating filters do not remove anesthetic vapor, and suction canisters are not designed for waste gas.

questions.stem: Which of the following volatile anesthetics do NOT produce carbon monoxide when exposed to dry, desiccated carbon dioxide absorbent? (Select 2)
options: Desflurane
Sevoflurane
Halothane
Isoflurane
Enflurane
Methoxyflurane
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide production is specific to difluoromethyl ethers containing the -O-CHF2 group (Desflurane > Enflurane > Isoflurane). Sevoflurane and Halothane lack this moiety and do not produce CO.

questions.stem: Scavenging transfer tubing uses 19 mm or 30 mm connectors. What is the reason for these sizes?
options: They match the 22 mm breathing circuit ports
They keep scavenging tubing off circuit fittings
They allow wall vacuum to connect directly
They reduce resistance below that of the APL
questions.explanation: Breathing-system fittings are 15 mm and 22 mm, so scavenging connectors are deliberately sized at 19 or 30 mm to prevent a scavenging hose from being connected to the breathing circuit by mistake. Attaching suction directly to the circuit could pull negative pressure on the patient's lungs.

questions.stem: Why is desflurane avoided for inhalation induction?
options: Its high blood solubility slows the induction
Its pungency causes coughing and laryngospasm
Its vapor pressure is too low for mask delivery
It forms carbon monoxide with fresh absorbent
questions.explanation: Desflurane is pungent and irritates the airway, so breathing it while awake or lightly anesthetized causes coughing, breath-holding, secretions, and laryngospasm. It actually has the lowest blood solubility of the volatiles, and carbon monoxide forms with desiccated, not fresh, absorbent. Sevoflurane is used for mask induction because it is not irritating.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: An ethyl-violet absorbent canister looks white even though inspired CO₂ has begun to rise. Which explanation is supported by the study guide?
options: White color always proves the absorbent is fresh
Regeneration, bleaching, or channeling can make color unreliable
Only a broken capnograph can produce inspired CO₂
High fresh gas flow permanently restores exhausted absorbent
questions.explanation: Absorbent color can mislead because exhausted dye may regenerate toward white, intense light can bleach it, and channeling can exhaust a gas path while much of the canister still looks fresh. Inspired CO₂ is the clinical warning.

questions.stem: Which volatile anesthetic has the greatest carbon-monoxide production potential with desiccated absorbent?
options: Sevoflurane
Halothane
Desflurane
Nitrous oxide
questions.explanation: The guide ranks carbon-monoxide production with dry absorbent as desflurane greater than enflurane greater than isoflurane. Sevoflurane and halothane are not listed as carbon-monoxide producers.

questions.stem: An oxygen E-cylinder reads 2,000 psig at 21°C and is left in a vehicle that reaches 50°C. About what will the gauge read?
options: About 1,800 psig
About 2,000 psig
About 2,200 psig
About 4,800 psig
questions.explanation: At a fixed volume, gas pressure rises in proportion to absolute temperature (Gay-Lussac's law). Converting to kelvin, 2,000 × 323 / 294 is about 2,200 psig. Using Celsius directly gives the inflated 4,800 figure, a common error. This is why cylinders are kept away from heat and carry pressure-relief devices.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 11, 12

questions.stem: During mask ventilation, slight chest movement is seen but SpO₂ is falling and no waveform ETCO₂ is present. How should ventilation be interpreted?
options: Adequate because visible chest movement is the best measure of ventilation
Inadequate because falling SpO₂ and absent waveform ETCO₂ outweigh slight chest movement
Adequate because low peak airway pressure excludes airway obstruction
Adequate until oxygen saturation falls below the emergency alarm limit
questions.explanation: The guide emphasizes combining clinical signs with objective measures. Falling SpO₂ and absent waveform ETCO₂ indicate failed ventilation despite slight visible chest movement.

questions.stem: During an isoflurane mask induction, the dial is set well above the target alveolar concentration for the first several minutes. What is the reason?
options: To offset vaporizer under-delivery at low flows
To limit compound A formation in the absorbent
To counter blood uptake and speed alveolar rise
To make up for dilution by the oxygen flush
questions.explanation: Isoflurane is fairly soluble in blood (blood:gas 1.46), so uptake keeps alveolar concentration well below the inspired concentration early on. Overpressurizing, delivering more than the target, offsets that uptake and speeds induction. The dial is lowered as alveolar concentration approaches the goal to avoid overdose.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: Which monitoring-alarm practice best matches the Exam 1 study guide?
options: Disable recurrent alarms once the cause seems benign
Evaluate every alarm every time and keep required alarms audible
Silence variable-pitch pulse oximetry during stable cases
Lower alarm limits below standards whenever nuisance alarms occur
questions.explanation: The monitoring guide states that every alarm is evaluated every time and that alarm limits remain audible and compliant with standards. Alarm fatigue is specifically identified as a risk for missed events.

questions.stem: PaCO2 is 40 mmHg at a tidal volume of 500 mL and rate of 10, with 150 mL dead space. Settings change to 250 mL at a rate of 20. Approximately what PaCO2 results?
options: 40 mmHg
55 mmHg
70 mmHg
80 mmHg
questions.explanation: Minute ventilation stays at 5 L/min, but alveolar ventilation falls from (500 − 150) × 10 = 3.5 L/min to (250 − 150) × 20 = 2.0 L/min. PaCO2 varies inversely with alveolar ventilation, so 40 × 3.5/2.0 is about 70 mmHg. Small, fast breaths spend a larger share of each breath on dead space.

questions.stem: Why is the oxygen flowmeter positioned downstream, or last, in a traditional flowmeter bank?
options: So an upstream leak preferentially loses another gas rather than oxygen
So oxygen can bypass the common gas outlet
So the oxygen analyzer can be omitted
So nitrous oxide pressure becomes higher than oxygen pressure
questions.explanation: Oxygen is placed downstream, or last, in a traditional flowmeter bank so that a leak in an upstream tube preferentially loses another gas before oxygen enters the final mixture. A leak in the oxygen flowmeter itself can still produce a hypoxic mixture.

questions.stem: What complication is most commonly associated with nasopharyngeal airway insertion?
options: Epistaxis
Dental fracture
Tracheal rupture
Pneumothorax
questions.explanation: The equipment guide identifies epistaxis as the most common complication of nasopharyngeal airway placement.

questions.stem: An open scavenging interface is connected to active suction. What happens if suction is excessive?
options: Positive pressure is transmitted directly to the breathing circuit
Room air is entrained through the open interface
The reservoir bag distends until the pop-off valve opens
The APL valve becomes permanently closed
questions.explanation: An open interface is valveless and open to room air. Excess suction therefore entrains room air rather than transmitting negative pressure to the breathing circuit.

questions.stem: Peak inspiratory pressure and plateau pressure both increase after pneumoperitoneum while tidal volume is unchanged. What mechanism best explains the pattern?
options: Increased airway resistance with unchanged compliance
Decreased lung/chest-wall compliance
A sampling-line obstruction only
Isolated endotracheal-tube secretions
questions.explanation: When both peak and plateau pressures rise, the guide points to reduced static and dynamic compliance. Pneumoperitoneum is listed as a cause of that pattern.

questions.stem: What is the saturated vapor pressure of Sevoflurane at 20°C?
options: 160 mmHg
240 mmHg
244 mmHg
669 mmHg
questions.explanation: At 20°C, the saturated vapor pressure of Sevoflurane is 160 mmHg (Isoflurane is 240 mmHg, Halothane is 244 mmHg, and Desflurane is 669 mmHg).
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 50

questions.stem: During IV sedation, CO2 is sampled through a nasal cannula delivering oxygen at 4 L/min. EtCO2 reads 22 mmHg with a regular waveform. What is the best interpretation?
options: The value is diluted and underestimates PaCO2
The patient is hyperventilating and needs more sedation
The reading is accurate, so oxygen can be reduced
The flat value means the cannula has dislodged
questions.explanation: Oxygen flowing through the cannula mixes with exhaled gas at the sampling point, so the measured value runs well below arterial PaCO2. During sedation, the waveform and its rate are the useful signals because they confirm breathing and detect apnea or obstruction early. A regular waveform argues against dislodgement, and the low number alone does not mean hyperventilation.

questions.stem: [REINFORCEMENT: Q301] Sevoflurane is administered at a dialed concentration of 3% with a fresh gas flow of 1.5 L/min. Using the clinical formula: Liquid agent consumed (mL/hr) = Vol % x FGF (L/min) x 3, how many milliliters of liquid sevoflurane will be consumed during a 2-hour surgical procedure?
questions.explanation: Using the formula: Total anesthetic used (mL/hr) = 3 (%) x 1.5 (L/min) x 3 = 13.5 mL/hr. For a 2-hour case: 13.5 mL/hr x 2 hr = 27.0 mL.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 52

questions.stem: Examine the Flow-Volume loop below. What category of respiratory pathology is demonstrated by this loop configuration?
options: Variable intrathoracic upper airway obstruction
Fixed large airway obstruction (e.g., tracheal stenosis, large foreign body)
Severe restrictive pulmonary parenchymal fibrosis
Obstructive small airways disease with gas trapping
questions.explanation: Symmetrical truncation and flattening of both the inspiratory and expiratory limbs of a flow-volume loop is diagnostic of a fixed intra- or extra-thoracic large airway obstruction, such as severe tracheal stenosis, compression from a mediastinal mass, or a fixed foreign body.
